What was decided: Build a fresh Python program that ports 3DMorph's logic in, rather than adding PrestoCell's features to MATLAB.
Why it was decided: napari, Cellpose and gudhi have no MATLAB equivalents, whereas 3DMorph's logic is standard numerical image processing with direct Python counterparts.

What was decided: Separate the pipeline into three independently runnable phases: A segmentation, B human confirmation, C morphometrics.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell fuses A+B and 3DMorph fuses A+C, so neither can be interrupted or resumed; the split falls exactly on the 'needs a human' line.

What was decided: Inherit 3DMorph's morphometric definitions verbatim instead of substituting standard library equivalents.
Why it was decided: They are peer-reviewed and citable, and there is no legacy data requiring a different convention.

What was decided: Implement only the 'keep small processes' skeletonization path (Lee thinning plus graph pruning).
Why it was decided: It is the method actually in use, and it removes the FastMarching package and its compiled .mexw64 binaries from scope entirely.

What was decided: Split a blob only when it overlaps two or more confirmed nuclei; blobs with one or zero nuclei are kept whole and never force-split.
Why it was decided: Real nuclei replace 3DMorph's morphological guess, whose nuc=2 forcing always split genuinely large single cells.

What was decided: Remove erosion+GMM splitting from the automatic pipeline, keeping it only as an optional manual tool in the semi-auto editor.
Why it was decided: GMM assumes cells are ellipsoidal voxel clouds, which ramified microglia are not, so its boundaries slice arbitrarily through processes.

What was decided: Erode the cell as 3DMorph does, but use the confirmed nucleus to select which remnant is the soma; fall back to largest remnant when no nucleus exists.
Why it was decided: 3DMorph's 'largest remnant' rule fails when a thick proximal process survives erosion, and the nucleus centroid alone risks cross-channel offset landing the anchor on a process.

What was decided: Implement both PBC-fragment propagation and nucleus-seeded intensity watershed as interchangeable splitters, then benchmark them.
Why it was decided: PBC is the published validated method while watershed is faster and deterministic; real images should settle which is better rather than assumption.

What was decided: Run Cellpose in 2D per slice with IoU stitching across z, rather than max-projecting z-batches.
Why it was decided: Max-projection fuses nuclei stacked in z, and since splitting is solely nucleus-gated every fused pair becomes a clump that silently never gets split.

What was decided: Make Phase C an on-demand incremental pass backed by a persistent 'confirmed but not analysed' queue.
Why it was decided: Review of 12,000-28,000 cells cannot be finished in one sitting, so analysis must survive interruption and resume.

What was decided: Present cells as a ranked contact sheet with bulk accept rather than one-by-one 3D inspection.
Why it was decided: At roughly 3 s per cell, reviewing every cell individually would take about 17 hours, making triage load-bearing rather than a convenience.

What was decided: Store cell metadata in SQLite with voxel arrays in compressed .npz files, and never use pickle.
Why it was decided: Review needs sortable queryable per-file access and atomic status updates, while pickle is version-fragile, uninspectable and unsafe to share between machines.

What was decided: Store each cell's mask, nucleus mask and a 2D thumbnail; re-read source images only for full 3D views.
Why it was decided: Thumbnails make contact-sheet triage fast without duplicating hundreds of gigabytes of intensity data.

What was decided: Cache per-file intermediates during processing and auto-purge them once that file's cells are analysed.
Why it was decided: They allow re-running later pipeline stages without repeating Cellpose and thresholding while the split engines are being benchmarked.

What was decided: Segment at 2x xy downsample but measure morphometrics at native resolution, validating the choice against native segmentation.
Why it was decided: Clustering is expensive but tolerant of coarser voxels while morphometrics is resolution-sensitive yet cheap per cell, and 2x puts nuclei at Cellpose's ~30 px operating point.

What was decided: Have each Phase A task write its own manifest fragment, merged into the pooled database by a separate step.
Why it was decided: SQLite over network filesystems corrupts under concurrent writers, and a crashed SLURM array task can then simply be re-run.

What was decided: Render the review's 3D view from stored masks, overlaying source intensity only when the source is reachable.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell loads the entire source TIFF per session, which breaks when review runs on a different machine from the images.

What was decided: Group cells per source file in natural order, ranked worst-confidence-first within each file.
Why it was decided: It avoids re-reading an 810 MB TIFF on nearly every click, and QC scores are not comparable across files with differing staining and signal quality.

What was decided: Allow 'accept rest of this file' only, requiring every file to be explicitly cleared.
Why it was decided: It guarantees no image is passed over unseen while still avoiding per-cell review of all 20,000+ cells.

What was decided: Iterate on a locally cropped sample and move to Bunya for full-scale GPU runs.
Why it was decided: 810 MB files make local iteration painful, while the phase split lets segmentation and analysis run as SLURM jobs with only review needing a display.

What was decided: Create the new package as 'prestomorph' inside the 'merged program' folder.
Why it was decided: The user designated that folder for the merged program.

What was decided: Use numpy (z, y, x) ordering throughout with physical voxel size carried alongside.
Why it was decided: It avoids inheriting 3DMorph's row/column/plane index-swapping, converting only at the MATLAB comparison boundary.

What was decided: Produce both per-cell 3D masks and a 3DMorph-format summary spreadsheet.
Why it was decided: Masks support re-inspection and downstream analysis while the spreadsheet matches the established output format.

What was decided: Apply Otsu per z-slice (3DMorph's mechanic) with PrestoCell's live slider interaction, plus a new guard for near-empty slices.
Why it was decided: Confocal signal attenuates with depth so a global threshold biases cell volume by z position, and per-slice Otsu on an empty slice would otherwise threshold pure noise into signal.

What was decided: Leave the choice between connected components and PBC clustering for coarse object detection open until Component 2 is built.
Why it was decided: It blocks only Component 2, and the trade-off (nuclei as sole separation authority versus fidelity to PrestoCell's published pipeline) deserves resolution against real data.

What was decided: Repurpose 3DMorph's erosion as an independent second opinion used for validation rather than for decision-making.
Why it was decided: It derives from a different channel than the nuclei, so it can cross-check nucleus counts, rescue missed nuclei, and produce a quality score neither parent program has.

What was decided: Use object size as evidence feeding triage priority rather than as a splitting trigger, derived from the cell population rather than eyeballed.
Why it was decided: 3DMorph required a hand-picked cutoff because it had no other information, whereas a population of 12,000-28,000 cells makes 'unusually large' statistically definable.

What was decided: Establish the size distribution from within-file statistics in semi-auto mode, then refine it batch-wide at Phase B in auto mode.
Why it was decided: Semi-auto has only ~20-40 cells available live, while auto mode completes all segmentation before any review begins.

What was decided: Replace 3DMorph's NearestPixel with a KD-tree query on physically scaled coordinates.
Why it was decided: The original multiplies the z difference by 1 instead of zscale, inflating z by 1.67x at 0.6 um slices; the bug is invisible whenever zscale equals 1.0, which is why it survived peer review.

What was decided: Replace the hop-counting wavefront path search with Dijkstra weighted by true micron distance.
Why it was decided: Treating all 26 neighbours as one step makes a 0.6 um z-hop cost the same as a 0.108 um xy-hop, biasing paths through z and systematically overestimating branch length.

What was decided: Emit NaN plus a per-cell status and reason on failure instead of zeros.
Why it was decided: 3DMorph's silent try/catch writes zeros that are indistinguishable from real measurements in the results spreadsheet.

What was decided: Report a union-based occupied volume alongside 3DMorph's summed convex hulls.
Why it was decided: Summing overlapping territories can exceed the image volume and drive the reported empty volume negative.

What was decided: Create docs/DESIGN_RATIONALE.md recording why each choice was made, including defects found in both parent programs.
Why it was decided: The reasoning behind non-obvious choices needs to survive beyond the conversation that produced it.

What was decided: Sequence the work as eight components, starting with the storage layer and prototyping morphometrics early.
Why it was decided: Everything depends on the storage format, and morphometrics is the highest-consequence component because it carries both bug fixes and all scientific output.

What was decided: Use SQLite's default rollback journal rather than WAL mode.
Why it was decided: WAL creates sidecar files that a partial sync from Bunya to a local machine could miss, and single-writer access makes WAL's concurrency benefit irrelevant.

What was decided: Rely on SQLite placing NULL agreement scores first when sorting ascending.
Why it was decided: A cell with no nucleus has no score and is exactly the kind that should be reviewed first.

What was decided: Sort files by natural-sorted full path rather than ASCII filename order.
Why it was decided: Plain sorting places img10 before img2, and path ordering also keeps files from the same animal or genotype adjacent during review.

What was decided: Derive a file_uid from a hash of the full source path and use it for cell ids, directory names and fragment names; make all identifiers deterministic.
Why it was decided: Filenames repeat across animal folders, so the bare filename would silently overwrite another file's fragment and lose an entire image's cells; determinism also makes a retried SLURM task safe.

What was decided: Store bounding boxes as half-open ranges matching numpy slicing exactly.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell's crop() drops the last voxel on three faces by mixing an inclusive max index with exclusive slicing.

What was decided: Compute per-cell CD68 volume natively and also export Imaris-compatible label images.
Why it was decided: Native computation keys results to the same cell ids in one spreadsheet, while the export preserves the option of the lab's established Imaris workflow.

What was decided: Export a uint16 label image with physical voxel size embedded, not a binary mask.
Why it was decided: Imaris builds surfaces by connected components, so a binary mask would re-merge cells that the nuclei channel was used to split, and missing voxel spacing makes every volume measurement wrong.

What was decided: Take a 4-channel TIF (DAPI, Iba1, CD68, plaque) as input, with channel roles as explicit configurable parameters.
Why it was decided: The plaque channel enables per-cell distance-to-plaque, the canonical 5xFAD phenotype, and configurable roles avoid PrestoCell's hardcoded channel indices.

What was decided: Split the database into three tables: files, cells and results.
Why it was decided: Per-file state (voxel size, channel roles, whether review is cleared) has no home in a cells-only schema, and separating results lets Phase C re-run without touching review decisions.

What was decided: Store no pickle anywhere, using compressed .npz arrays with a JSON manifest and a SQLite index.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell's per-cell pickles are version-fragile, uninspectable, unsafe to move between machines and impossible to query.

What was decided: Make the Phase A writer a separate type from the reader, with no database access at all.
Why it was decided: The unsafe pattern - a parallel batch task writing to the shared database - then cannot be expressed by accident.

What was decided: Preserve status, rejection reason and review timestamp when a fragment is re-merged, behind an explicit reset flag.
Why it was decided: A naive upsert would silently reset every accept and reject already made, destroying human work that cannot be recovered.

What was decided: Write every file atomically as a temporary file, fsync, then os.replace.
Why it was decided: A task killed mid-write must not leave a truncated fragment that the merge step then parses as valid.

What was decided: Verify declared channel roles against the pixel data by measuring CD68 containment within Iba1, and refuse to proceed on a mismatch.
Why it was decided: The first test images were described with two channels the wrong way round, and segmenting CD68 as microglia would have produced plausible rather than obviously broken output.

What was decided: Read channels lazily by role rather than loading whole stacks.
Why it was decided: Phase A needs only DAPI and Iba1, so deferring CD68 and 6E10 halves the working set at 32-bit.

What was decided: Refuse to proceed when the file's recorded voxel size disagrees with the supplied parameters.
Why it was decided: At 5.5:1 anisotropy a wrong scale corrupts every physical measurement downstream without ever raising an error on its own.

What was decided: Require the axis order to be declared explicitly for plain TIFFs that carry no layout metadata.
Why it was decided: Which axis is z and which is channel is otherwise a coin flip, and a wrong guess silently swaps the data.

What was decided: Keep images 32-bit rather than converting them to 16-bit.
Why it was decided: Deconvolved peaks exceed the 16-bit ceiling so any conversion must rescale, and per-image rescaling would break CD68 comparability across the dataset.

What was decided: Fill holes in the cell mask as part of building it, rather than leaving each consumer to remember.
Why it was decided: Iba1 is cytoplasmic so the nucleus is a hole in the signal; unfilled, nucleus membership fails and clumps are never split.

What was decided: Recover native resolution by treating the upsampled labels as region assignment intersected with the native threshold mask.
Why it was decided: Upsampling the label volume alone would quantise every boundary to the downsample factor and blunt the thin processes the study measures.

What was decided: Suppress DAPI wherever 6E10 plaque signal is present, before nucleus detection runs.
Why it was decided: Dense-core plaques are DAPI-positive, and a plaque read as a nucleus manufactures a spurious split precisely where microglia cluster most tightly.

What was decided: Put Cellpose behind a thin adapter targeting the version 3 nuclei model.
Why it was decided: It is purpose-trained and exposes an explicit diameter, while the adapter keeps the version 4 generalist swappable for a later comparison.

What was decided: Use connected components at 26-connectivity for coarse object detection, resolving the choice left open earlier against persistence clustering.
Why it was decided: Connected components only ever fuses and never divides, so nuclei remain the sole authority on separation, and microglial processes often connect only diagonally.

What was decided: Merge two objects that overlap the same nucleus into a single cell.
Why it was decided: A dim patch across a soma breaks one cell into two components, which would otherwise be reported as two cells each with a partial volume and a truncated skeleton.

What was decided: Split clumps by flooding smoothed intensity outward from nucleus seeds rather than by a distance transform.
Why it was decided: Microglial processes are thin everywhere, so a distance map is nearly flat along them and boundaries would land arbitrarily mid-process.

What was decided: Size every smoothing kernel, dilation and crop padding in microns rather than in voxels.
Why it was decided: An isotropic element measured in voxels reaches about 5.5 times further in z than in plane at this anisotropy.

What was decided: Compute all label overlaps by single-pass label-pair counting.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell scans the whole volume twice for every cell-nucleus pair inside a nested loop, which is intractable at batch scale.

What was decided: Replace PrestoCell's 1% overlap test with a substantial-majority membership threshold measured against the filled mask.
Why it was decided: The 1% figure exists only to compensate for a hollow mask, and it admits a neighbouring neuron's nucleus just as readily as the cell's own.

What was decided: Apply the size filter by default but make xy border removal an explicit user choice.
Why it was decided: Border removal discards real, correctly segmented cells on the grounds the frame cut them off, which is a scientific judgement rather than a technical one.

What was decided: Always keep cells that touch the top or bottom of the stack, examining only the lateral faces.
Why it was decided: A 24 um stack cannot contain a 50 um cell, so excluding z-truncated cells would discard most of the dataset.

What was decided: Defer the PBC splitter until marked clumped data exists to benchmark it against.
Why it was decided: Building a second engine that cannot yet be compared would be work done blind.

What was decided: Parameters are re-tuned on two thirds of the marked images with a third held back.
Why it was decided: Every shipped value had been fitted to a single image, which the log itself named the project's highest risk.

What was decided: The holdout is drawn at random, constrained to ~a third of somata and a quarter of the clumped marks.
Why it was decided: An unconstrained draw put 44% of somata and an entire animal in the holdout, leaving the tuning set with fewer clumped marks than the holdout.

What was decided: program training crop is forced into the tuning set rather than being eligible for holdout.
Why it was decided: The shipped parameters were already fitted to its 13 somata, so it cannot honestly serve as a held-out image.

What was decided: The holdout stays sealed until after the WT retune instead of being scored immediately.
Why it was decided: Scoring it before the WT images arrived would spend it on an intermediate model that stops existing the next day.

What was decided: scripts/tune.py is built as a permanent harness rather than a throwaway script.
Why it was decided: It re-runs verbatim on every later marked set, and its cache at the Cellpose boundary turns a 45-minute pass into 2-5 s per image.

What was decided: The PBC split back end is built and benchmarked even though watershed already worked.
Why it was decided: The counter-1 marks the benchmark had been waiting on now existed, and the user chose evidence over letting watershed win by being the only implementation.

What was decided: Component 6 is planned in a document first, then built in the same unattended run.
Why it was decided: §4.12 already fixed every contested definition, so the plan was a written record rather than an open design question.

What was decided: Nothing outside the agreed queue is started when it empties.
Why it was decided: Component 4 still needed the filename convention and Component 7 the Imaris check, and neither had been given.

What was decided: WT/2345 is refiled under 5xFAD/.
Why it was decided: Genotype is read from the path and never the filename, so a wrong folder silently mislabels every cell inside it.

What was decided: CD68 is measured over the whole cell mask rather than the soma alone.
Why it was decided: Process-resident CD68 is real signal, and restricting the region would break the volume-fraction measure against the ramification index it exists to pair with.

What was decided: All 6E10 signal counts as plaque, with no dense-core versus diffuse distinction.
Why it was decided: Diffuse deposits are real amyloid, accepted at the cost that the DAPI veto then consumes a broader mask.

What was decided: An empty plaque channel yields NaN plus a status, never zero.
Why it was decided: A zero distance is indistinguishable from a cell sitting directly on a plaque, which is the opposite of the truth.

What was decided: The CD68 threshold is left explicitly undecided rather than given a provisional value.
Why it was decided: The user would not commit to a number, and a default presented as validated is how a guess becomes a published constant.

What was decided: The two close mark pairs in 691619_4Subiculum1 are two cells each, not one soma marked twice.
Why it was decided: The user inspected both and found two nuclei and two Iba1 somata pressed together on the slice between the marks, retracting the double-mark hypothesis.

What was decided: Log-compress DAPI intensities before Cellpose instead of relying on its own percentile normalisation.
Why it was decided: Bright nucleoli dominate percentile scaling and flatten the nuclear body, and correcting it took per-slice detection from about 5 nuclei to 24 where 20 to 25 are visible.

What was decided: Upsample nucleus labels by nearest neighbour rather than region-assigning them to the cell mask.
Why it was decided: Region assignment gives every foreground voxel its nearest label, which is correct for cells but smears each nucleus across the whole cell and inflates the recorded count.

What was decided: Take each cell's nucleus list from the split assignment rather than from whatever labels overlap its mask.
Why it was decided: Nuclei are not clipped to cell boundaries, so a neighbour's nucleus can graze a crop and imply a clump where the split was in fact correct.

What was decided: Score soma-nucleus agreement with a smoothly decaying function normalised by the nucleus radius.
Why it was decided: A clamped form pinned a third of real cells to exactly zero, destroying the ordering the score exists to provide.

What was decided: Filter candidate cells before returning them to native resolution.
Why it was decided: Most candidates are sub-micron debris, so promoting all of them and then discarding most of them is wasted work.

What was decided: Hash the parameter set and record it on every stored cell.
Why it was decided: Results must trace back to the exact settings that produced them.

What was decided: Mark ground truth in three categories: confident isolated, confident clumped, and probable.
Why it was decided: Confident marks alone measure recall but cannot verify that a split landed correctly or make extra detections interpretable as false positives.

What was decided: Merge hand-placed markers of different categories within 4 um as one soma, never merging same-category pairs.
Why it was decided: Two categories on one soma describe a single cell carrying both attributes, whereas two clumped marks a few microns apart are exactly what a clump is.

What was decided: Read genotype and animal from the directory path, and region and section from the filename.
Why it was decided: Filenames are unreliable - one animal's files are named WT while sitting correctly in the 5xFAD folder - whereas the path is authoritative.

What was decided: Adopt the parameter set measured against the marked somata rather than the initial defaults.
Why it was decided: Tuning lifted recall from 7 of 13 marked somata to 13 of 13, with each value derived from the data rather than assumed.

What was decided: Treat record keeping of plans, decisions and corrections as a standing requirement of the work.
Why it was decided: Reasoning left only in conversation is lost the moment the context window fills.

What was decided: Cite the source file and line for every claim made about either parent program.
Why it was decided: It lets a later session check a specific claim in seconds instead of re-deriving it by re-reading two codebases.

What was decided: WT marking is treated as exhaustive, so unmarked detections count as false positives.
Why it was decided: The user marked exhaustively allowing for human error, and tolerates a few false positives because review deletes them before Component 6 measures anything.

What was decided: Component 3 is primarily a nucleus editor in PrestoCell's style, with parameter tuning secondary.
Why it was decided: Five parameter dimensions were swept without moving recall off 97%, while a human resolves a fused nucleus by eye in seconds.

What was decided: Napari is the platform, running on a Bunya interactive desktop.
Why it was decided: Click-to-edit labels on a 3D volume is the interaction that matters most, and napari provides it directly.

What was decided: Manual nucleus and process edits are per-image overrides that deliberately do not transfer to batch.
Why it was decided: A hand-placed split is a judgement about one image and cannot be meaningfully replayed against a different one.

What was decided: Segmentation uses two Iba1 thresholds — one for separation and nuclei, a second for the 3D cell mask.
Why it was decided: A threshold tuned to produce clean somata drops the thin processes morphometrics is made of, and ramified cells carry more of them, biasing toward the null.

What was decided: Morphometrics and CD68 are both measured on the permissive measurement mask.
Why it was decided: The earlier claim that morphometrics should stay on the segmentation mask "for 3DMorph comparability" was wrong: parity concerns the definitions, not which mask feeds them.

What was decided: mask_coefficient ships with no default and the two-mask path activates only once the user sets it.
Why it was decided: Inheriting a number fitted for a different job is exactly how the process-loss bias would be baked in silently.

What was decided: Growth into the measurement mask follows connectivity, not nearest-neighbour distance.
Why it was decided: A process must be physically continuous with its cell; distance-based assignment hands a detached blob of debris to whichever cell happens to be nearest.

What was decided: Noise filtering runs after assignment, never before it.
Why it was decided: A disconnected fragment of a real process is itself a small object, and reconnecting exactly those is what the second threshold exists to do.

What was decided: Unassigned measurement-mask components are counted and reported, not size-filtered.
Why it was decided: Nothing downstream reads them because every measurement is per cell, and a large unassigned component is evidence the segmentation threshold missed a cell.

What was decided: The cell-size minimum moves after the measurement mask, behind a ~20 µm³ speck floor.
Why it was decided: The user picks the cutoff against the volumes they are actually looking at, and the floor exists only to avoid upsampling hundreds of sub-micron fragments.

What was decided: The 200 µm³ minimum is not re-derived for the measurement mask.
Why it was decided: The user sets it visually against the volume distribution on each run, so there is nothing to fit.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: No maximum cell size is asked of the user.
Why it was decided: Nuclei already decide cell count so a maximum would trigger nothing; it survives instead as a computed volume-per-nucleus flag that orders review worst-first.

What was decided: remove_xy_border is deprecated as a segmentation-time action.
Why it was decided: It destroys cells irreversibly to answer a question better answered at analysis, and touches_xy_border already travels with every cell.

What was decided: Batch review gets the same add- and remove-process editing as semi-auto.
Why it was decided: Edits are local to a stored crop so the compute is trivial, and without it a process error in a batch run would have no repair path at all.

What was decided: Process review displays a padded 3D crop around the cell, PrestoCell-style.
Why it was decided: The whole field is more than the decision needs, and PrestoCell's padding=10 is a working precedent.

What was decided: Integrated CD68 intensity is the headline measure, with mean intensity reported alongside.
Why it was decided: A larger cell with more lysosomes genuinely has more phagocytic capacity, so total content is the biologically direct reading.

What was decided: CD68⁺ volume is published as a curve across several thresholds, never as a single number.
Why it was decided: The volume fraction falls smoothly from 82% to 56% between thresholds 1 and 100 with no plateau anywhere, so any one cutoff would silently set the answer.

What was decided: The within-cell percentile profile is deferred until per-cell data exists.
Why it was decided: The rank guidance offered for it came from pooled per-image percentiles, which mix bright and dim cells and describe neither.

What was decided: Plaque burden is a legitimate study outcome rather than only a covariate.
Why it was decided: The user confirmed the imaged fields were chosen by anatomical region, blind to plaque content.

What was decided: Plaque burden is reported as integrated 6E10 intensity *and* thresholded volume, with the full per-plaque size distribution.
Why it was decided: Intensity needs no cutoff and is the defensible figure, while segmentation buys the count and a distribution that a single total would hide.

What was decided: plaque_coefficient stays at 1.0 with the evidence recorded rather than being changed.
Why it was decided: WT reads 782 µm³ of "plaque" across 53 objects with no amyloid present, so 1.0 is probably too permissive, but fixing a value needs all the WT images first.

What was decided: min_spur_um = 1.0 is adopted as the skeleton pruning length.
Why it was decided: Measured over 152 cells it is where the two measurement thresholds converge, removes ~31% of endpoints in both genotypes alike, and leaves the longest branch untouched.

What was decided: The filename fields decode as <section><Region><index>, with HPL and C3 carried verbatim.
Why it was decided: The user supplied the convention, and those two tokens are constant across every file so they carry no discriminating information.

What was decided: The batch driver globs the image tree and then writes out the manifest it used.
Why it was decided: Discovery is convenient and a recorded list is auditable, so a run can be replayed months later even if the directory has moved on.

What was decided: An ambiguous resubmit is refused, requiring an explicit --resume or --force.
Why it was decided: Skipping finished images silently would make "reprocess everything" a no-op, and reprocessing silently would repeat 600 finished files.

What was decided: Semi-auto and batch write to one pool, with every human-edited cell flagged.
Why it was decided: Those cells are not reproducible from the parameters file, so an analysis has to be able to include or exclude them deliberately.

What was decided: Results ship as two sheets per image — 3DMorph's exact column order and an analysis layout.
Why it was decided: Comparability with 3DMorph output is worth keeping and costs almost nothing when both are built from the same rows in one pass.

What was decided: Output is one workbook per image plus a combined table written as a final step.
Why it was decided: Each image stays inspectable on its own while the combined file is the one actually loaded for analysis.

What was decided: The combined table is CSV rather than xlsx.
Why it was decided: At ~20,000 rows a workbook is slow to write and awkward to read programmatically, and this file is loaded rather than opened by hand.

What was decided: Figures are written for every cell, as JPEG.
Why it was decided: Measured against the user's own 3DMorph output the cost is ~5.9 GB across 80,000 files, which is 2% of their block quota and 8% of their file quota.

What was decided: matplotlib is installed.
Why it was decided: Unlike gudhi and skan, no substitution existed — marching_cubes is in scikit-image but the 3D rendering is not.

What was decided: Both volumes appear in the compatible sheet, the measurement mask in 3DMorph's CellVolumes position and the segmentation mask appended after.
Why it was decided: Appending after their layout keeps anything reading the sheet by position working, while losing neither number.

What was decided: Rejected cells are listed at the bottom of both files, with blank rather than zeroed measures.
Why it was decided: Rejection happens at review before Phase C runs so they genuinely have no morphometrics, and "how many were discarded" must be answerable from the file itself.

What was decided: The Imaris export carries each cell's centroid and volume beside the label_id ↔ cell_uid map.
Why it was decided: Whether Imaris preserves label ids on import is unresolved, so matching can fall back to geometry regardless of the answer.

What was decided: Component 6's missing measures are built before Component 7.
Why it was decided: Export cannot write plaque burden, the per-plaque size distribution or the CD68 curve while those measures do not yet exist.

What was decided: Components 4 and 7 are authorised for unattended build.
Why it was decided: Both were fully planned and every decision inside them had been made, leaving nothing left to ask.

What was decided: The first parity attempt is abandoned and 3DMorph re-run with a higher CellSizeCutoff.
Why it was decided: Only one of fourteen objects fell in the comparable window, because everything larger was GMM-split by a mechanic deliberately not ported.

What was decided: membership_threshold lowered from 0.30 to 0.25.
Why it was decided: Membership scores are bimodal with nothing between 0.02 and 0.35, and a confirmed microglial nucleus scored 0.2996 — the old cutoff sat at the gap's edge rather than in it.

What was decided: min_spur_um raised from 0.0 to 1.0.
Why it was decided: Across 152 cells the WT/5xFAD endpoint ratio held at ~2.0 while 31% of branches were removed and max branch length was unchanged, so the filter took noise and not signal.

What was decided: plaque_coefficient split into plaque_veto_coefficient at 1.0 and a separate measurement coefficient with no default.
Why it was decided: The veto measured higher recall at 97% against 94%, while WT read 782 µm³ of impossible amyloid at the same value — one number serving two contradictory purposes.

What was decided: Five measures added to Component 6 — contact area, sphericity, clustering counts, background-corrected intensity, and a diffuse/dense-core split.
Why it was decided: The CD68/6E10 literature review named them as standard practice absent here, and the DAPI channel already acquired makes the core split possible with no new stain.

What was decided: The sealed holdout was not scored that night.
Why it was decided: §8's own rule still applied — a number measured against a non-final configuration describes a model that no longer exists, and the splitter was undecided.

What was decided: Component 8 to be planned in a written document before any code.
Why it was decided: The standing agreement that no component is implemented straight from the build plan.

What was decided: touches_z_border recorded as a flag rather than truncated cells being removed.
Why it was decided: A 24 µm stack cannot contain a 50 µm microglion, so excluding z-truncated cells at segmentation would irreversibly discard most of the data.

What was decided: No acquisition QC fields added, despite the review treating acquisition consistency as a precondition.
Why it was decided: Holding laser power, gain and offset constant is the user's responsibility at the microscope, not something the pipeline should audit.

What was decided: Τ swept on the tuning set and dedicated clump crops only, never on the holdout.
Why it was decided: Selecting a parameter on held-out data converts it from validation into tuning and leaves nothing to validate the choice against.

What was decided: The holdout seal was broken and scored once, across three splitters and two membership values.
Why it was decided: Parameter tuning was exhausted and the configuration as final as it would get, and the resource is spendable exactly once.

What was decided: The splitter default stays watershed despite pbc_gudhi leading 33/43 pairs against 28/43.
Why it was decided: At the measured 11.6% discordance rate the holdout's ten clump pairs yield roughly one disagreement, so it could neither confirm nor refute the tuning result.

What was decided: The CD68 curve was re-anchored to background multiples and then reversed the same day.
Why it was decided: Background median measured 0.013–0.048 against puncta at 10²–10⁴, so all five levels landed in the noise floor and the curve became four times less discriminating.

What was decided: DAPI dense-core coefficients set to 0.5–2.0 to bracket the measured peak.
Why it was decided: 5xFAD/WT separation rises to 32.3× at 1.5 and falls beyond it — the only turning point any curve in this project has produced.

What was decided: ramification_index and cd68_integrated promoted to indexed columns.
Why it was decided: Both are threshold-free so they stay meaningful across parameter sets, and review already sorts on QC fields that live on cells.

What was decided: The plaque size floor became one parameter at 25 µm³, replacing two conflicting floors and a five-value curve.
Why it was decided: Without a floor 39,765 objects sit ~1–2 µm apart and every cell reads as plaque-adjacent; the 73 µm³ ceiling comes from a single image, so 25 leaves margin where 50 does not.

What was decided: No genotype declaration that would skip plaque measurement on WT.
Why it was decided: WT is the only negative control for the plaque detector, and it is what revealed the 692146 anomaly in the first place.

What was decided: CD68 and 6E10 thresholds become absolute values picked in the semi-auto UI.
Why it was decided: Acquisition is held constant across the batch, so a value chosen once transfers unchanged — where an Otsu multiplier re-adapts per slice and lands on a different intensity in every image.

What was decided: Both threshold curves centre on the chosen value at a factor of 2.
Why it was decided: Visual threshold-setting is reproducible to roughly a factor of two, so a 16× span brackets any plausible alternative pick.

What was decided: One export folder per run, and the side-by-side parameter-set sheet deleted.
Why it was decided: A re-run producing its own output leaves each file internally homogeneous, which none of the refuse/merge/side-by-side options offered.

What was decided: Every output written as CSV and the hand-rolled xlsx writer deleted.
Why it was decided: ~150 lines of SpreadsheetML existed only because openpyxl is absent, and named CSVs make cells, plaques and images equally loadable.

What was decided: Files organised by unit of analysis, with columns grouped by goal within each.
Why it was decided: Morphology, phagocytosis and pathology each span cell, plaque and image rows, so a goal cannot be a file.

What was decided: cell_plaque_links.csv added, carrying per-pair distance rather than membership alone.
Why it was decided: Every other plaque measure is anonymous, so without it the per-plaque compaction measures can never be analysed against the cells surrounding them.

What was decided: The 3DMorph comparison output becomes a flag, off by default.
Why it was decided: It validates the port, which is done once on a few images rather than routinely across 700.

What was decided: The parameters file is copied verbatim into each export folder beside a short summary of counts.
Why it was decided: A verbatim copy cannot drift from what actually ran, where a restated run-info file can.

What was decided: Export folders named export_<date>_<hash8>.
Why it was decided: Sorts chronologically while the hash keeps runs unique and tied to the parameters that produced them.

What was decided: mean_z kept in the export despite not being a result.
Why it was decided: Intensity attenuates with depth, so a CD68 comparison between genotypes is confounded unless depth is available as a regressor.

What was decided: cd68_integrated_corrected dropped.
Why it was decided: Subtracting a background of ~0.02 from intensities in the millions is a no-op here, and it implies a normalisation an absolute threshold does not use.

What was decided: agreement_score, size_outlier_score and plaque_status dropped from the export.
Why it was decided: The first two exist to order review worst-first and are not results, and review runs before Phase C so it never queries measurements at all.

What was decided: is_clustered, hierarchy_voxels and n_voxels_segmentation dropped.
Why it was decided: is_clustered is fully derivable from n_cells_within, and n_voxels_segmentation only differs when mask_coefficient is set, which it is not.

What was decided: Territorial overlap volume and overlap index kept.
Why it was decided: Healthy microglia tile with minimal overlap and that organisation degrades in disease — information 3DMorph destroys by summing hulls.

What was decided: 3DMorph's occupancy trio reproduced but marked a check on the port rather than a result.
Why it was decided: Its inputs are identical to ours, so a mismatch would mean our hull code is wrong — unlike the centroid measure, whose soma definition also differs.

What was decided: 3DMorph's mean-pairwise centroid distance not reproduced; nearest-neighbour distance used instead.
Why it was decided: Mean pairwise distance converges to a fraction of the box diagonal almost regardless of clustering, and their largest-remnant soma centroid differs from ours by design.

What was decided: The plaque burden curve carries volume only, not plaque count.
Why it was decided: Count across thresholds reports how the segmentation fragmented rather than how much amyloid is present.

What was decided: Compartments keep a five-coefficient curve per image while per-plaque core is fixed at 1.5.
Why it was decided: The measure is exploratory and cannot be cross-validated without Thioflavin-S or X34, which is where a robustness spread earns its place.

What was decided: Contact tolerances stay three fixed values and are not user-chosen.
Why it was decided: Unlike an intensity they have no visual anchor, and 0.3 µm is half the z-spacing — the smallest tolerance that can mean anything at 5.5:1 anisotropy.

What was decided: smallest_plaque_um3 added to the per-image burden.
Why it was decided: Requested, with the caveat recorded that the floor truncates the distribution from below so it will sit near 25 µm³ in most images.

What was decided: MEASUREMENT_REFERENCE.md, docs/output_templates/ and BUILD_PLAN_REVISION_DRAFT.md deleted.
Why it was decided: Each described an export that had been replaced, and the templates advertised 72 columns where the writers emitted 37.

What was decided: The build-plan revision draft was merged rather than walked component by component.
Why it was decided: The export walkthrough had already settled most of its questions, leaving only the Components 3 and 5 UI items which are reserved for joint design.

What was decided: PROJECT_LOG.md restructured into state, durable knowledge and dated history.
Why it was decided: Three sections claimed to describe the present while months stale, and a stale "current state" heading asserts authority where a date invites checking.

What was decided: The export rebuild was fully specified but deliberately left unimplemented.
Why it was decided: Running out of context mid-rebuild would leave a half-migrated export, which is worse than not starting it.

What was decided: Count n_branch_points as merged junction clusters rather than raw junction voxels.
Why it was decided: One branch point spans several adjacent voxels at 26-connectivity, and the inflation scales with arbour complexity, so it biased the genotype comparison.

What was decided: Restore section, region and image_index to the identity block of cells, plaques and images.
Why it was decided: The recommended analysis nests cells in sections within animals, and omitting a nesting level understates standard errors.

What was decided: Add Sholl analysis, both Euclidean and geodesic, at a 2.0 um step.
Why it was decided: Every other morphology column is a count or an extent and none says where along the radius the arbour sits, which is what de-ramification changes.

What was decided: Export branch hierarchy as length in um per order rather than as voxel counts.
Why it was decided: At 5.5:1 anisotropy a voxel is not a unit of length, so a z-running branch and an xy-running one of equal length would give different counts.

What was decided: Keep union_unoccupied and union_percent_occupied after proposing to drop them as derivable.
Why it was decided: The marked crops are not all one size, so the constant-multiple argument that made them redundant does not hold across the current data.

What was decided: Define soma_volume_um3 as the morphological opening of the cell mask at soma_erode_um.
Why it was decided: The column had never had a producer at all, and the raw eroded remnant understates the soma by a shape-dependent amount.

What was decided: Add burden_status and compartments_status columns beyond the specification.
Why it was decided: A blank plaque count must be distinguishable from an unset threshold, an absent channel and a genuine zero, which is a real finding on WT images.

What was decided: Score future 3DMorph parity on endpoint and branch-point counts rather than on branch lengths.
Why it was decided: 3DMorph agreed with manual tracing on counts and diverges on lengths by a documented convention difference, so only counts are informative.

What was decided: Add image_cd68_integrated, a threshold-free whole-image CD68 sum, alongside the 6E10 equivalent.
Why it was decided: It depends on neither the segmentation nor the unchosen threshold, so it exists today and is the stable reference the per-cell measures read against.

What was decided: Rename union_occupied to union_surveyed, with unsurveyed and percent to match.
Why it was decided: The measure is the union of convex hulls, the tissue microglia collectively monitor, while occupied read as bulk, which is an order of magnitude smaller.

What was decided: Replace free-text reject_reason with debris or real_cell plus an optional note, and make rejection permanent with no deferral.
Why it was decided: Free text made the loss uncountable, and the cells expensive enough to abandon are the clumped 5xFAD ones, so the bias points at the population under study.

What was decided: Delete the optional 3DMorph comparison output and its flag.
Why it was decided: Segmentation parity is closed at -0.5 percent, only three of its eight columns were ever comparable, and the parity harness survives independently.

What was decided: Keep one consistent cell mask for every measurement rather than widening it for CD68.
Why it was decided: Numerator and denominator of cd68_fraction then share a mask, and the signal outside is captured by the whole-image CD68 measure instead.

What was decided: Keep the per-plaque DAPI dense-core coefficient at 1.5.
Why it was decided: It is the peak of the 5xFAD-to-WT ratio and survives excluding the one anomalous WT image, though WT never reaches zero at any coefficient tested.

What was decided: Define n_real_cells as confirmed cells plus cells rejected as real_cell.
Why it was decided: Both are cells the reviewer judged real, so together they answer how many microglia were in the field, and debris is excluded because it is not a cell.

What was decided: Add image_cd68_fraction_in_cell_masks with every measured cell in the numerator regardless of review status.
Why it was decided: Counting only confirmed cells would multiply mask tightness by review attrition and drift downward as review proceeds, looking like masks getting worse.

What was decided: Allow a reviewer to split a clumped cell by three routes, nucleus split, placed seeds or drawn boundary, with the reviewer choosing.
Why it was decided: Rejection is now permanent, so the reviewer needs a repair path, and the existing watershed already accepts markers from any source.

What was decided: Delete the parent cell after a manual split and flag both children human-derived.
Why it was decided: The user chose deletion over keeping a superseded parent, accepting that the under-split rate must then be recovered another way.

What was decided: Approve a created_by_split flag but build it only with the splitting feature.
Why it was decided: It preserves the under-split rate once the parent is deleted, and adding it earlier would leave a field nothing can set, which is the defect just fixed.

What was decided: Fix mean_z at the producer by giving measure_cell a z_offset, and delete the duplicate in markers.
Why it was decided: The exported value was crop-local and carried no stack depth, and two same-named fields let a test assert the right rule against the wrong function.

What was decided: Convert mean_z to mean_z_um.
Why it was decided: The conversion is exact because the measure is single-axis, and depth attenuation is a physical process better expressed in microns than in grid indices.

What was decided: Fix n_cells_within by padding the plaque crop per axis in physical microns rather than switching to the nearest-plaque field.
Why it was decided: Padding is exact rather than merely wider, while the nearest-plaque field would silently answer a different question under the same column name.

What was decided: Make min_spur_um a real parameter in the file and the params hash instead of a hardcoded fallback.
Why it was decided: It removes 31 percent of branches at 1.0 and sets n_endpoints, so two runs differing on it currently produce the same hash.

What was decided: Generate a parameter reference from SegmentationParams rather than maintaining one by hand.
Why it was decided: Two parameters existed in no document at all, and a hand-kept list goes stale the next time one is added with nothing to compare against.

What was decided: Document plaque_dilate_um and sweep it.
Why it was decided: The veto 97 percent recall figure was measured at some dilation the section never mentions, and too large a value eats genuine nuclei near plaques.

What was decided: Make export refuse to run without --params rather than assert UNSET thresholds.
Why it was decided: The pool knows the real values, so an unparameterised run writes a false export_summary, which is the file someone quotes in a methods section.

What was decided: Extend the spec-to-header test to all eight files, derive the expected set from the specification, and assert values.
Why it was decided: Three columns shipped full and wrong because the test checked only that headers existed.

What was decided: Add avg_nearest_neighbour_status with ok, too_few_somata and no_soma_centroids.
Why it was decided: A sparse field and a soma-finding failure are opposite meanings and currently produce an identical blank.

What was decided: Keep the five status columns and document why.
Why it was decided: A blank that could be a real zero is the most dangerous ambiguity in the export, and the cost is five columns on about twenty image rows.

What was decided: Keep SystemExit in the semi-auto stubs and correct the plan that claims NotImplementedError.
Why it was decided: The stubs are reached only from the command line, where a clean message beats a traceback.

What was decided: Let a reviewer state how many real cells a single rejection covers, and treat that number as authoritative.
Why it was decided: The project already treats human marks as ground truth, so calling the same person cell count an estimate would be incoherent.

What was decided: Propagate the rejection multiplicity into n_real_cells, n_cells_within and the cell-plaque link table together.
Why it was decided: A clump of three at a plaque is three recruited microglia, and a partial application would leave columns counting cells by different rules.

What was decided: Add field_volume_um3 as a column on images.csv.
Why it was decided: It is the denominator for every density measure and is currently only recoverable by opening the pool.

What was decided: Require every test count in the documentation to carry the date it was measured or be removed.
Why it was decided: An undated count asserts it is current and drifted twice within hours, including one in durable knowledge stale by two hundred tests.

What was decided: Freeze PROJECT_LOG, COMPONENT_STATUS, BUILD_PLAN and DESIGN_RATIONALE, and give each parallel session its own continuation log.
Why it was decided: There is no git, so two sessions appending to one file is the most likely way for work to be destroyed.

What was decided: Bump PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION from 3 to 4 when min_spur_um becomes a field.
Why it was decided: params.py's own rule is to bump when a field is added, and the recorded argument for skipping it was wrong: load_params refuses a missing field and separately refuses a stale params_hash, so an old file is rejected twice over either way.

What was decided: Remove only the getattr on the params object and keep the min_spur_um defaults on measure_one and measure_cell.
Why it was decided: Those two are library entry points called with explicit values by two scripts and four tests.

What was decided: Let the cell_labels inclusion rule reach both n_cells_within and covered_fraction, and leave territory alone.
Why it was decided: Both are built from one array and both ask what lies near the plaque, which a review verdict does not change.

What was decided: Record the uids of real_cell rejections whose stored arrays are missing, as cell_label_gaps in the image payload.
Why it was decided: Skipping them silently would undercount the two cell-facing plaque columns again through a different door, which is the defect NEW-b had just closed.

What was decided: Surface cell_label_gaps as a cell_labels_status column on images.csv.
Why it was decided: A key inside a stored payload reaches nobody: no CSV carried it, nothing printed it and no column pointed at it.

What was decided: Add n_cells_real_cell to images.csv as a per image count of real cell losses.
Why it was decided: export_summary carried the figure per genotype only, so it could not be related to anything else measured on the same image, and its rate is expected to depend on genotype.

What was decided: Reuse n_real_cells_status for n_cells_real_cell rather than adding a second status column.
Why it was decided: Both counts become determinate at exactly the same instant, when no cell of the image is still a candidate, so a second status could never disagree with the first.

What was decided: Keep territory built from measured cells only and make the exclusion visible with a count instead.
Why it was decided: Including real_cell rejections would over-report, because such a mask is one the reviewer judged wrong and is usually a fused clump; excluding them under-reports.

What was decided: Add min_spur_um to export_summary.csv.
Why it was decided: That file carried every value a column name depends on, and a pruning length suffixes nothing.

What was decided: Raise the missing-params refusal inside export_pool rather than in argparse.
Why it was decided: argparse can only say the argument is required and cannot name the pool it never opened.

What was decided: Complete EXPORT_SPEC section 5 with column names for cd68_curve and image_curves before parsing it.
Why it was decided: Those two files were specified as shapes rather than names, so 61 columns could be checked by neither a parser nor a reader.

What was decided: Keep DAPI_CORE_COEFFICIENTS at 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0.
Why it was decided: The calibration swept seven values and the export ships the lowest five, which no document recorded.

What was decided: Let Workstream A edit schema.py to state the soma_centroid coordinate frame.
Why it was decided: The file is B's, but B had not started, which is the widest that window ever gets.

What was decided: Notify Workstream B through the user rather than through a file.
Why it was decided: One writer per file, and the only reliable channel between two accounts is the person holding both.

What was decided: Leave the four frozen documents stale until the merge rather than editing them in place.
Why it was decided: The alternative was offered once B was known to be clear of them and was declined.

What was decided: Accept the test suite runtime as it stands.
Why it was decided: About 80 percent of it is test_cli_end_to_end re-segmenting from scratch six times, which is 18 Cellpose runs on CPU.

What was decided: Leave plaque_dilate_um at 0.3 and put the sweep result to the user.
Why it was decided: Recall is flat from 0.0 to 0.3 and breaks at 0.6, where one confident soma is lost in a clumped 5xFAD field.

What was decided: Record soma_volume_um3 as unvalidatable by this dataset rather than as unvalidated.
Why it was decided: The ground truth marks somata as points: no radius, outline, area or volume appears on any of the 22 files, so no soma volume exists here to score one against.

What was decided: Leave the 11 parameters that carry no comment bare, and mark them loudly in the generated reference.
Why it was decided: Writing a plausible purpose without evidence is the documentation form of inventing a parameter value, and a blank cell is indistinguishable from a tool that failed to find the comment.

What was decided: Treat DESIGN_RATIONALE as frozen for Workstream A as well, resolving the disagreement between the two handoff documents.
Why it was decided: A's handoff lists it as frozen for both and B's lists it as A's to edit.

What was decided: Correct the SegmentationParams docstring to name the Phase C knobs it carries, not just Phase A.
Why it was decided: The class holds five fields read during measurement and the docstring claimed segmentation only.

What was decided: Reserve no_soma_centroids for images with two or more cells and none carrying a centroid, and report every other shortage as too_few_somata.
Why it was decided: With a single cell there is nothing to measure between whether or not it has a soma, so a missing-field diagnosis there would raise a suspicion the data does not support.

What was decided: State the soma volume limit at the COMPONENT_06 plan as well as in the export specification.
Why it was decided: That section says soma volume matches tools in the review, which is the sentence that invites a reader to assume external validation transfers.

What was decided: Cancel the proposed review of the 61 curve-file columns against intent.
Why it was decided: The intent was already recorded in COMPONENT_06_PLAN section 7.6, which specifies two compartments each reporting volume and integrated and mean 6E10.

What was decided: Order the queue so that the two blocking tasks run first, then the value-asserting test before the defect it should catch.
Why it was decided: Landing the instrument before the fix means the fix arrives with a failing test to satisfy rather than a green suite to hope about.

What was decided: Rewrite EXPORT_SPEC section 11.3 as the reasoning for the status columns rather than an errata note about columns beyond section 5.
Why it was decided: Nothing is beyond section 5 any more, and the section's count was wrong by three before two more columns were added.

What was decided: Report the soma over cell fraction as a finding and do not add it as a column.
Why it was decided: It tracks ramification at rho -0.805 where soma volume alone is null, because cell volume sits on both sides of the raw comparison.

What was decided: Put the synthetic soma gate in the test suite rather than in a tuning run.
Why it was decided: It has an analytic answer, so it belongs where it runs every time.

What was decided: Move the Iba1 separation threshold above nucleus review instead of after it.
Why it was decided: DAPI stains every nucleus in the field, so without the Iba1 mask a reviewer cannot tell which nuclei are microglial and would correct ones that membership discards moments later.

What was decided: Merge nucleus review into the detection screen so results appear where the parameters are set.
Why it was decided: Judging whether nucleus_diameter_um was right would otherwise mean walking two screens forward and paying 200-500 s to come back.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move the cell-size screen above cell review.
Why it was decided: min_cell_volume_um3 is applied inside segment_image before any cell is written, so cells below it never exist and reviewing first would leave edits recorded against cells that do not.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move the CD68 and 6E10 threshold pickers out of the per-image flow onto a study-level screen run once after review.
Why it was decided: Both are absolute values applied unchanged to about 700 files, so a per-image step would produce many answers to a question that has one.

What was decided: Give the plaque veto its own screen rather than merging it with detection.
Why it was decided: The detection screen already carries four layers, three edit gestures and two commits, and the veto is a separate judgement with its own cost.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Treat anything whose recompute costs multiple seconds as edit-then-commit, never a slider.
Why it was decided: A control that silently triggers a five-minute recompute is worse than a button that admits it; this answers the long-open Q2.

What was decided: Show progress during nucleus detection but offer no cancel.
Why it was decided: Detection runs per slice so aborting between slices would be feasible, but the user judged it unwanted.

What was decided: Review nuclei in 2D slice view rather than 3D volume, following PrestoCell.
Why it was decided: napari applies no level-of-detail in 3D and its default mip rendering destroys the depth cue the fused-nucleus judgement depends on.

What was decided: Make the z-batch projection view-only, with all editing done per slice.
Why it was decided: A click on a max projection carries no z, and resolving it by argmax is least reliable exactly where two nuclei overlap in xy and separate in depth.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Display and edit nucleus labels at working resolution with a per-layer scale of (1,2,2).
Why it was decided: Detection and splitting run at half resolution, so edits feed the pipeline with no conversion and no label-safe downsampler is needed.

What was decided: Show raw Iba1 as review context rather than the thresholded mask or a membership score.
Why it was decided: Raw signal cannot hide a nucleus behind a badly set parameter, and a confirmed microglial nucleus is on record scoring 0.2996 against a 0.25 threshold.

What was decided: Highlight microglial nuclei rather than filtering the view down to them.
Why it was decided: Many fields carry about 80 percent non-microglial nuclei, but filtering would let membership_threshold decide what a human is allowed to see.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move membership_threshold onto the detection screen as its only live control.
Why it was decided: Its effect is the highlighting shown there, and recomputing membership over labels and a mask that already exist is cheap.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make threshold 2 a live picker on the same machinery as threshold 1.
Why it was decided: The operation is literally the same call, measured at 0.25 s for one slice against about 59 s for the whole stack.

What was decided: Cap mask_coefficient at cell_coefficient dynamically and impose no lower bound.
Why it was decided: Above cell_coefficient the parameter is provably a no-op because a cell can never shrink, while 0.02 was only where the sweep happened to stop.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give the size screen one job and carry size_outlier_score forward as cell review ordering instead.
Why it was decided: The plan already notes the user never types a maximum because no action would follow, so outliers shown there are information with nowhere to go.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Adopt the 3DMorph three-panel size screen but have selection populate an editable value rather than set it outright.
Why it was decided: It preserves picking the smallest object still judged a cell without forcing the cutoff to be exactly that object's size.

What was decided: Offer no suggested minimum cell size, despite a measurable trough existing.
Why it was decided: The trough was measured on one 5xFAD image in one-mask mode, so it would not generalise to WT and would not survive threshold 2 shifting every volume.

What was decided: Keep border-touching cells, flag and mark them, and delete them only when under the minimum size.
Why it was decided: Deleting them would push their tissue into union_unsurveyed_um3, reporting edge tissue as unoccupied when a cell is demonstrably there.

What was decided: Make Phase C parameters editable on the save screen and Phase A parameters read-only.
Why it was decided: By that screen the cells already exist, so editing a Phase A value would write a parameters file claiming settings that did not produce them.

What was decided: Give Pool the ability to create and delete cells after merge.
Why it was decided: Only PoolWriter can add a cell today, which blocks both Component 5 splitting and Component 3 re-segmentation.

What was decided: Record an optional per-image operations log of the human edits performed, exported with the run.
Why it was decided: It yields the intervention rate, which storing only the final state cannot answer.

What was decided: Put the operations-record toggle in the parameters file outside params_hash rather than on SegmentationParams.
Why it was decided: On the dataclass it would re-queue every measurement in the pool whenever a documentation preference was flipped.

What was decided: Store edit coordinates in native full-image voxels, converting once at the point of capture.
Why it was decided: Three coordinate frames are live at once, and reading one as another already doubled avg_nearest_neighbour_um on every row ever exported.

What was decided: Give human_edited a setter, add it to preserve_cell, and have it carry a kind of split or mask.
Why it was decided: It has no writer today and is absent from preserve_cell, so a re-merge would silently discard the flag.

What was decided: Offer two re-entry modes, Edit and Re-segment, with Re-segment deleting all prior data for that image.
Why it was decided: Re-derived cells are different objects, so keeping review decisions against them would transplant judgements onto cells nobody judged.

What was decided: Have Re-segment re-run the whole pipeline but still use a warm cache.
Why it was decided: A cache hit returns an identical array because the key is the parameters, so discarding a valid 500 s result buys nothing.

What was decided: Write semi-automatic and batch runs into separate, enforced pools.
Why it was decided: Whether semi-auto output counts as study data varies by user, so the choice belongs at export time rather than baked into the software.

What was decided: Derive the pool from the study rather than asking for it, keeping the pool flag only as a CLI override.
Why it was decided: If nobody names a pool there is nothing to point at the wrong one, which makes the separation structural rather than a check.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Use PoolWriter and merge for derivation and Pool for edits, writing first after the size screen.
Why it was decided: Reusing the exact batch code path removes the second code path that would let the interactive and batch routes silently diverge.

What was decided: Have semi-auto merge its own fragment at commit.
Why it was decided: Batch separates merge only because hundreds of concurrent Slurm tasks cannot write one SQLite file, which does not apply to one image in one process.

What was decided: Keep no intermediate pool save, so an abandoned session leaves nothing behind.
Why it was decided: Every step before the size screen produces a different cell set, so writing earlier would commit work that is immediately replaced.

What was decided: Hold raw channels in memory as uint16, loading only those the current step needs.
Why it was decided: ImageSource.channel re-reads the TIFF on every call, and holding all four as float32 would cost 3.40 GB against 850 MB for the two that matter.

What was decided: Cache nucleus labels on disk and nothing else, inside the pool directory, with a size cap and LRU eviction.
Why it was decided: Detection is the only stage whose recompute cost massively exceeds its I/O cost.

What was decided: Guard cache keys with an exhaustiveness test as well as a perturbation test.
Why it was decided: Perturbation alone passes vacuously when a new field is wired in but left undeclared, which is the very failure the test exists to catch.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put only napari-touching modules in a flat ui package, keeping the cache outside it.
Why it was decided: prestomorph is already 23 flat modules, and the Component 3 versus Component 5 boundary is a planning boundary rather than a runtime one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep napari optional through a dependency group, late imports and a viewer Protocol.
Why it was decided: Cellpose is installed and still sits behind a Protocol, because no test of screen order should need a Qt window or a display.

What was decided: Assert the no-blocking rule with two static tests over the import graph.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell called napari.run inside its pipeline and thereby has no batch mode; the rule is the direction of the dependency arrow.

What was decided: Add a console script entry point so the documented prestomorph command actually exists.
Why it was decided: The short form appears 13 times across 5 files and works nowhere, and the package must be installable for Bunya regardless.

What was decided: Move channel roles onto SegmentationParams as four flat fields, bumping the schema to v5.
Why it was decided: Two runs with swapped roles segment completely different channels and would otherwise hash identically.

What was decided: Build no display pyramid for Component 3, replacing it with projection precompute.
Why it was decided: napari applies no level-of-detail in 3D and a 2304x2304 slice draws in 7.7 ms, so the only measurable cost is the 43 ms projection.

What was decided: Guard preserve_cell on params_hash so review decisions do not survive a re-segmentation.
Why it was decided: cell_uid is positional, so a rejected piece of debris hands its decision to whatever real cell next occupies that index.

What was decided: Have an edit delete its own cell measurement rows.
Why it was decided: Measurements are keyed on cell_uid and params_hash, and a nucleus edit changes which cells exist without changing the hash.

What was decided: Hold channels as uint16 but cast to float32 at the threshold call.
Why it was decided: uint16 and float32 yield different Otsu thresholds, so semi-auto and batch could otherwise produce different masks from identical parameters.

What was decided: Qualify the reproducibility gate to unedited runs, and have the edit gate also assert the negative.
Why it was decided: Overrides deliberately never reach the parameters file, so an edited run cannot replay identically and a test guards that better than a sentence.

What was decided: Block on a channel-role swap with no interface override, and flag a suspicious voxel size while allowing an explicit one.
Why it was decided: The role check has already caught one reversed dataset, and an xy size of exactly 1.0 is a TIFF default rather than a measurement.

What was decided: Change plaque_dilate_um from 0.3 to 0.0.
Why it was decided: The sweep found 0.00 scores identically on recall while vetoing 5.5 percent of DAPI against 8.4 percent, making the margin unpaid-for exposure landing entirely on 5xFAD.

What was decided: Split a nucleus with shift plus double-click, recorded as one split operation rather than a delete and two adds.
Why it was decided: Storing the mechanism would read as three operations and lose the under-split rate, the main QC number for the weakest point in the pipeline.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Open the threshold 1 screen at the middle slice, scrollable, previewing the raw threshold rather than the finished mask.
Why it was decided: Otsu is per slice so one slice is exactly right, whereas a single-slice build_cell_mask clips a 3D closing element and shows a mask the pipeline never makes.

What was decided: Show 6E10 raw, the veto mask, DAPI and the vetoed DAPI together on the veto screen.
Why it was decided: The DAPI core sits inside the 6E10, so the four layers make an over-reaching veto visible before it removes nuclei that would leave no trace.

What was decided: Assign cli.py and pyproject.toml to Workstream B.
Why it was decided: Neither appeared in the ownership map, and both are needed for the interface entry point and its optional napari dependency.

What was decided: Assign pipeline.py to Workstream A, resolving a contradiction between the two handoff documents.
Why it was decided: A's founding list always named it while B's called it unassigned and B had already edited it once, so one writer had to be named before SegmentationParams could be touched.

What was decided: Make the four channel roles real fields on SegmentationParams and bump PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION from 4 to 5.
Why it was decided: Roles reached Phase C but were in no parameters file and no params_hash, so two runs segmenting completely different channels hashed identically.

What was decided: Default cd68_channel and plaque_channel to None rather than to the shipped channels 1 and 3.
Why it was decided: None is load-bearing - it is how the pipeline learns an image has no such channel - whereas a default of 1 would make an image without CD68 assert that channel 1 carries it.

What was decided: Add the roles as four flat fields instead of one nested ChannelRoles object.
Why it was decided: load_params compares unknown keys at the top level only, so a nested object would have its own key recognised and nothing inside it validated.

What was decided: Write a separate purpose comment above each of the four new fields rather than one shared block.
Why it was decided: The PARAMETERS.md generator attributes a group comment to only the first field below it, so a shared block would have left two of the four documented as blank.

What was decided: Make segment refuse when --roles contradicts the parameters file, naming both values for each differing role.
Why it was decided: Letting the flag win would record channels in params_hash that the run did not use, and letting the file win silently would ignore a flag the user deliberately passed.

What was decided: Treat a role present in one source and absent in the other as a disagreement, not only a differing index.
Why it was decided: 'This image has no CD68' against 'channel 1 is CD68' is a real conflict with twelve export columns behind it.

What was decided: Change the --roles default from the shipped layout string to None in both cli.py and batch.py.
Why it was decided: With an always-present default the new check would refuse conflicts the user never created, so absence had to mean 'take the parameters file's'.

What was decided: Put the roles refusal in batch.main rather than inside segment_image.
Why it was decided: A parameters file always states all four fields explicitly while a SegmentationParams built in code may merely have defaulted, and a frozen dataclass cannot tell those apart.

What was decided: Return exit code 4 from the roles refusal instead of raising an exception.
Why it was decided: batch.main's two existing refusals print to stderr and return 2 and 3, so matching the surrounding function beat introducing a second error idiom into it.

What was decided: Remove nuclei_coefficient from SegmentationParams on the same schema bump as the channel roles.
Why it was decided: It was declared once and read nowhere - an Otsu multiplier for a DAPI-thresholding design never built, since DAPI goes to Cellpose - yet being inside params_hash it made two identical runs re-queue Phase C.

What was decided: Record the nuclei_coefficient removal in the class docstring rather than as a comment where the field had sat.
Why it was decided: A comment left in the field position was published by the generator as the purpose of the next field down, which is worse than the blank it replaced.

What was decided: Document that SegmentationParams says which channels to segment with while FileRecord.channel_roles records which were actually used.
Why it was decided: Two homes for one fact with neither naming its meaning is exactly how soma_centroid came to have its bounding-box origin added twice.

What was decided: Add n_cells_touching_xy_border and n_cells_touching_z_border to images.csv.
Why it was decided: Five per-image measures aggregate over cells before an analyst can filter, and once the union is a number the truncated hulls cannot be taken back out.

What was decided: Count the two border columns over the measured cells rather than over every exported row.
Why it was decided: Territory is built from the measured cells alone, so only that population describes the exposure these columns exist to report.

What was decided: Give the border counts no status column.
Why it was decided: Zero is a real answer - an image the frame cut nothing from is the good case - and the territory block they qualify carries no status either.

What was decided: Keep both an xy and a z border count even though z-truncation is near universal in this data.
Why it was decided: The z count is what makes the lower-bound caveat checkable per image instead of asserted once in prose.

What was decided: State in EXPORT_SPEC that every territory measure is a lower bound everywhere, not only at the frame edge.
Why it was decided: A 24 um stack cannot contain a 50 um microglion, so nearly every cell is z-truncated and territory must never be compared across datasets of different z-depth.

What was decided: Exclude ramification_index from that lower-bound caveat and give it its own statement.
Why it was decided: It is territorial over cell volume, so truncation clips both terms and the direction of the error is undetermined; a confident wrong caveat on the headline measure is worse than none.

What was decided: Record the territory caveat in EXPORT_SPEC section 7 only, with no DESIGN_RATIONALE amendment.
Why it was decided: Section 7 is where a reader of the column set meets caveats, and the rationale document is frozen, so an amendment would add merge debt for no extra reach.
