What was decided: Defer the measure-time role override to its own task rather than fold it into the schema change.
Why it was decided: phasec.py lets measure --roles silently override what segmentation recorded, but it is a pre-existing defect and expanding a time-critical task was the worse risk.

What was decided: Let Workstream A edit batch.py, which is assigned to neither workstream.
Why it was decided: It needed the identical one-line --roles change as cli.py and B was on hold, but the file still has no owner and four others are in the same position.

What was decided: Withdraw human_edit_kind and narrow human_edited to mean only that this cell's mask was hand-drawn.
Why it was decided: Morphometrics measure the mask, so a hand-drawn boundary partly measures the human, while a corrected nucleus set leaves the boundary machine-drawn by the same rules as every other cell.

What was decided: Record a manual cell split as created_by_split rather than as a kind of human_edited.
Why it was decided: split_by_watershed places the dividing surface from human markers so the child's mask is machine-drawn, and two fields carrying one fact would be free to drift apart.

What was decided: Put human_edited and created_by_split on CellRecord, not on FileRecord or in the operations record.
Why it was decided: Both facts vary within a single image, so per-image storage would collapse the distinction the flags exist to make.

What was decided: Store origin on FileRecord beside run_id and export it as one export_summary.csv key rather than a cells.csv column.
Why it was decided: Pool separation is enforced so origin cannot vary within a pool, and a column carrying one value on every row of every export says less than a single key.

What was decided: Export run_id as a cells.csv column even though origin is not.
Why it was decided: Nothing separates pools by run id, so two runs at identical parameters land in one pool and a single summary key would have to pick one and misreport the rest.

What was decided: Key each pool on the Phase A parameter subset - pool_<origin>_<phaseA_hash> - instead of on the full params_hash.
Why it was decided: Five fields on SegmentationParams are read only during measurement, so a full-hash key would let picking cd68_threshold strand the very cell set it was picked from.

What was decided: Include soma_erode_um in the Phase A subset despite its docstring listing it as a measurement knob.
Why it was decided: segment_image reads it at pipeline.py:526 to compute soma_centroid on every stored cell, so changing it changes stored Phase A output.

What was decided: Guard the Phase A subset with an exhaustiveness test and a perturbation test rather than a hand-listed set.
Why it was decided: min_spur_um escaped a hash that digested every field on the dataclass, so breadth without a test is not a defence.

What was decided: Move the nucleus cache out of the pool to a study-level cache folder.
Why it was decided: Detection depends on only some Phase A fields, so two pools differing only in cell_coefficient would each re-pay 200-500 s per image for a bit-identical result.

What was decided: Store the Phase A hash on FileRecord.params_hash rather than the full hash.
Why it was decided: The full hash at segment time folds in Phase C values still set to None, so two Phase-A-identical images would carry different values.

What was decided: Drop the planned params_hash guard on preserve_cell as no longer needed.
Why it was decided: Pools keyed on Phase A parameters put identically-numbered cell_uids in separate pools, so the cell_uid transplant it guarded against cannot occur.

What was decided: Reject an absolute cutoff for plaque geometry after measuring it across 20 real images.
Why it was decided: A coefficient of 1.0 realises levels from 115 to 18334, and low values gave three zero-plaque WT images 30, 20 and 7 objects while high values erased all 6 from a dim 5xFAD field.

What was decided: Replace the two 6E10 cutoffs with one seed-grow mask - seed by plaque_veto_coefficient, grow by an absolute threshold - serving geometry and burden alike.
Why it was decided: Contact is a surface-to-surface measure and so depends on where the plaque boundary sits, which the argument that a plaque's centre barely moves does not cover.

What was decided: Admit unseeded objects above the same 25 um3 floor and flag every plaque as seeded or not.
Why it was decided: A genuinely diffuse deposit has no dense core, so excluding it would lose 5xFAD signal, and the flag keeps the question answerable from the export afterwards.

What was decided: Rename plaque_threshold to plaque_grow_threshold and bump the schema from 5 to 6.
Why it was decided: Keeping the name would let it quietly mean something larger, which is the failure found in human_edited's docstring three days earlier.

What was decided: Retarget the plaque veto at the DAPI core rather than at the visible amyloid.
Why it was decided: The veto exists to remove false DAPI, so every bit of mask beyond it eats genuine nuclei near plaques - exactly where plaque-associated microglia are.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Run item 9 before item 8 and make item 8 study-level rather than per-image.
Why it was decided: Both pickers are None until item 9 runs, so with item 8 first the parameters file was written incomplete while export requires it complete.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep the screen numbers fixed rather than renumbering them to match the new order.
Why it was decided: A pointer of the form 'item N' decays into a plausible wrong target rather than a broken one, and four had already decayed that way.

What was decided: Keep the two study thresholds at the end of Phase B rather than moving them earlier.
Why it was decided: A semi-auto user still wants a pool of reviewed cells before sending it to Phase C, even though the plaque threshold needs no cells at all.

What was decided: End the interface at save-parameters, offering no bridge into Phase C.
Why it was decided: One route into Phase C beats two even when the second is safe, so a semi-auto user runs measure and export exactly as a batch user does.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make item 8 the session's commit point, holding steps 1-7 entirely in memory.
Why it was decided: A crashed session then leaves nothing by construction, where a write at step 6 would leave merged cells that a later measure from another session would sweep up.

What was decided: Remember nothing between runs: every session re-enters channel roles, study root and the two editable parameters.
Why it was decided: Roles sit in the Phase A hash, so a mistyped one produces a separate pool rather than a contaminated one - a stronger guarantee than remembering plus verification.

What was decided: Ask for the study root at intake instead of inferring it from the image path.
Why it was decided: parse_metadata cannot know where a study begins, and one extra level of nesting silently yields a parent folder name as a genotype.

What was decided: Write the parameters file into a derived folder under a user-chosen name, blocking any overwrite and offering the rename in place.
Why it was decided: An existing file may already have produced cells in a pool, so overwriting leaves that pool's params_hash matching no file on disk.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Require the save: quitting or crashing before item 8 discards the entire session.
Why it was decided: Taken with the cost visible - item 7's human editing is inside the blast radius and the cache cannot rebuild it - in exchange for a pool that can never hold half-finished work.

What was decided: Lift the path hold and adopt the root-relative contract of genotype folder then animal folder then file.
Why it was decided: The hold's own note said a declared root would remove the need for the closed genotype vocabulary, and intake gained one the same day.

What was decided: Stop parsing section, region and index from the filename.
Why it was decided: The program may fairly demand a folder structure but not that every file be renamed, and the analyst reads them off the file column.

What was decided: Store genotype and animal on FileRecord rather than re-deriving them at export.
Why it was decided: The export holds the path but not the root, so under a root-relative contract it cannot derive either.

What was decided: Give up GenotypeMismatch and retire the hardcoded genotype vocabulary.
Why it was decided: Matching a filename against a path needs the vocabulary a declared root retires; the gain is that genotype becomes whatever the folder is called.

What was decided: Remove section, region and image_index from cells.csv rather than leaving them blank.
Why it was decided: A permanently empty column reads as missing data rather than as data nobody collects.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Split item 9 into two screens, 9a for CD68 and 9b for plaque.
Why it was decided: Measured at production scale the two pickers fall on opposite sides of the live-versus-commit line - 460 ms against 9-11 s - so they cannot share an interaction model.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Pick both study thresholds on the one session image, with no cross-check against the rest of the study.
Why it was decided: Taken against measured evidence that CD68 p99.9 spans 136 to 58641 and sorts by genotype, so a value picked on a bright field can silently zero a dim one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Show seeded and unseeded plaques only after commit, never on the live per-slice view.
Why it was decided: Seeded status is a property of the whole 3D component, so a slice view could show a seeded object as unseeded and be wrong.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build intake as one screen: select buttons for root and file, four channel rows, and a single voxel box in z, y, x order.
Why it was decided: The dependency chain is short, and a sequence would make the user page backwards to fix a role after seeing the result.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Show both stain and role in each channel dropdown.
Why it was decided: The segment refusal and the parameters file both name roles, so a screen that only says Iba1 leaves the user unable to recognise cell.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Show a max-projection thumbnail beside each channel dropdown.
Why it was decided: Roles are re-entered every run, and seeing that one channel is punctate and another ramified is what makes that both fast and safe.

What was decided: Remove the channel-swap check from the interface entirely.
Why it was decided: The thumbnails show what each channel contains, and what replaces it - an exact comparison against FileRecord.channel_roles in edit mode - cannot be wrong the way a statistical test can.

What was decided: Block Continue when the chosen file is not exactly two folders under the root.
Why it was decided: Genotype is the folder under the root and animal the folder under that, so any other depth takes both from the wrong place.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build item 2 as one overlaid view of four layers, controls on the right, with a single projection toggle for all layers.
Why it was decided: The judgement is containment, which can only be read stacked, and a per-layer toggle would let the mask cover more than it should and make everything look contained.

What was decided: Colour-code DAPI as removed versus retained on the veto screen.
Why it was decided: The retargeted test is whether the mask ate a real nucleus, which cannot be judged from a view showing only what was eaten.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Block Continue on every commit screen while a control differs from its committed value, marking the commit button with an exclamation.
Why it was decided: Under edit-then-commit the view still describes the previous values, and gating the only action that leaves the screen removes the danger of acting on a stale one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Lay item 3 out 3DMorph-style: controls on the left, raw Iba1 and the binary mask beside them.
Why it was decided: Two layers in two panels leave the left column free, and 3DMorph's ThresholdGUI is the direct precedent for this screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make cell_coefficient a slider from 0 to 3 that recalculates on release.
Why it was decided: 0.25 s per slice is live but dragging would queue five seconds of work behind the hand, and PrestoCell's 0-to-5 slider puts 96% of its travel above the shipped 0.18.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep min_object_voxels and closing_radius_um as commit-only controls on item 3.
Why it was decided: Both are genuinely 3D, so a single-slice preview of either would show a mask the pipeline will never make.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Report one connected-component count under the binary panel, updating on commit only.
Why it was decided: All three controls move it, and a falling count as the slider drops is the signature of cells fusing - one measured field ran 489 objects to 537 cells.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give item 3 no projection toggle at all.
Why it was decided: Otsu is computed per slice so the judgement is per slice, and a projection would show a union that no single plane ever produces.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put item 4's live membership_threshold slider above the detection parameters, with commit last.
Why it was decided: The two classes of control are 500 seconds apart, and the separation stops anyone nudging nucleus_diameter_um expecting the responsiveness the slider just gave them.

What was decided: Colour nucleus labels per label - microglial saturated, non-microglial muted - instead of a single highlight colour.
Why it was decided: A fused pair and a touching pair are otherwise indistinguishable, and the split gesture then cannot be used because you cannot see when to reach for it.

What was decided: Keep non-microglial nuclei individually distinguishable rather than one undifferentiated wash.
Why it was decided: A microglial nucleus fused with a neighbour's scores roughly half - 0.35 falls to about 0.18, under the threshold - so the fusion most worth catching sits in that population.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Split a nucleus by shift-clicking each one and releasing shift to execute.
Why it was decided: split_by_watershed takes a markers array, so one click per nucleus gives N-way splits for free and the release supplies the terminator a single click could not.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Bind undo to the u key, stepping back exactly one operation on the operations record per press.
Why it was decided: The record is then the undo stack, so undo and the persisted history cannot disagree.

What was decided: Fix normalize at log and keep it off the interface.
Why it was decided: Its reasoning is measured - the default found 5 nuclei on a test slice against log compression's 24 - so no judgement is left for the user to make.

What was decided: Warn before a detection commit discards nucleus edits, and only when edits exist.
Why it was decided: Re-running Cellpose returns an entirely new label array, but a warning that fires with nothing to lose is one people learn to click through.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep the view interactive through the 200-500 s detection, with per-slice progress.
Why it was decided: Holding the previous result on screen buys nothing if the canvas is frozen, and detection runs slice by slice so a slice count is available.

What was decided: Defer colour and typography to a session after all nine layouts are settled.
Why it was decided: Colour already carries meaning on four screens plus red for errors, and decided per screen those meanings collide.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Title item 5 'Iba1 measurement threshold' and mirror three layers across two panels, threshold 1 left and threshold 2 right.
Why it was decided: Judging what the extension added needs the boundary it started from beside it, and one toggle driving both copies keeps the panels in a single state.

What was decided: Show raw against raw while uncommitted and cells against cells after, never one of each.
Why it was decided: Threshold 1's finished mask beside threshold 2's raw preview would credit the coefficient with hole-filling and 3D closing it did not do.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Draw item 5's committed panels as cells rather than masks, as booleans.
Why it was decided: assign_labels_by_connectivity leaves no-cell components unassigned, so a mask view would credit threshold 2 with foreground that joined no cell.

What was decided: Run mask_coefficient from 0 to the current cell_coefficient and open it at the top.
Why it was decided: Above cell_coefficient the parameter is provably a no-op, so the screen opens with both panels identical and every move is visibly additive.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Accumulate one row per commit in item 5's results table, and make it scroll.
Why it was decided: The trade between CD68 captured and mask volume is only legible as a comparison, and a session may try many values.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Disable item 5's z-batch depth box until the first commit rather than leaving it inert.
Why it was decided: Before a commit only one slice has been computed, and a control that silently does nothing is worse than one that says it cannot yet.

What was decided: Link contrast limits as well as visibility across each mirrored layer pair.
Why it was decided: The same tissue at two brightnesses would make the tighter-looking mask simply the one drawn darker.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Title item 6 'Cell size cutoff' and copy 3DMorph's CellSizeCutoffGUI rather than redesigning it.
Why it was decided: Its three panels and list already fit the job, and only four things genuinely differ from what that screen does.

What was decided: Open item 6's cutoff box at 0 and sort its list smallest-first.
Why it was decided: Nothing is filtered at 0 so every move is visibly subtractive, and the cutoff is a floor so the cells being judged should be where you land.

What was decided: Withdraw the proposed volume histogram from item 6.
Why it was decided: The sorted list of about 60 volumes is the distribution already, so a histogram beside it would draw the same evidence twice.

What was decided: Colour item 6's field view by size RANK, computed once, rather than by absolute volume.
Why it was decided: Survivors span 20 to about 4000 um3 so a value ramp squashes nearly every cell into one end, and re-ranking would shift every colour as the cutoff moved.

What was decided: Carry removed and selected on ALPHA rather than a second hue, with selection winning over the cutoff.
Why it was decided: A sequential ramp puts small cells at the dark end, which is exactly where the removed ones are, so desaturation would collide with size.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Accept that item 6's field view is one max projection, so cells overlapping in xy but separated in z collapse.
Why it was decided: Every number comes from the 3D labels and never from the picture, so the view locates while the list decides.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Title 9a 'CD68 threshold' and make it purely visual - no readout, no commit, no gate.
Why it was decided: The whole above-threshold volume renders live, so nothing on the screen can lag its controls and a gate would have nothing to guard.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Preview 9a over the whole volume rather than one slice, and allow projection at any time.
Why it was decided: 460 ms is inside the live budget, and CD68 is punctate so a single plane is the least informative view of exactly that channel.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give both study-level pickers a LOG slider with the absolute value in a box beside it.
Why it was decided: The useful range spans about three orders of magnitude low in the sensor's range, so a linear slider would be dead across most of its travel.

What was decided: Draw 9a's cells layer and 9b's plaque layer as outlines rather than fills.
Why it was decided: Each sits on top of the thing being judged, and a fill tints the interior that is being looked at.

What was decided: Start 9b's 22 s seed mask in the background any time after item 2, silently and without blocking.
Why it was decided: It depends only on item 2's coefficient, so 9b can open with its expensive half already done.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Title 9b '6E10 threshold', naming both study-level pickers by channel.
Why it was decided: It makes their symmetry visible and keeps 9b apart from item 2, which uses the same channel for the opposite purpose.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Preview 9b's grow mask over the whole volume rather than per slice.
Why it was decided: 617 ms is inside the live budget; what actually costs 9 to 11 s is labelling and classifying, which no preview reaches.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move min_plaque_volume_um3 from item 8 to 9b as a live, ungated control.
Why it was decided: Item 8's own rule makes a parameter editable there only if nowhere else asks, and the floor now has a screen that shows its consequence.

What was decided: Add item 2's veto mask to 9b as a third layer, off by default.
Why it was decided: It is the only thing that explains whether an object is unseeded because it is coreless or because the veto ran small, and it is already computed.

What was decided: Accumulate 9b's seeded and unseeded counts with the threshold and floor that produced them.
Why it was decided: The count is a trend rather than a state - the rate unseeded objects appear at is the signal that background has been reached.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give item 8 intake's shape: one titled screen, no viewer, button centred at the bottom.
Why it was decided: It is the only screen in the component with nothing to look at, so the form is the whole content.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Head item 8's read-only groups with SCREEN TITLES rather than item numbers.
Why it was decided: The read-only rule has always promised to name the screen to go back to, which bare numbers could not do until the nine titles existed.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Show item 8's hand-edits sentence only when edits exist, carrying the count.
Why it was decided: A user who hand-splits nuclei and expects batch to reproduce it would be silently wrong, but a warning that fires with nothing to lose gets clicked through.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Report item 8's filename collision as red text under SAVE rather than as a dialog.
Why it was decided: It fires on every session from the second onward, and item 1 already puts its failures under its button.

What was decided: End item 8 with a popup carrying the cell count, both paths and both commands, including --params-hash.
Why it was decided: Choosing no bridge to Phase C means the user types them, and export refuses when a pool holds more than one parameter set.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move through z with the LEFT and RIGHT arrow keys on every screen.
Why it was decided: The tool runs on a laptop where scrolling is unreliable, and napari already binds the arrows by default so nothing has to be built.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put a labelled position indicator - z slice (23/40) or z batch (1/4) - on every screen with a z slider.
Why it was decided: The same two keys move between slices in one mode and between batches in the other, and nothing else on screen said which.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put a clickable '?' on every adjustable control, saying what it changes here and whether it is live or on commit.
Why it was decided: The controls carry their parameter-file names, which say what they are called rather than what moving them does.

What was decided: Give COLOURS and LAYERS one block-level '?' each rather than one per row.
Why it was decided: Applied per row the rule gave item 2 ten extra marks for a block whose entire content is how the layers are drawn.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Let the user pick each layer's colour, with a translucency slider beneath it.
Why it was decided: The two layers where alpha already carries meaning are exactly the two with no picker, so the pair travels together with no exception to remember.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Drop the projection checkbox everywhere and let z-batch depth 1 be the slice view.
Why it was decided: The two controls were doing one job, and depth 1 gives the native slider back unchanged.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Raise a popup naming the changed control when CONTINUE is pressed uncommitted, on every screen with a COMMIT.
Why it was decided: The exclamation mark said something was wrong but not what, and stating the set by property stopped a hand-listed one going stale.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Add item 4 to the commit-gated set and remove 9a from it.
Why it was decided: Item 4 has three commit-only detection parameters and had no gate at all, while 9a has no commit to gate.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep item numbers out of the interface entirely, naming screens by title or by description.
Why it was decided: They are a device for planning between the user and the sessions, and nobody using the tool has ever seen one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Correct item 3's stated reason for making closing_radius_um commit-only: the closing is xy-only, not 3D.
Why it was decided: fill_soma_holes builds a one-slice-thick element deliberately, so the step that cannot be previewed is the 3D hole fill before it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Reclassify normalize on item 8 from read-only to not-shown.
Why it was decided: Item 4's layout took it off that screen the day after the table was written, and the user is never asked for it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Correct the cache plan: the CD68 channel opens at item 5, not at a picker.
Why it was decided: Item 5's headline figure is threshold-free, so a screen can need a channel without needing that channel's parameter.

What was decided: Make plaque_dilate_um signed and rename it plaque_veto_margin_um.
Why it was decided: Raising the coefficient can erase a dim plaque's mask entirely while an erosion pulls every mask back uniformly, and a name saying dilate cannot carry a negative.

What was decided: Pad stored cell crops by 6.0 um, specified in micrometres rather than voxels.
Why it was decided: Review edits masks on the stored crop, and at 5.5:1 anisotropy a voxel count reaches five and a half times further in z than in plane.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Measure item 9a's own readout cost instead of accepting the 3.4 s figure that had made it a commit screen.
Why it was decided: That figure timed the per-cell loop Phase C runs; the two numbers the screen wanted cost 39 ms on a preview already being paid.

What was decided: Run review as ONE queue, with triage the entry for both pool kinds and rich review a mode entered per cell.
Why it was decided: Two separately launched tools would give two positions in the work, and resuming at the first unreviewed cell only has one meaning with one queue.

What was decided: Make rich review always resolve the cell - accept, delete, or split and then resolve each daughter.
Why it was decided: The cell then leaves triage for good, so there is no edited-but-unaccepted state to resume into and no page position to store.

What was decided: Hold the rich review episode in memory until it is finalised, so undo unwinds splits as well as process edits.
Why it was decided: The parent is not deleted until the episode commits, which is the shape Component 3 already uses for its own steps.

What was decided: Order review files by ARRIVAL rather than natural path order, and allow no skipping.
Why it was decided: New files then always append instead of inserting before work already done, so the queue never reshuffles under a reviewer.

What was decided: Treat a review session as a sitting, resuming at the first unreviewed cell.
Why it was decided: The queue belongs to the pool rather than the session, and stopping mid-file is the normal case across 20,000 decisions.

What was decided: End review at the pool with no bridge to Phase C, showing the pool path and the two commands.
Why it was decided: One route beats two even when the second is safe, which is the answer Component 3 took for the same question.

What was decided: Treat item 7 as Component 5 at one-image scale rather than a separate screen.
Why it was decided: Triage works for one image's 60 cells, so the shared editor is reached the same way from both entry points.

What was decided: Hold the colour and typography session until after Component 5's planning and layout.
Why it was decided: Colour is more shared than the editing module is, and contact-sheet density decides how many pixels a cell gets to be distinguished in.

What was decided: Add a merge-stamped import_order to FileRecord.
Why it was decided: created_at is stamped at segment time, which a 700-task array produces in arbitrary order, whereas arrival is a merge-time fact.

What was decided: Give Pool a replace_cell_mask that writes arrays, updates n_voxels and human_edited, and clears that file's measurements.
Why it was decided: Pool can read arrays but not write them, and Phase C's queue is defined by absence so an edit must delete rows to re-queue itself.

What was decided: Write the array file before the database row when a mask changes.
Why it was decided: A crash between the two then leaves a recomputable n_voxels rather than a row claiming an edit that never happened.

What was decided: Add human_edited and n_voxels to preserve_cell, with a test classifying every column as Phase A's or a human's.
Why it was decided: A re-merge otherwise reverts both while the edited mask stays on disk, and the status still reads confirmed so nothing looks wrong.

What was decided: Delete each fragment after the merge that consumed it, and resume from fragment OR file record.
Why it was decided: Fragments stop being a rebuild source once a human touches the database, and re-folding them is what damages an edited cell.

What was decided: Drop a debris rejection's arrays and keep its row.
Why it was decided: The precision count is a database query, and nothing downstream reads a debris cell's mask.

What was decided: Delete every measurement for a file when any of its cells is edited.
Why it was decided: The per-image row derives from the cell masks, and one rule that cannot rot beats a selective one needing a maintained list.

What was decided: Extend check_integrity to compare n_voxels against its own mask.
Why it was decided: It looks only for arrays with no manifest entry today, so the one failure the file-first write order can leave behind is invisible.

What was decided: Give the colour and typography session's agenda a single home in COMPONENT_03_PLAN section 6d, gathering the constraints while leaving the originals where they sit.
Why it was decided: The count 'five constraints' appeared twice in the log and was enumerated nowhere, and a wrong inference drawn from that count is what proved the gap was real.

What was decided: Add a sixth colour constraint: items 4 and 6 want opposite kinds of colormap, so that session needs at least two schemes rather than one.
Why it was decided: Item 4 needs categorical distinctness per label while item 6 needs a sequential ramp by size, and a palette chosen for one is wrong for the other.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Record that cividis is reachable in napari 0.7.1 only through ensure_colormap's matplotlib fallback, not through AVAILABLE_COLORMAPS.
Why it was decided: Item 6's ramp is assigned in code rather than picked from a dropdown so the constraint stands, but a later session must not read 'napari ships both' as meaning both appear in the picker.

What was decided: Settle split_method as watershed program-wide rather than switching to pbc_gudhi.
Why it was decided: On the clumpiest images yet marked, watershed separated 10 of 14 clump pairs against gudhi's 9, with fewer false positives and about 50x less runtime.

What was decided: Disqualify the fixed-tau pbc back end from consideration entirely, keeping it in split.py only for comparison.
Why it was decided: Its historic advantage vanishes at tau of 0.10 and above, and the constant was invented for this project where PrestoCell searches for it, so the advantage was a tuned number rather than a mechanism.

What was decided: Accept that the splitter has no remaining headroom, because every under-split watershed leaves is a one-nucleus cell.
Why it was decided: Splitting needs at least two seeds, so 7 of 7 residual failures are structurally unreachable by any back end and the remaining accuracy is upstream in nucleus detection.

What was decided: Make route B, the reviewer seeding each cell body, the only split route in Component 5, dropping route C and leaving route A to Component 3's item 4.
Why it was decided: Every residual under-split is a one-nucleus cell, so the reviewer's markers are the missing second seed and no algorithm can supply it.

What was decided: Give triage and rich review separate undos that hand over at finalisation.
Why it was decided: Triage only flips statuses and destroys nothing, whereas a debris rejection drops the cell's arrays at finalisation and is genuinely irreversible.

What was decided: Split each file's triage into three screens, hard then medium then easy, by within-file quantile at 15 per cent, 35 per cent and the rest.
Why it was decided: QC scores are not comparable across images, so a study-wide cutoff cannot work while a relative band is self-calibrating and needs no constant.

What was decided: Offer no per-cell accept in triage; a single cell is resolved only by clicking into rich review.
Why it was decided: It keeps triage to two bulk actions and makes every individual judgement a deliberate act rather than a keystroke.

What was decided: Flag only xy border contact under a triage tile, reusing item 6's exclamation mark rather than inventing a second vocabulary.
Why it was decided: Nearly every cell reaches a z boundary because a 24 um stack cannot contain a 50 um microglion, so a z badge would appear on almost every tile and stop being a signal.

What was decided: Confine rejection to rich review, running it as two popups asking real cell or debris and then how many cells.
Why it was decided: Section 8 rejected a per-rejection modal as unaffordable at contact-sheet pace, and moving rejection off that pace is exactly what makes it affordable.

What was decided: Answer section 7's Q4: rich review carries per-cell editing and splitting only, with no thresholds and no re-segmentation.
Why it was decided: Both populations arrive already segmented under settled parameters, and a second place to set a hashed value would be a second route into a decision Component 3 owns.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Refuse to take material from a cell already accepted, and offer a popup transfer from any other neighbour.
Why it was decided: cell_labels gives every voxel exactly one label so overlapping claims are corruption, and silently altering an accepted cell would change a decision nobody looks at again.

What was decided: Allow any addition without a connectivity check and bridge it to the cell instead of blocking it.
Why it was decided: A strict touch requirement would block the severed process the feature exists to repair, since a severed process is detached by definition.

What was decided: Record that a detached addition is invisible three ways at once: status stays ok, endpoint and branch-length counts disagree, and ramification index shifts with distance.
Why it was decided: The same 25-voxel blob moved ramification index by 12 per cent at 50 px against 1.2 per cent for a larger attached blob, because the index is a convex hull ratio.

What was decided: Colour the soma as its own region that cannot be deleted, re-derived rather than edited when a cell is split.
Why it was decided: A cell with no body is not a repair, and the soma is the morphological opening the export already reports as soma_volume_um3.

What was decided: Show only this cell's stored nucleus mask in rich review, never the DAPI channel.
Why it was decided: Raw DAPI cannot be filtered by cell, and the ceiling measurement shows no residual clump has a second nucleus to reveal anyway.

What was decided: Define an editable part by intensity persistence, using PrestoCell's ToMATo clustering of the clicked region.
Why it was decided: The threshold adapts to each region's own persistence spans rather than resting on a constant, and watershed makes its errors at intensity dips rather than at branch points.

What was decided: Set idx_coef to 0.96 for processes and 0.90 for parts within a process.
Why it was decided: Measured across five real cells 0.96 gives 11 to 29 processes and 0.90 gives 4 to 9 parts, against PrestoCell's shipped 0.75 which gives 50 to 154.

What was decided: Add a seventh colour constraint: the cell editor needs up to about 29 distinct categorical regions at once.
Why it was decided: 0.96 scales the process count with cell volume, which is above the range where colour-blind-safe hues exist, so the scheme needs a second channel beyond hue.

What was decided: Let review read the source image, resolving it exactly as measure does from FileRecord.source_path.
Why it was decided: phasec.py already opens the source, so measure cannot run without the images either, and reading one channel of the largest image on disk costs 0.60 s.

What was decided: Retire section 2's clause that review must stay usable when the source is unreachable.
Why it was decided: It guarded a state in which nothing downstream works, so it was protecting nothing.

What was decided: Store nothing extra in the per-cell crop for review: no intensity, no threshold mask, no neighbouring labels.
Why it was decided: All three come from elsewhere once review reads the source, which removed 8.86 GB of measured storage across the study.

What was decided: Store the file's threshold-2 mask at Phase A and delete it when that file completes review.
Why it was decided: Phase A already computes and discards it, re-deriving it during review costs 38 to 54 s per file, and deletion bounds peak storage by unreviewed files rather than by the study.

What was decided: Compute the per-file threshold mask and each cell's decomposition in the background while the reviewer works that file's triage screens.
Why it was decided: Triage renders from stored thumbnails and touches the source not at all, so the window exists by construction rather than needing to be made.

What was decided: Reduce the stored thumbnail to a mask-only max projection, dropping the nucleus pane.
Why it was decided: Triage renders a silhouette in the style of item 6's cell size cutoff screen and never needs the nucleus channel.

What was decided: Close the pyramid question: there is no multi-resolution pyramid anywhere in this project.
Why it was decided: Rich review shows a crop of about 4.5 M voxels against a field's 212 M, napari does no level-of-detail in 3D, and a pyramid costs about 31 per cent more memory than a flat array.

What was decided: Run rich review in 3D only, with no slice mode and no z control of any kind.
Why it was decided: Clicking is a ray cast that takes the first visible voxel, so the reviewer rotates to reach whatever is occluded.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make the display margin a slider in micrometres that takes effect on release.
Why it was decided: PrestoCell's equivalent is in pixels applied isotropically, which at this project's 5.5:1 anisotropy reaches 5.5x further in z than in the plane.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Settle pointer conventions: wheel and pinch zoom, scrollbars do the scrolling, and z navigation stays on the arrow keys.
Why it was decided: Scrolling is unreliable on the laptop this runs on, which is the reason z went to the arrow keys in the first place.

What was decided: Make finalisation one transaction over the whole rich-review episode rather than one per cell.
Why it was decided: A transfer touches two cells, an addition can grow the bounding box, and a split creates and deletes cells, all within a single episode.

What was decided: Withdraw request 18, the 6.0 um of stored crop padding, before it was ever sent.
Why it was decided: Reading the source removes the display need and a growable bounding box removes the limit rather than raising it by 6 um.

What was decided: Send request 19, storing the file threshold mask and making the thumbnail mask-only, and request 20, the endpoint and branch-length disagreement on disconnected masks.
Why it was decided: Both live in Workstream A's files, and request 20 is marked latent because bridging means a disconnected mask should never be produced.

What was decided: Hide only confirmed cells in rich review, leaving real_cell rejections visible and takeable and debris material freely addable.
Why it was decided: A real_cell rejection is still a cell, while a debris rejection has already had its arrays deleted so its voxels cannot be identified as owned even in principle.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give the everything-else layer a colour picker rather than a two-class ownership scheme.
Why it was decided: With confirmed cells hidden, everything remaining is either added directly or through one popup, so the visual distinction stopped being load-bearing.

What was decided: Mute the other processes while one is entered, and drop the status block that would have announced it.
Why it was decided: Without muting the two states draw the same picture, and muting is item 4's modulate-do-not-replace constraint applied to a second component.

What was decided: Offer mip, translucent and attenuated mip as rendering modes in rich review, defaulting to translucent.
Why it was decided: Depth is the judgement on this screen, and translucent is the napari equivalent of the Blend mode the Imaris review named for exactly that job.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Record that PrestoCell runs on napari's default mip rendering and never offers a choice.
Why it was decided: It only ever sets blending, which governs how layers composite rather than how a volume is projected, and the two property names invite exactly that confusion.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give the two triage accept actions buttons with no key, and give undo a key with no button.
Why it was decided: The actions that dispose of work then need a deliberate pointer act, while the action that recovers work stays the fast one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Title all three triage screens CELL REVIEW - TRIAGE and name the band only inside the screen 1 of 3 popup.
Why it was decided: The tool should not grade the reviewer's work in a heading, and the band is a rank within one image rather than a difficulty.

What was decided: Collapse rich review's seven-gesture legend to a single question mark above the buttons.
Why it was decided: Drawn out it consumed the whole right column, and a screen whose controls are mostly invisible gestures is better served by one honest mark than a wall of text.

What was decided: Mint split children by suffixing the parent uid, giving file__c0007_s1 and _s2, nesting on any re-split.
Why it was decided: Provenance then reads straight off cells.csv with no join and no surviving parent row, and Phase A never emits _s so collision is impossible.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Clarify that item 7 has no layout of its own and is a step in Component 3's flow rather than a screen.
Why it was decided: It is Component 5 at one-image scale, so there is nothing separate to design and every phrase about item 7's layout means Component 5's layout session.

What was decided: Have merge's completion line name the pool and the review command, and add review to the CLI usage banner.
Why it was decided: The banner documents the batch route as segment, merge, measure, export, so a user following it runs measure on an unreviewed pool and gets zero cells with no reason given.

What was decided: Record that NEW-g and NEW-b landed on 2026-08-12, against B's closing documents listing them as pending blockers.
Why it was decided: Both are live in the code and B had verified them itself in its first session, so acting on the stale claim would have repeated finished work and re-bumped the schema.

What was decided: Restore nuclei.py, markers.py and soma.py to Workstream A's file list.
Why it was decided: A's founding handoff has always assigned all three, and B's closing ownership map dropped them and called nuclei.py unclaimed and urgent for its request 17.

What was decided: Treat request 10 as writing soma_erode_um's first comment rather than correcting an existing docstring.
Why it was decided: The field has no docstring at all - it sits under a bare group header and is one of ten with no purpose recorded - though the substance stands, since it is read in both phases.

What was decided: The ten colours every picker offers are defined by us, with raised endpoints.
Why it was decided: Pure primaries left 6 of 10 too dim to use on black — blue at relative luminance 0.072 — and gave a dichromat 10 identical pairs against 3.

What was decided: Napari's own colormaps are not used for layer colours.
Why it was decided: 8 of its 30 map value 0 to a non-black colour, so under additive stacking a layer's empty part paints the screen.

What was decided: violet and spring green join the user's eight.
Why it was decided: They are the only two gaps left in the hue wheel, so the ten lay out as a spectrum a user scans rather than reads.

What was decided: One hue per channel, program-wide — 6E10 magenta, Iba1 white, CD68 green, DAPI blue, DAPI-removed red.
Why it was decided: A colour then means the same thing on every screen it appears on, rather than one thing per screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Every image layer uses additive blending.
Why it was decided: Translucent lets a mostly-empty layer's black pixels blank the layer beneath it, and every layer here is mostly empty.

What was decided: The picker is a 2×5 swatch grid in hue-wheel order, 24 px cells, the current choice ringed 2 px #e2e4e6 with a 1 px gap.
Why it was decided: The gap is what keeps the ring readable on the white swatch, and wheel order lets a user move toward a colour instead of searching.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: No text is ever drawn over image data; readouts sit in a strip above the canvas.
Why it was decided: Text over dark fluorescence is legible until the image is bright underneath it, and the alternative is inventing a scrim.

What was decided: Panels stay flat #262930, no tints and no dividers.
Why it was decided: The canvas is black against the chrome's #262930, so it separates itself, and #2e323a stays reserved for popups.

What was decided: Side columns fixed at 260 px and 280 px with the centre stretching.
Why it was decided: Controls need a constant width to stay legible and only the image benefits from more room.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Screen titles are Title Case, correcting §4's sentence-case table.
Why it was decided: §6e.2 requires it for titles and item 1 had already settled Image Intake.

What was decided: Control labels stay as the code identifiers.
Why it was decided: Item 8 lists them read-only and the parameters file uses the same words, so a second vocabulary is one more thing to keep in step.

What was decided: Item 2's veto mask is drawn as a 2 px outline rather than a fill.
Why it was decided: No four of the ten usable colours survive a dichromat (best 4-set ΔE 7.8 against a 3-set's 95.4), and an outline drops the count to three.

What was decided: The veto outline takes 6E10's own magenta.
Why it was decided: Form separates it from the raw fill, measured at 5.9× brighter on typical amyloid and 2.0× even on a saturated core.

What was decided: vetoed DAPI starts off.
Why it was decided: It holds the identical voxels to DAPI-removed (nuclei.py:157), so both on sum to double brightness and read as a third class of object.

What was decided: Accepted: 6E10 magenta and DAPI blue are ΔE 12.9 apart for a protanope.
Why it was decided: Alpha, shape and position separate them, and one hue per channel is worth more than the pair.

What was decided: orange rejected for DAPI-removed in favour of red.
Why it was decided: *Removed* is what red means, and the veto outline already carries the state by position.

What was decided: Above z-batch depth 1 the mask is projected and then outlined, never the reverse.
Why it was decided: Outline-then-project stacks ten slices' boundaries into nested rings instead of one silhouette.

What was decided: Item 3 needs no colour choice at all.
Why it was decided: Greyscale *is* the white colormap, so the channel convention and both parent programs give the same instruction.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 3's panel boundary is carried by the header labels, not a drawn rule.
Why it was decided: GridCanvas puts both panels in one black canvas, so any gap between them is black on black and invisible.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The panels are headed Raw Iba1 and Threshold preview, not "binary mask".
Why it was decided: The committed mask is fuller than the preview, and a header has to say some word so it may as well be the honest one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: n objects moves out of the right panel into the header strip.
Why it was decided: It was drawn over image data, which the no-text-over-data rule forbids.

What was decided: Contrast limits are fixed across the whole stack.
Why it was decided: Auto-stretching each slice makes a dim slice look as strong as a bright one while the per-slice Otsu threshold underneath genuinely differs.

What was decided: One slider style program-wide — groove #414851, fill #5a626c, handle #e2e4e6, value 11 pt, endpoints 10 pt muted.
Why it was decided: Item 2's translucency sliders and item 3's parameter slider are the same widget, and it introduces no new colour token.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Continue always sits at the bottom-right of the window, which on a controls-left frame means a bottom strip.
Why it was decided: It preserves §4's 2026-08-17 correction on a frame that has no right column to hold it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 3's two panels split 50/50.
Why it was decided: The comparison is like-for-like, so neither panel earns more room.

What was decided: Nucleus labels use a twelve-hue ring built in CIELAB at constant lightness L\*68 C\*38.
Why it was decided: Every hue at relative luminance 0.380 frees lightness to carry exactly one thing — membership.

What was decided: Napari's label_colormap() rejected as the label palette.
Why it was decided: Its 128 labels span luminance 0.008–0.877 and 25% are already dimmer than the muted class, so "dimmer" would mean nothing.

What was decided: A larger hue cycle rejected.
Why it was decided: The worst pair falls from 17.3 at twelve hues to 3.9 at twenty, so adding colours makes every pair worse rather than fixing collisions.

What was decided: Non-microglial nuclei mute by alpha 0.6 alone, not desaturation.
Why it was decided: Alpha costs 3 ΔE of per-label distinctness against desaturation's 6, and desaturation attacks the property the constraint protects.

What was decided: An Outline nuclei checkbox driving Labels.contour = 2, default off.
Why it was decided: At twelve hues a dichromat's worst pair is 7.8, so no palette carries identity — and contour replaces the fill, so it cannot be permanent.

What was decided: The Labels layer stays translucent and top of the stack.
Why it was decided: Additive would sum a label's hue with the DAPI beneath it and corrupt the one thing the layer exists to carry.

What was decided: A mask derived from a channel takes that channel's hue and is drawn as an outline.
Why it was decided: Item 4 overlays Iba1 raw and the Iba1 mask in one panel, so form has to separate what hue cannot.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's two Iba1 layers start off.
Why it was decided: §4's own wording is that the user identifies the soma by switching them on, which keeps the opening view to the nuclei.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Split markers are white crosses numbered 1, 2, 3 in click order.
Why it was decided: A lone 1 on screen says the split will silently do nothing *before* the user releases shift.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: LIVE removed from beside the membership slider.
Why it was decided: The "?" popup is already required to state whether a control is live or takes effect on COMMIT.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's layer table corrected to four layers and three toggles, with CD68 on both panels.
Why it was decided: B§5 requires the panels be in the same state or the screen flatters threshold 2, and CD68 on one side only is that failure.

What was decided: Both of item 5's threshold masks are white outlines.
Why it was decided: §4 gave the layer a colour because a filled mask *"would occlude both"* — an outline occludes nothing, so the objection dissolves.

What was decided: Default alpha becomes per-channel and program-wide — 6E10 0.45, Iba1 0.40, CD68 0.60, DAPI 1.00, derived outlines 1.00.
Why it was decided: Under additive blending the slider is a weight, so a default alpha is a property of the channel's role rather than of the screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's Iba1 raw amended 0.50 → 0.40.
Why it was decided: One number per channel, and it lifts item 4's own outline headroom from 2.0× to 2.5×.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's panels are headed Segmentation threshold and Measurement threshold.
Why it was decided: It reuses the vocabulary §4's title table chose when it renamed the two screens by what they decide.

What was decided: The accumulating table has a muted header, normal rows, and the current row marked ●.
Why it was decided: A mark rather than a colour, because the muted/normal pair is already carrying the hierarchy bold would otherwise.

What was decided: Disabled controls keep surface #414851 and drop their text to #6a7380.
Why it was decided: It is napari's own highlight, so no new token is invented, and the state is said in words as well as greyed.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's slider range labels stay bare — 0 and 0.18.
Why it was decided: The number is the number, and the "?" popup is where the coupling to item 3's cell_coefficient is explained.

What was decided: cividis replaces viridis for item 6's size ramp.
Why it was decided: viridis is not monotonic in lightness for a deuteranope, failing the same test §6d uses to reject jet.

What was decided: Size rank maps onto cividis[0.25, 1.0] rather than the whole ramp.
Why it was decided: The full ramp's floor is relative luminance 0.017 and the small cells being adjudicated sit exactly there.

What was decided: Selection by high alpha rejected on item 6.
Why it was decided: Kept 0.75 to selected 1.0 is 1.33×, and at the dark end of the ramp that is 0.019 against 0.014 — invisible.

What was decided: The selected cell is drawn as a white fill.
Why it was decided: 17.2× the ramp at the smallest cell and 7.3× at the cutoff, and cividis tops out at #fee838 so white never collides.

What was decided: A border-touching cell is a white outline, against selection's white fill.
Why it was decided: Same colour, different form — the split already used on items 2, 4 and 5, and it costs the palette nothing.

What was decided: The ! in item 6's list takes napari's warning #e3b617.
Why it was decided: A border cell is a caution, not an error, so it must not dilute the #f28b82 reserved for failure.

What was decided: Removed cells sit at alpha 0.25 against kept at 0.75.
Why it was decided: A flat 3.0× at every rank, because alpha multiplies — no hue-based encoding is rank-independent.

What was decided: Item 6's detail panel draws the cell in white.
Why it was decided: The selected cell is almost always a small one, and small cells sit where the ramp is too dark to read shape.

What was decided: List rows below the cutoff drop to #9aa0a6 and the selected row sits on a #414851 band.
Why it was decided: The band becomes the program-wide list-selection style rather than being settled per list.

What was decided: Rich review's regions are graph-coloured over six hues rather than given ~29 distinct ones.
Why it was decided: The requirement is that no two *touching* regions share, and a branching cell's adjacency graph needs four.

What was decided: The twelve-hue ring splits in half — the warm six for this cell, the cool six for the nucleus layers.
Why it was decided: Six already exceeds what the graph colouring needs, so the split costs nothing and buys the nuclei their own half of the circle.

What was decided: The soma is white.
Why it was decided: It is 32.7 to 49.7 from every warm hue even for a dichromat, because it differs in lightness, and it is the only region with a name.

What was decided: Entering a process draws it at alpha 1.0 and mutes the others to 0.30.
Why it was decided: A 3.3× separation, stronger than item 4's 0.6 because up to 29 regions compete rather than two classes.

What was decided: The three nucleus layers take blue, violet, and blue at 0.35 with raw DAPI off by default.
Why it was decided: Blue against violet is only ΔE 12.2 for a dichromat, so position carries it — this cell's nucleus is the one inside the white soma.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: everything else is yellow, and the derived-layer rule yields on this screen.
Why it was decided: White is the soma, and the ring has priority where the subject is a decomposition rather than a channel.

What was decided: Rich review's Iba1 signal is white at alpha 0.15, recorded as uncertain.
Why it was decided: Additive white desaturates the ring beneath it, and the value wants looking at on a real crop rather than settling from a desk.

What was decided: Triage tiles are white on black, in black tiles on #262930 gutters.
Why it was decided: The stored thumbnail is a mask-only projection with nothing written on it, so the judgement is shape.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A per-tile hover ring dropped from triage.
Why it was decided: Every tile is clickable and the only non-clickable areas are the gaps, so an affordance that is uniform needs no marker.

What was decided: Reject is not colour-coded on rich review.
Why it was decided: The popup is the guard, and it already says the action cannot be undone.

What was decided: Gaps left by resolved cells stay empty, with no placeholder.
Why it was decided: A marker there would draw the eye to work already finished, and the gap exists only so positions do not move.

What was decided: CD68 ≥ T is orange rather than CD68's green.
Why it was decided: A *state* of a channel takes its own colour, as DAPI kept and DAPI removed already do on item 2.

What was decided: Magenta and red rejected for CD68 ≥ T despite better numbers.
Why it was decided: magenta is 6E10's and 9b is the next screen; red already means *removed* on item 2 and is relY 0.04 for a protanope.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The derived-layer rule generalised: the containing thing is an outline, the contained thing is a fill.
Why it was decided: On 9a the derived mask is the contained thing, so derivation was a coincidence of the first three screens.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: 9a carries no header strip.
Why it was decided: One panel, so nothing to name, and §4 removed its readouts on 2026-08-17.

What was decided: The translucency caption is dropped from under each swatch row.
Why it was decided: The row is label → swatches → slider, and a slider beneath a swatch grid needs no caption.

What was decided: 6E10 raw rises to alpha 0.60 on item 9b.
Why it was decided: The screen judges the deposit's dim edge, so 6E10 cannot be held at a context channel's weight; the outline still runs 3.2× typical.

What was decided: 9b's plaque layer is an outline in all three states and never becomes a fill.
Why it was decided: Filling it would hide the deposit being judged, exactly when the seeded/unseeded call is being verified.

What was decided: Live plaque outlines are magenta and recolour to cyan seeded / yellow unseeded on commit.
Why it was decided: 96.6 apart for a dichromat, and neither reads as an error — §6b sends both forward into every measurement, labelled.

What was decided: The recolour doubles as the commit gate's second carrier.
Why it was decided: Moving the grow threshold reverts the outlines to magenta while the floor leaves them coloured, so the whole canvas says what is provisional.

What was decided: 9b's seed mask is spring green.
Why it was decided: White fails at ΔE 19.9 against the magenta raw fill-to-fill, and spring green is the only candidate carrying no meaning from another screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: 9b's accumulating table moves below the canvas.
Why it was decided: It matches item 5's, so the program's two accumulating tables sit in the same relation to their image.

What was decided: Item 8 needs no colour decision.
Why it was decided: §6d excluded it as the one screen with no viewer, so it takes the settled chrome unchanged.

What was decided: Task 15's six mutations were run one per tool call, restoring the pristine file at the top of each step rather than after pytest.
Why it was decided: An interrupted loop had already left a stripped confirmation gate live on disk once, and there is no git, so a green UI subset after the batch is the only proof the restores happened.

What was decided: The five-across grid test was checked not to rest on its GRID_COLUMNS == 5 line.
Why it was decided: It also asserts the wrap positions literally on twelve tiles, so a mutation caught only by an assertion restating the constant would prove nothing about the grid.

What was decided: The ToMATo cell decomposition went into prestomorph/split.py as decompose_by_persistence, not into ui/editing.py.
Why it was decided: That module already configures ToMATo and carries the argument for r=1.8 on the voxel lattice, and a second call site would be free to drift from it with nothing to say so.

What was decided: PrestoCell's pbc_mid_tau was ported with merge_threshold=max(density)+1 kept and its span index clamped.
Why it was decided: The +1 is what stops the first fit merging anything on a flat region, and int(len(spans) * idx_coef) lands one past the end as idx_coef approaches 1 and would raise.

What was decided: SomaResult gained a region array field, excluded from repr and from equality.
Why it was decided: find_soma already built that array to compute volume_um3 and then dropped it, so rebuilding the opening at the screen would be a second construction of one region free to drift — and an array field would otherwise make SomaResult == SomaResult raise.

What was decided: The rich-review screen is screen_edit_cell.py, superseding §3a's planned review_rich.py.
Why it was decided: Task 15 settled that a screen file is named for the title the user sees, so Cell Review — Edit Cell sits beside screen_triage.py.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ViewerPort gained set_rendering and set_ndisplay, and RecordingViewer refuses a mode the layer kind cannot take.
Why it was decided: Verified against napari 0.7.1: Labels accepts only translucent and iso_categorical, so a recorder that accepted mip would let a screen pass a test it would fail in front of a user.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The rendering radio drives the volume layers only, and this cell keeps translucent.
Why it was decided: The same napari fact — the control cannot reach a Labels layer even in principle, so it is recorded as a limit rather than worked around.

What was decided: The warm-six graph colouring picks the least-used legal hue rather than the first free one.
Why it was decided: Measured on a six-process cell, first-free painted every process the same pink: legal under "touching regions never share a hue" and useless against §3b's "each process its own".

What was decided: The soma stays at full alpha while a process is entered; only the other processes mute to 0.30.
Why it was decided: §3d.4 mutes "every other process" and §3b is explicit that the soma is not one, and it is the anchor for "this cell's nucleus is the one inside the white soma".

What was decided: A cell whose erosion leaves no remnant draws as one process with no white region.
Why it was decided: Taken literally from §3b's "a thin fragment with no soma reads as one process", since decomposing a fragment would claim a structure it does not have.

What was decided: An edit leaves whatever process the reviewer was inside.
Why it was decided: Re-deriving the decomposition renumbers it, so a held id may no longer denote the same region, and the cell un-muting is visible where a stale id would not be.

What was decided: bridged() joins every disconnected component of an addition, not only the nearest.
Why it was decided: Added material arrives in more than one piece whenever a debris clump is taken in parts, and one bridge would leave the rest floating — the exact failure bridging exists to prevent.

What was decided: "Already touching" means 26-adjacent — a distance of at most √3 — rather than overlapping.
Why it was decided: Testing for distance 0 called every face- and corner-adjacent addition detached and drew a bridge across a gap that did not exist; caught by a test, not by reading.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The click ray walks one voxel per step along its dominant axis, against PrestoCell's two.
Why it was decided: np.arange(1, u_max - 2, 2) skips every other voxel while microglial processes are one voxel thick, and the saving is nothing beside the 0.19–0.48 s decomposition on the next line.

What was decided: CountPopup was added to widgets.py for the rejection multiplicity.
Why it was decided: Two buttons can only answer a yes/no *about* a number, and §4.4's NEW-d is literally "this is 3 cells I cannot afford to split".

What was decided: No free-text note field was built on the real_cell rejection branch.
Why it was decided: §3c lists the screen's popups exhaustively and a note is not among them, and §8 requires that the note never be mandatory.

What was decided: The rejection multiplicity is produced by the screen and stored nowhere.
Why it was decided: Request NEW-f is deferred at HANDOFF_MERGE.md §5, so no schema field exists to receive it and inventing one would pull deferred work forward.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: gudhi>=3.7 was declared in the ui optional-dependency group.
Why it was decided: It was an undeclared optional pipeline path until rich review made the decomposition a hard requirement of the interface.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ui/preview.py was created and the four shared preview helpers moved into it.
Why it was decided: Task 13 recorded the condition — "two callers did not justify the churn, three would" — and item 9a is the third caller.

What was decided: screen_threshold1 re-exports the four moved helpers.
Why it was decided: Item 5 and item 3's own tests name them there, so the definitions move to one place while every existing import path stays valid.

What was decided: Item 9a's preview is named and computed as CD68 > T, against the plan's drawn CD68 ≥ T.
Why it was decided: measure_cd68 is values > threshold and the threshold is an absolute integer the user types, so on a uint16-derived channel the screen would otherwise light voxels the export will not count.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ParameterSlider gained log=True, and a logarithmic slider refuses a non-positive minimum.
Why it was decided: CD68 p99.9 runs 136 to 58,641 across 13 images while puncta live at 10²–10⁴, so a linear slider puts the whole decision in the bottom ~2% of its travel, and log(0) has no answer to clamp to.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9a's slider is rebuilt when the image loads, and its top is p99.9 rather than the maximum.
Why it was decided: Its ends are two percentiles of the volume so it cannot exist before the data, and one hot voxel would push the useful range back into the bottom of the very slider that exists to escape that.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The number box is authoritative over the slider — a typed value moves the slider without being written back.
Why it was decided: 1000 log positions over three orders of magnitude quantise to ~0.7%, invisible on screen and wrong in a parameters file that is hashed and applied to 700 images.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ParameterSlider._format strips trailing zeros only after a decimal point, and falls back to three significant figures when a non-zero value rounds to zero.
Why it was decided: It rendered 100 as 1 and rendered 9a's smallest-non-zero floor as 0, and every earlier screen used decimals=2 or more so neither defect could fire.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9a's z indicator reads z batch above depth 1 and z slice at depth 1.
Why it was decided: The control's own popup already says so, and a label reading *slice* while showing ten is the quiet contradiction §6e.4 exists to prevent.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9a's two slider-wiring sites were collapsed into one _wire_slider method.
Why it was decided: Two mutations changed nothing because set_channels replaces the constructor's slider, so the constructor's log and its signal connection were dead code the tests were right to ignore.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9a's absent readout is asserted as an exact set of label texts rather than by searching for digits.
Why it was decided: CD68 and CD68 > T both contain digits, so a digit search either misses a readout or fails on a layer name.

What was decided: The test_ui_*.py subset runs after every task and the full suite only when a task edits something outside prestomorph/ui/.
Why it was decided: The user's instruction this session; task 16's soma.py and split.py edits were the only ones to qualify so far, and that run passed at 960.

What was decided: Preserve both continuation logs' section numbering when folding them into PROJECT_LOG.md.
Why it was decided: A dozen documents cite pointers such as A20, B31 and B7 by name, so renumbering into one sequence would break every one of them silently.

What was decided: Retain the folded continuation logs and rationale files as banner-marked originals.
Why it was decided: There is no git and a fold is not reversible.

What was decided: Apply Workstream A's rationale amendments in place at their target sections.
Why it was decided: A-1a at 4.13.7, A-1b at 7 and A-2 at 4.12.1 were written as amend section X line ~N, and every line number still resolved.

What was decided: Apply amendment A-2 as v4, and v5 today rather than as it was written.
Why it was decided: A wrote it as schema v4 on 2026-08-12 and the version moved again on 2026-08-15 when the four channel-role fields landed.

What was decided: Leave the Component 2, 6, 7 and 8 sub-point tables at their 2026-08-11 snapshot.
Why it was decided: Reconciling them is a real audit against PROJECT_LOG.md 23 to 25 rather than a text fix.

What was decided: Correct the split_method claim in all four documents that carried it.
Why it was decided: BUILD_PLAN.md, COMPONENT_STATUS.md, COMPONENT_02_PLAN.md and HANDOFF_WORKSTREAM_A.md all said watershed was kept pending more clumped data with evidence favouring pbc_gudhi 33/43 against 28/43, pointing a reader at the wrong splitter.

What was decided: Mark COMPONENT_03_PLAN.md section 2c as historical rather than a live warning.
Why it was decided: nuclei_coefficient was removed on 2026-08-15 on that section's own analysis, and HANDOFF_B2.md section 6a asked for the marker the same day.

What was decided: Correct HANDOFF_B5.md in place on the two record errors A found.
Why it was decided: B5 section 5 presented NEW-g and NEW-b as live blockers binding the build when both landed 2026-08-12 and PROJECT_LOG_B.md B1 had verified them against the code.

What was decided: Drop module ownership as a gate on the build.
Why it was decided: Ownership was a clobber-prevention device for two accounts writing concurrently, and there is one session now.

What was decided: Allow no backward movement within a pool once every cell in a file is resolved.
Why it was decided: Re-review is re-segmentation under different parameters into a different pool, which section 4a.9's one-pool-per-parameter-set already provides.

What was decided: State in the debris rejection popup that the deletion is permanent.
Why it was decided: Section 9.4e deletes a debris cell's arrays, so unlike a real_cell rejection it cannot be reversed even in principle.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Let single-click decomposition apply to unowned material, not only to the cell being edited.
Why it was decided: Rejecting a debris clump releases every voxel it held into the addable layer, and a severed process inside it is the material worth rescuing.

What was decided: Give triage an undo of exactly one action and rich review a stackable undo.
Why it was decided: Rich review unwinds an in-memory episode before finalisation, so it can run back to the cell's original mask; triage reverses a committed decision and goes back one step.

What was decided: Show only unresolved cells when a file is entered.
Why it was decided: Showing previously confirmed cells would undo the property that a finalised cell never comes back, which is what makes the resume point reconstructable with no stored page state.

What was decided: Delete no measurements when a decision changes, and retract no export.
Why it was decided: A different parameter set is a different pool with a different params_hash and a separate export, so the two describe different settings and neither invalidates the other.

What was decided: Forbid the interface from offering re-review within a pool, and write it into section 7a.
Why it was decided: store.py already carries mark_file_reviewed with a complete flag and merge carries reset_review, so the machinery for the forbidden thing exists and looks like an invitation.

What was decided: Organise the output root as cache, semiauto and batch with a parameter-hash folder under each.
Why it was decided: Each parameter set holds its pool and every export produced from it, so two parameter sets are physically separate trees and two exports of the same images cannot be mistaken for concatenable.

What was decided: Refuse to open review when a queued file's source cannot be resolved, naming the path.
Why it was decided: Both screens read the source now.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Treat an empty review queue as a success state showing the end-of-run popup.
