Why it was decided: Under the no-reopen rule an empty queue means the pool is finished rather than that there is nothing to do right now, and Pool.files already filters completed files out of the queue.

What was decided: Remove edit-survives-a-re-merge as a verification gate and keep 9.4c as a storage test.
Why it was decided: Section 9.4d deletes fragments after the merge that consumed them and makes the resume signal fragment or file record, so no live path reaches a re-merge of a human edit.

What was decided: Close Workstream A's request 2 as moot rather than building the preserve_file fix.
Why it was decided: The same section 9.4d reasoning means a reviewed file is never re-merged, so run_id is never at risk of being overwritten and there is nothing to preserve it against.

What was decided: Split the study root into an image root on the RDM and an output root on scratch.
Why it was decided: A full field is 3.17 GiB, so about 700 files is roughly 2.2 TB against a 300 GB scratch quota.

What was decided: Read genotype and animal from the two directories under the image root, whatever they are called.
Why it was decided: Identity becomes root-relative. parse_metadata cannot know where the study begins, so taking two folders up with one extra level of nesting silently yields a wrong genotype.

What was decided: Retire the _GENOTYPES whitelist and the GenotypeMismatch warning without replacing them.
Why it was decided: A mistyped genotype directory produces an extra genotype with a handful of cells, and export_summary.csv already reports per-genotype blocks, so the typo is visible in output the analyst already reads.

What was decided: Capture genotype and animal on FileRecord at segment time.
Why it was decided: export.py re-parses paths at lines 595 and 686 and holds a path without a root, so under a root-relative contract it cannot tell which directory level is the genotype.

What was decided: Carry genotype, animal, origin and import_order in a single pool schema bump from 1 to 2.
Why it was decided: Three separate bumps would otherwise be needed for one additive change of the same shape reject_note already took.

What was decided: Keep origin stored on FileRecord even though the output path now states it.
Why it was decided: Request 15 exists precisely because deriving a fact from a path broke, so reading origin back out of a directory name would repeat the mistake being fixed in the same section.

What was decided: Remove section, region and image_index from cells.csv.
Why it was decided: metadata.py parses them from filenames and they work on this study's names, but no other lab's convention can be assumed, and a parser that silently succeeds on one and mis-parses another is worse than none.

What was decided: Extend the section, region and image_index removal to images.csv as well as cells.csv.
Why it was decided: IMAGE_IDENTITY carries the same three columns, so removing them from cells.csv alone would leave images.csv with three permanently blank columns, which is the failure the request cites as its own justification. cells.csv goes 51 to 48 and images.csv 32 to 29.

What was decided: Record the column removal in the plan and leave EXPORT_SPEC.md section 5 untouched for now.
Why it was decided: Section 5 is parsed by tests/_spec_columns.py, and test_export.py checks spec against header in both directions plus column order plus section 5.1's stated counts, so any partial change turns the suite red.

What was decided: Give the triage and rich review screens a data provider rather than a Pool.
Why it was decided: Item 7 runs inside a semi-auto session where steps 1 to 7 are entirely in memory and the first write is at item 8, while review --pool reads stored cells.

What was decided: Hold source channels as float32 and save memory by holding fewer channels, not narrower ones.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.6 planned uint16 calling it the source dtype, but the files are float32 with fractional values from 0.0095 to 7169.57 on one plane.

What was decided: Split rich review's nucleus layer into this cell's nucleus, other microglial nuclei, and raw DAPI.
Why it was decided: The splitter ceiling argument that no second nucleus exists covers splitting only, and rich review also adds material, where a nucleus in what is being absorbed is the evidence that another cell is being swallowed.

What was decided: Number the new nucleus layers 2a and 2b rather than renumbering the layer table.
Why it was decided: Other passages refer to layer 3 as the editable layer and layer 4 as everything else, and renumbering would decay those references into plausible wrong targets.

What was decided: Hide the nuclei of confirmed cells along with the cells themselves.
Why it was decided: A finished cell is finished, and showing its nucleus would reintroduce the visual noise that hiding confirmed cells removes.

What was decided: Offer raw DAPI as an optional layer that is off by default.
Why it was decided: A microglial nucleus fused with a neighbour's has its overlap roughly halved, 0.35 to about 0.18 against a 0.25 threshold, so it is stored on no cell.

What was decided: Defer requests 10, 12, 17 and 19 past the build and accept the rename rework.
Why it was decided: The free-while-no-pool-exists urgency protects real data, and the demo pool is disposable, so the constraint does not bind for it.

What was decided: Keep the section 9.4 storage foundation off the demo path.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.5's 2026-08-16 amendment made semi-auto steps 1 to 7 in-memory, so item 7 edits a label volume rather than a pool.

What was decided: Include full rich review in the demo.
Why it was decided: Item 7 is Component 5 at one-image scale and sits inside Component 3's flow between the size cutoff and the pickers, so a semi-auto run reaches it naturally rather than as a separate tool.

What was decided: Keep per-decision checkpointing and do not build the per-image fallback.
Why it was decided: Measured on Bunya scratch at 2.139 ms per decision in the configuration store.py already builds, which is about 43 seconds across a whole 20000-cell review and imperceptible after a keypress.

What was decided: Leave store.py on the rollback journal at synchronous FULL rather than switching to WAL.
Why it was decided: WAL ran on GPFS against the prediction that it would fail, and is 7.5x faster at 0.283 ms against 2.139 ms.

What was decided: Record the 0.12 second RDM channel read as a floor rather than a planning figure.
Why it was decided: 6898 MB/s is achievable on a striped parallel filesystem and is also what a warm page cache looks like, and the file had been opened moments before.

What was decided: Do not repeat the node-local disk comparison.
Why it was decided: TMPDIR resolved to /scratch/temp, so the run measured scratch a second time rather than a local disk.

What was decided: Keep the Bunya benchmark outputs in tuning_runs as artefacts alongside their script.
Why it was decided: This project records measured decisions as re-runnable artefacts rather than re-arguable prose, the same way splitter_clumptest.txt and splitter_ceiling.txt are held.

What was decided: Bundle IBM Plex Sans with the application rather than relying on a system font.
Why it was decided: Qt silently substitutes a missing font and the layout shifts, a failure that would appear only on the cluster.

What was decided: Set the type scale at 16 pt bold title, 11 pt labels and buttons, 10 pt helper, 11 pt errors.
Why it was decided: Only the title is bold anywhere on any screen, so hierarchy comes from size and colour alone.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Use Title Case for titles and buttons and sentence case for labels and helper text.
Why it was decided: Sentence case reads faster in a form, and the split keeps the title distinct without asking bold to do all the work.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Inherit napari's dark background at #262930 for every screen.
Why it was decided: Image screens must be dark: fluorescence on black is universal, napari's canvas defaults to black, and a dim CD68 punctum on a light field reads as noise. napari's own chrome surrounds every image screen, so a different grey would mean two greys in one window.

What was decided: Replace napari's error colour with #f28b82 program-wide.
Why it was decided: napari's dark error is #99121f, which measures 1.7:1 against its own background and is used there to tint icons rather than for text.

What was decided: Replace napari's secondary with #9aa0a6 for muted text.
Why it was decided: napari's #868e93 measures 4.4:1, just below WCAG AA, and with no bold available the muted colour carries hierarchy rather than decoration. #9aa0a6 measures 5.5:1.

What was decided: Set body text to #e2e4e6 rather than napari's #f0f1f2.
Why it was decided: 11.4:1 against 12.9:1 is still far above any threshold, and pure white on dark causes halation across a four-hour review session.

What was decided: Render popups on #2e323a with a 1 px #5a626c border.
Why it was decided: A modal sharing the screen's exact background reads as part of the page.

What was decided: Require that colour is never the only carrier of a state on any screen.
Why it was decided: About 8% of men cannot reliably separate the common pairs.

What was decided: Label item 2, 9b and 8's controls with the parameter names the code carries today rather than the drawn renames.
Why it was decided: Section 6f.10 draws plaque_veto_margin_um and plaque_grow_threshold, which are requests 17 and 12 and ride the PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION 5 to 6 bump that is deferred past the build.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Ship item 9b's seeded and unseeded recolour as a display-only readout.
Why it was decided: The cyan and yellow outlines and the commit table's counts are section 6b's SEED-GROW design, which is Workstream A's request 12 and is deferred past the build as the largest item on either list.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Fix the single-slice preview guard with an optional volume_contrast keyword defaulting to today's computation.
Why it was decided: threshold_channel derives its empty-slice floor from slice_contrast of whatever volume it is handed, so a one-slice preview becomes its own reference and the test reads x < x times 0.05, which can never fire.

What was decided: Build one task at a time and update a resumable handoff document at the end of each.
Why it was decided: The user asked that a session running out of usage be replaceable without losing its place.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build all eleven screens without a visual checkpoint after the first one.
Why it was decided: A checkpoint was proposed after task 10, the first screen carrying a colour picker, a canvas and a commit gate, on the grounds that the other nine inherit its chrome and picker.

What was decided: Derive the build's task list from the component plans rather than from BUILD_PLAN.md.
Why it was decided: BUILD_PLAN.md carries no task decomposition for the interface: Component 3's section is a paragraph ending 'reserved for joint design', Component 5's is the same, and its 'What to do next' reduces the whole build to the single line 'Build Component 3's nine screens'.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build the shared foundation as eight tasks before building any screen.
Why it was decided: Six of the eleven screens carry a colour picker and six carry a parameter slider, so building screens in flow order would have written the swatch grid six times and let it drift six ways.

What was decided: Declare a build backend and an explicit package list in pyproject.toml.
Why it was decided: The file had no build-system table, which pip install -e requires, and setuptools' flat-layout auto-discovery errors outright on a tree with tests, scripts and docs beside the package.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Name the GUI dependency group ui and floor it at napari 0.5.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.7 calls for an optional-dependency group and does not name it or pin it.

What was decided: Have the headless import probe import every module outside ui, not only the entry points.
Why it was decided: The entry-point version asserts the property a Slurm job depends on but does not catch a new headless module with a GUI import at the top, which sits undetected until something imports it.

What was decided: Run the GUI import probe in a clean subprocess rather than in the pytest process.
Why it was decided: pytest auto-registers napari's plugins, confirmed by the run header naming napari 0.7.1, napari-plugin-engine 0.2.1 and npe2 0.8.3, so the suite process already carries napari before any test runs.

What was decided: Assert that the ui boundary scan actually scanned the package before trusting its result.
Why it was decided: A broken glob would make the boundary test pass silently, which is EXPORT_SPEC section 5.1's failure in another form, where 37 columns were written where 72 were advertised.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Resolve relative imports when scanning for forbidden ui imports rather than skipping them.
Why it was decided: A line reading 'from .ui import viewer' is precisely the offence the test exists to catch, and it contains no literal prestomorph.ui anywhere in its text.

What was decided: Import Qt lazily inside theme.py rather than at module scope.
Why it was decided: The palette is strings, so a test that checks a contrast ratio or a title-case rule should not have to find a display. theme.py sits inside ui and is therefore allowed to import Qt, so this is a choice rather than a constraint.

What was decided: Provide a title_case helper that preserves stain names instead of calling str.title.
Why it was decided: str.title turns CD68 into Cd68, so it cannot be used on any string in this interface.

What was decided: Recompute every stated contrast ratio from the hex values rather than transcribing them.
Why it was decided: All twelve figures in section 6e.3 matched to two decimal places, including napari's error at 1.71 to 1 and its secondary at 4.37 to 1.

What was decided: Raise rather than warn when the bundled typeface is missing.
Why it was decided: Section 6e.1's whole argument is that Qt substitutes a missing font silently and the layout shifts, a failure that appears only on the cluster.

What was decided: Keep the data palette in its own module, separate from the chrome.
Why it was decided: theme.py is section 6e, the chrome; palette.py is section 6f and its descendants, being the ten data colours, the channel convention, the per-channel alphas, the label ring and its warm and cool halves, and the size ramp.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Dim the list rows below item 6's cutoff rather than hiding them.
Why it was decided: The trough has to be visible by eye, because judging where the size cutoff falls is what the screen exists to support.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Hold the commit staleness flag as widget state rather than reading Qt visibility back.
Why it was decided: Qt reports a child of a window that has never been shown as not visible regardless of setVisible being true, so is_stale answered false for every screen still being assembled, and that flag is the gate stopping a user continuing from a view the commit no longer matches.

What was decided: Keep the recording viewer beside the Protocol in viewer.py rather than in the tests.
Why it was decided: It is what makes the Protocol demonstrably satisfiable, it contains no napari, and the screens need it.

What was decided: Implement the mask outline as one function that projects and then outlines at every depth.
Why it was decided: Section 6f.6 gives two paths, slicing a pre-outlined volume at depth 1 and projecting before outlining above it, but the two agree exactly at depth 1, so the shortcut is an optimisation rather than a different answer.

What was decided: Draw the mask outline inside the mask rather than outside it.
Why it was decided: Outside would overstate the mask by the line's own thickness at exactly the boundary being judged, and item 2's whole question is whether the veto stops short of a real nucleus.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Leave build_cell_mask without the volume_contrast passthrough.
Why it was decided: It calls threshold_channel internally and would hit the identical single-slice trap, but no screen previews through it: section 4 specifies the preview as threshold_channel on one slice, and build_cell_mask runs at commit on the whole volume.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Round floats in the preview cache key to nine decimal places.
Why it was decided: A slider reporting 0.1 and 0.10000000000000001 on two passes would otherwise miss its own entry, and a missed key serves a wrong preview, which is the one failure a preview cannot have because the user is deciding a parameter by looking at it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make the in-memory slice preview cache least-recently-used and bound it at 32 entries.
Why it was decided: The reason a preview is cached at all is that stepping back is free, which is precisely what a first-in first-out policy would evict first.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give only item 4 a Back button, returning to item 3.
Why it was decided: Section 3a's diagram of 2026-08-13 draws loop-backs from steps 5 and 6 to step 4 and calls steps 4 to 6 freely re-enterable, but section 4's per-screen sections of 2026-08-17 give items 5 and 6 no BACK at all, item 6 because every volume on it is a threshold-2 volume so going back would invalidate the whole screen, and item 3 CONTINUE only.

What was decided: Leave section 3a's flow diagram unmarked rather than editing it to match the built flow.
Why it was decided: The diagram still reads as current and its re-enterability claim is repeated in three other places, so it wants a superseded marker, but that is a documentation edit and the user's standing rule is that writing is their call.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Value the flow's step enum by the screen title the user sees rather than by item number.
Why it was decided: Item numbers are a planning device and never appear in the interface; nobody using the tool has seen item 4, they saw Microglial Nuclei Detection at the top of a screen.

What was decided: Offer unused as a channel role so an absent channel can be recorded.
Why it was decided: A two-channel study is real, and a cd68_channel of None is what says the study has no CD68.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Assert the intake screen's channel roles through the real parameters writer and reader.
Why it was decided: The failure being prevented happens one command later, when segment exits 4 on a contradiction between the roles flag and the file, so a test stopping at the screen's own dictionary would not have covered it.

What was decided: Refuse a file that is not exactly two folders under the image root rather than guessing its identity.
Why it was decided: Genotype and animal come from the path, and a wrong genotype is silent: every number downstream is plausible and only the comparison is wrong.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build the five frame types as their own module rather than inline on each screen.
Why it was decided: Frame C alone serves items 2, 4, 9a, 9b and rich review, which is five screens, so building it inline would have given the 260 by stretch by 280 column widths five chances to drift apart.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Compute item 2's readout as a share of DAPI intensity rather than of voxels.
Why it was decided: It matches veto_plaque_signal's own second return value, which is where the number comes from in the real flow rather than being recomputed on the screen.

What was decided: Assert rendered widget properties under an offscreen Qt platform rather than the stylesheet text.
Why it was decided: Qt applies a stylesheet it cannot parse by doing nothing at all, with no exception and no warning, so asserting that the stylesheet string contains the right hex values is not evidence that anything is styled.

What was decided: Leave the IBM Plex Sans files out of the repository pending the user's approval to fetch them.
Why it was decided: Section 6e.1 says bundled and budgets about 300 KB, but the files are not on the machine, not in site-packages and not in the project.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Leave cli.py's interactive and review stubs in place until the screens behind them work.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.7 calls this one of the last steps of Component 3 rather than one of the first: replacing them early would make interactive open an empty window, which is strictly worse than an honest error message naming the component that is missing.

What was decided: Draw item 9b's plaque layer as 6E10 above plaque_threshold, matching the pipeline rather than the drawn greater-or-equal.
Why it was decided: markers._plaque_sizes computes mask = channel > threshold, and every plaque column in plaques.csv and images.csv reaches CSV through it via measure_plaque_burden.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build item 9b's plaque mask as five additive image layers under three picker rows rather than one Labels layer.
Why it was decided: Section 6l.8 draws three swatch rows and three checkboxes while the mask is drawn in three states, so plaque is one concept driving three layers, which is item 2's shape where a single DAPI checkbox drives two.

What was decided: Keep item 9b's seeded cyan and unseeded yellow out of the colour picker and let the swatch recolour only the provisional outline.
Why it was decided: Section 6l.4's pair is measured at 96.6 apart for a dichromat and 73.3 and 74.9 clear of the magenta beneath, and it carries the commit gate's second signal, so a user recolouring it could destroy the gate.

What was decided: Number unseeded 2 and seeded 1 so the z-batch max projection breaks ties toward unseeded.
Why it was decided: The batch view is a max over the slab, so where two components overlap in projection the larger id wins.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Label item 9b's plaque components without the volume floor so min_plaque_volume_um3 stays live after the commit.
Why it was decided: The floor is applied by class_lookup against volumes computed once, so typing a smaller number brings objects back without re-labelling, which is the only reason the control moved to this screen on 2026-08-17.

What was decided: Return ndimage.label's output uncast, since it is already int32.
Why it was decided: An astype(np.int32) that reads as a safety net is a full-volume copy, which is 848 MB at a production width of 2304 by 2304 by 40.

What was decided: Take item 9b's live outline from the already projected plane rather than from a whole-volume grow mask.
Why it was decided: A max over z followed by the threshold is the same set as the threshold followed by any over z, so this is an identity rather than an approximation, and a test asserts it against outline_of_batch at three depths.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Add update_current_row to AccumulatingTable rather than appending a row when item 9b's floor moves.
Why it was decided: Section 6l.7 requires the floor to update the live row only, so earlier rows keep the floor they were taken at and two rows at different floors can never be read as comparable.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Return item 9b's floor box to disabled whenever the components are discarded, not only before the first commit.
Why it was decided: Item 5 clears its is_committed flag when a parameter moves and its z-depth box greys out again; moving the grow threshold throws the components away, so the floor has nothing left to filter.

What was decided: Name item 9b's module screen_plaque.py with class PlaqueThresholdScreen rather than screen_6e10.py.
Why it was decided: The code already calls this screen plaque throughout, in Step.PLAQUE, plaque_threshold, min_plaque_volume_um3 and the plaque layer itself; only the title the user sees is named by channel.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Import slider_range, batch_projection and z_label from screen_cd68 rather than moving them into preview.py.
Why it was decided: Task 13 recorded the rule that two callers do not justify the churn mid-build and three would.

What was decided: Set item 9b's seed mask fill to the derived-mask alpha of 1.0 although that constant is justified for outlines.
Why it was decided: Section 6l.6's 103.4 against the magenta fill is the separation of spring green at full strength, so a weight below 1.0 would spend part of the one margin that chose the colour.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Derive item 9b's LAYERS table from CONCEPTS and COMMITTED_COLOURS rather than typing it out.
Why it was decided: A mutation flipping the seed mask's arrival state in a hand-written LAYERS changed nothing and all 66 tests stayed green, because LAYERS was read in exactly one place and only for its colour column, while the arrival state and alpha that reach a user came from CONCEPTS.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Ship item 9b's commit gate as a disabled Continue with the exclamation, matching the four screens already built, rather than adding the specified popup to 9b alone.
Why it was decided: COMPONENT_03_PLAN section 4 item 2's amendment of 2026-08-17 specifies a Not-committed popup for every screen with a COMMIT, and it is built on none of the five.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Build item 8 with no frame, no LAYERS tuple and no viewer, following item 1's stacked form.
Why it was decided: Section 6d excluded item 8 from the colour session on its own words, that item 8 has no viewer, so it takes section 6e's chrome unchanged.

What was decided: Key the semi-auto pool on a Phase A hash over 25 of SegmentationParams' 29 fields rather than on the full params_hash.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.9. cd68_threshold and plaque_threshold are None until item 9, so keying the pool on the full hash would move the whole session's cells into a different, empty pool at the last act before saving: the pickers would invalidate the pool they were picked from. min_spur_um would strand a cell set for a skeleton-pruning length that touches no mask, at 200 to 500 s of Cellpose per image to refill.

What was decided: Derive the Phase A field list by subtracting a hand-kept Phase C list rather than listing the Phase A fields by hand.
Why it was decided: A hand-listed subset rots silently: omit a field and changing it no longer moves the pool key, so cells made differently land in the same pool and nothing errors.

What was decided: Keep soma_erode_um in the Phase A pool key despite the dataclass grouping it with the measurement knobs.
Why it was decided: segment_image calls find_soma with erode_um to compute soma_centroid on every stored cell record, so it is read in both phases and changing it changes stored Phase A output.

What was decided: Refuse an unrecognised origin in pool_dir_name rather than accepting it into a path.
Why it was decided: A typo producing pool_semi_auto_ would be a silently separate pool, which is the failure section 4a.3's enforcement exists to prevent. run_id cannot carry the category because it is free text: --run-id experiment2 produces a batch pool whose records say nothing about being batch.

What was decided: Write the session's cells through PoolWriter and merge_fragments, and merge semi-auto's own fragment in process.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.5 requires the derivation to use batch's own path, because cli.py's standing warning is that a second code path for the same job is the most likely way the batch and interactive routes would silently diverge.

What was decided: Write item 8's parameters file first and check the name collision before either write.
Why it was decided: A collision discovered after the cells were written would leave the session half committed, with a pool holding cells whose params_hash names a file the user is then being told to rename.

What was decided: Carry the session's cells, image shape and nucleus edit count as three new fields on Session.
Why it was decided: Item 8 needs all three and no earlier screen carried any of them.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Record item 4's hand-edit count onto the session at CONTINUE rather than at commit.
Why it was decided: Section 6a requires item 8 to say plainly that manual edits stay with this image, and that sentence names a number which exists nowhere else, because nucleus edits are per-image overrides that never reach the parameters file.

What was decided: Print an unset parameter as not set in item 8's read-only block rather than as a blank.
Why it was decided: mask_coefficient, cd68_threshold and plaque_threshold are all legitimately None before their screens run, and a blank row reads as the value is zero on a screen whose whole job is showing what is about to be written.

What was decided: Show fifteen parameters read-only in seven groups on item 8 and hide thirteen others entirely.
Why it was decided: Section 4 item 8's third class is what keeps the screen a decision point rather than a parameter dump, so the block is exactly the set of choices this session made.

What was decided: Permit cli.py alone to import ui, and only from inside a function, rather than relaxing the boundary rule.
Why it was decided: The source scan walks every import node, so even a lazy import inside a function was caught, and cli.py cannot open the interface it documents without crossing.

What was decided: Split segment_image into a derivation and a write, with a null pool root returning the cells unwritten.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.5 requires the derivation to be batch's own code, and its amendment of 2026-08-16 requires steps 1 to 7 to hold the label volume in memory; both cannot be true while computing and writing are one function.

What was decided: Yield the cell payloads from a generator so batch still crops one cell at a time.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.5's memory line is that the cost is one array, not sixty.

What was decided: Compose item 7's triage and rich review into one flow step in the driver rather than inside either screen.
Why it was decided: Triage emits cell_entered, the editor emits resolved, and neither screen knows the other exists.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put the flow's heavy steps behind a Compute Protocol with a substitutable implementation.
Why it was decided: Cellpose takes 200 to 500 s and a production field is 3.17 GiB, so a test driving ten screens through the real functions would be neither fast nor headless.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make the driver's show_step move the flow's position as well as the widget.
Why it was decided: Every screen holds the same Flow and asks it is_stale and can_continue, which are answered for flow.step, so a driver that swapped the widget without moving the flow would show item 2 while its exclamation and disabled Continue reported on item 1.

What was decided: Rewrite the review stub's message to name the pool-backed route rather than five open layout questions.
Why it was decided: It said Component 5 was reserved for joint design with the user and five layout questions open, which stopped being true when task 16 built both screens.

What was decided: Assert that the pipeline derives the cell border flags rather than only that they round-trip.
Why it was decided: A mutation forcing touches_xy_border to False on every cell changed nothing.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Fix the four wiring defects the first ten-screen walk exposed.
Why it was decided: The intake screen's own sync clears the session at construction, so an image path given on the command line never survived; show_step did not move flow.step, so every screen's gate would have reported on the wrong step; item 8 has no continue_requested because it is the last screen, and the driver required one on every screen; and a screen reached with no channels loaded handed None to a slider.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Remove the "max projection thumbnails" label from item 1.
Why it was decided: Intake is the one screen with no viewer, so the label promised something that was never built.

What was decided: Channel dropdowns read stain-first with the role in brackets — Iba1 (cell), CD68 (lysosomal marker).
Why it was decided: A channel is identified by its stain at the microscope, and a swapped role is silent — plausible numbers, never an error.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The dropdown label is display-only; the parameters file still records the bare role.
Why it was decided: Those strings become <role>_channel and are parsed again by segment --roles, so a label reaching the file would exit 4 one command later.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2 draws DAPI as one layer with a toggleable vetoed DAPI overlay.
Why it was decided: DAPI removed and vetoed DAPI were the same array drawn twice, so the split spent a layer and a colour saying what one toggle says.

What was decided: PipelineCompute.veto returns both the raw and the dilated mask.
Why it was decided: Detection re-applies the dilation itself, so the downstream copy must stay undilated while the screen must draw the dilated one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Add per-channel min/max display-range boxes to item 1.
Why it was decided: The user sets the range in Fiji and types it in, and the two scales were confirmed identical to the last decimal on DAPI slice 1.

What was decided: Display ranges are not written to the parameters file.
Why it was decided: They change nothing the pipeline computes, and entering the hashed block would fork the pool directory on a brightness change.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Blank min/max falls back to a 0.1–99.9 percentile stretch.
Why it was decided: A blank box must never mean a black screen, and the percentile is what items 3, 5, 9a and 9b already use.

What was decided: Apply contrast limits on items 2, 4 and 7b.
Why it was decided: They passed none at all, so one hot voxel 54× the real signal rendered 6E10 at under 2% of the brightness ramp.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Strip napari's three default canvas gestures at viewer construction.
Why it was decided: double_click_to_zoom fired on every nucleus edit, and Windows delivers a trackpad pinch as the Ctrl+scroll dims_scroll listens for.

What was decided: Every layer that is not a label projects over the z-batch.
Why it was decided: Only the derived masks projected, so the box moved an outline across a picture frozen on one slice.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4 becomes view-only above z-batch depth 1.
Why it was decided: A projection collapses slices, so a click names a y and an x and no z, while every edit on that screen is a 3D operation.

What was decided: MUTED_LABEL_ALPHA 0.6 → 0.25.
Why it was decided: 0.6 did not read as a difference on real data, and which individual *rejected* nucleus is which is not a judgement this screen asks.

What was decided: Negative plaque_dilate_um erodes the veto toward the plaque core.
Why it was decided: Mean DAPI rises 4.7× from the rim of the 6E10 mask to 1–2 µm inside it while 6E10 itself stays flat.

What was decided: Items 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 each gained a parameters() method and a _sync that writes it onto session.chosen.
Why it was decided: Only items 9a and 9b had ever written there, so every commit ran at SegmentationParams' defaults and the parameters file recorded defaults.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The number parser lives once, in semiauto.parsed_numbers, rather than in each screen.
Why it was decided: Five copies of a parser drift five ways — the same argument that produced widgets.py.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A half-typed box contributes nothing to session.chosen rather than a zero.
Why it was decided: float("") raises and a box mid-edit is not a choice, so a defaulting branch would commit at a value the screen is not showing.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Items 2, 4 and 5's COMMITs run through SemiAutoApp.run_commit, while items 3 and 9b own theirs.
Why it was decided: The three need ImageSource, detect_nuclei and build_cell_mask, and a screen importing those puts a cellpose import inside a widget.

What was decided: PipelineCompute.detect was rewritten to the call pipeline.py:542 makes, with the veto applied inside detect_nuclei.
Why it was decided: It had never been called from anywhere and had drifted: detect_nuclei takes diameter_px, not diameter_um — an unexpected keyword and a missing required argument.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Detection reuses item 3's committed mask instead of rebuilding it.
Why it was decided: build_cell_mask over the whole stack is ~59 s at 40 × 2304 × 2304, and the session was already holding the result.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: CommitButton.set_working forces a repaint, scoped to ExcludeUserInputEvents, before returning.
Why it was decided: The work is synchronous, so between setting the line and blocking the event loop never runs and no paint event is delivered — the line had never once appeared.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: set_detection ends with a draw.
Why it was decided: The commit computed 35 nuclei and drew none of them; the readout moved to microglial: 5 of 35 and the canvas did not change.

What was decided: n_detected counts the label ids actually present rather than the fractions array's size.
Why it was decided: membership_fractions returns one entry per id up to the largest, so deleting any but the highest id left the count unchanged.

What was decided: Item 4 does not show the DAPI at native resolution with the labels scaled, as §4a.1 describes; prepare block-averages both channels instead.
Why it was decided: A production field is 849 MB per float32 channel at native against 212 MB downsampled, and item 4 shows two of them.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: viewer.show_image and show_labels gained an optional scale, defaulting to None.
Why it was decided: It keeps §4a.1's own arrangement one line away and stops a working-resolution layer landing over the top-left quarter of the field.

What was decided: The working-resolution factor is read off the two arrays rather than passed in, and rounded to an integer.
Why it was decided: A downsample carried alongside can disagree with the data, and downsample_xy truncates the last partial block so the shape ratio is not the mapping.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Flow.commit invalidates every commit downstream of it, while invalidate does not cascade.
Why it was decided: Item 4 is the only screen with a Back button, so a re-committed item 3 left item 4's membership answering for a mask that had just been replaced.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: An arriving screen re-reads its own gate, except item 1.
Why it was decided: _sync runs only when that screen's own controls move, and item 1's _sync is a write that clears roots and roles the session was given from elsewhere.

What was decided: The shakeout's stand-in became a subclass of PipelineCompute, overriding only load and detect.
Why it was decided: Three faults came out of the gap in one afternoon: a missing protocol method, the wrong coordinate frame, and a skipped speck floor.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The shakeout presses COMMIT on all five commit screens and photographs the committed state beside the arrival state.
Why it was decided: The committed state is most of what those screens exist to show, and the walk had only ever photographed arrival.

What was decided: The synthetic Iba1 clips each Gaussian at 0.6 of its amplitude, and the synthetic derive applies speck_floor_um3.
Why it was decided: Unclipped tails put the threshold inside a background ramp, so every slice tripped max_foreground_fraction and item 3 committed 0.0000% foreground.

What was decided: The mutation runner refuses to start unless it owns every file any mutation names.
Why it was decided: One entry mutated viewer.py, which was not in FILES, so nothing restored it and the md5 check at the end never looked at it.

What was decided: The pristine snapshot is deleted whenever the code legitimately changes mid-task.
Why it was decided: The runner restores at the top of every invocation, so an edit made after the snapshot is silently reverted by the next call — which happened once.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The gestures reach the screens through ViewerPort rather than through napari.
Why it was decided: It is what lets RecordingViewer fire a click, so the editing paths are testable in a suite with no display.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Shift-Left and Shift-Right are bound beside the plain arrows on all six screens that have a z.
Why it was decided: napari keys on the whole combination, so with SHIFT held a binding on Left alone never fires — and a clump's daughters sit on different slices.

What was decided: A hand-added nucleus is a seed the program grows, not PrestoCell's fixed block of side nucleus_diameter / 2.
Why it was decided: The user's rule, and it is the contract the split already had: markers place seeds and the watershed finds the parts.

What was decided: nucleus_min_volume_voxels is not applied to a hand-placed seed.
Why it was decided: It is the detector's floor and the seed is the user overriding the detector, so a real 75-voxel nucleus was being replaced by a fabricated 1550-voxel ball.

What was decided: A seed that lands on nothing still adds a nucleus, as a ball of the expected diameter.
Why it was decided: Refusing silently leaves a double-click that sometimes does nothing, with no way to tell that case from a missed click.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's edits are replayed from the record onto the committed labels rather than applied in place.
Why it was decided: OperationRecord's claim that undo and the persisted history cannot disagree is true only if the picture is a function of the record.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The z contract moved into ui/gestures.py, item 2 gained a z, and items 9a and 9b gained an absolute set_z.
Why it was decided: Five screens carried five copies of the rule and item 2 carried none, and napari's slider reports a slice rather than a step.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The Qt keyPressEvent handlers are kept alongside the napari bindings.
Why it was decided: They are what answers while the *controls* have focus, which is where the keyboard is before the first click on the image.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: NapariViewer tracks the KeyBinding objects taken from the keymap's difference across a bind.
Why it was decided: viewer.keymap is keyed by objects rather than the string passed, so keymap.pop("u") removed nothing and every screen's bindings would have leaked into the next.

What was decided: bind_key detects a generator callback and binds press and release.
Why it was decided: napari decides that from inspect.isgeneratorfunction on the function it is handed, so a lambda wrapper silently makes SHIFT press-only.

What was decided: show_points was added to the port so the split markers are drawn and numbered.
Why it was decided: SplitMarkers had existed since task 12 with nothing drawing it, and an N-way split placed blind cannot show that one marker does nothing.

What was decided: Rich review converts the crop offset once, where a split marker is captured.
Why it was decided: A region id is the same number in either frame, but a marker is a position and CellEditor.split works on the full volume.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A double-click on the background in rich review does not reach the editor.
Why it was decided: double_click_action("this cell") is remove, so remove(0) would make a miss an undoable step.

What was decided: The result[target] = 0 before a split was removed as dead code.
Why it was decided: split_by_watershed assigns every voxel of the object to exactly one marker, so each is overwritten anyway — a mutation deleting the line could not be made to fail.

What was decided: Item 4 calls gestures.bind_z_stepping instead of keeping its own copy of the arrow and dims bindings.
Why it was decided: Three mutations on the shared contract came back green because item 4 was obeying a duplicate of it.

What was decided: Whether item 4's hand edits should reach the pipeline was flagged for the user rather than decided.
Why it was decided: Making them count needs a new argument on a Phase A function and yields a run segment --params cannot reproduce, which is a judgement about what the numbers are for.

What was decided: The plaque veto margin becomes a true sphere in microns, via distance_transform_edt(sampling=voxel_size_um).
Why it was decided: The one-slice-thick element reached its stated distance in xy and zero in z, so plaque DAPI on the neighbouring slice survived, was detected as a nucleus, and joined the microglial set whenever membership_threshold was lowered.

What was decided: The margin's radius carries a one-voxel floor IN PLANE ONLY, with no z floor.
Why it was decided: Forcing 0.108 µm to reach a slice 0.6 µm away would reintroduce the exact anisotropy error the sphere was adopted to remove.

What was decided: A 0.5 µm margin not reaching the next slice is reaffirmed as correct rather than a rounding failure.
Why it was decided: The next slice centre is 0.6 µm away at this study's spacing, and a sphere of radius 0.5 does not touch a point at 0.6.

What was decided: The margin's sign convention is reaffirmed unchanged — positive dilates, negative erodes toward the dense core.
Why it was decided: Erosion is what the screen's own name asks for, and the measured DAPI gradient inside the mask rises 4.7x from rim to core.

What was decided: The margin is NOT split into separate z, y and x controls.
Why it was decided: Spherical couples z reach to xy reach, but the coupling only matters if a real nucleus is seen being eaten, and it has not been.

What was decided: The distance transform's ~1.7 GB float64 on a full field is accepted rather than optimised.
Why it was decided: The program is written for a cluster, so the bounding-box refinement buys nothing that is needed now.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's DAPI -veto layer must be handed DAPI with the veto subtracted.
Why it was decided: It was passing session.channels["nuclei"] raw, so the layer named for a subtraction never performed one on the screen where the veto is judged.

What was decided: That subtraction happens at full resolution and is downsampled afterwards, never the reverse.
Why it was decided: downsample_xy block-averages, so averaging first would smear vetoed intensity into surviving neighbours and leave a ghost exactly where the veto bit.

What was decided: The twelve-hue label ring is walked in an interleaved order — 0, 6, 3, 9, … — rather than sequentially.
Why it was decided: ndimage.label numbers in raster-scan order, so spatially adjacent objects take consecutive ids and were being handed the closest hues the ring has.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A Step by batch checkbox switches LEFT/RIGHT between a rolling window and fixed batches.
Why it was decided: Both windowings already existed — outline_of_batch rolling, ProjectionCache fixed and used by nothing — and neither had ever been chosen.

What was decided: Rolling stays the default and the toggle is disabled at depth 1.
Why it was decided: Rolling cannot have the straddling artefact ProjectionCache's own docstring records, and at depth 1 both modes show the same slice, so the control would do nothing.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The z indicator reads the window range — z batch (20-29/40) — instead of a single index.
Why it was decided: With two modes selectable the same index names different slices in each, so a lone number stops being merely vague and becomes wrong.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Stepping stops where the window last fills, at 31-40/40 on a 40-slice stack.
Why it was decided: Past that point the projection thins to nine slices and fewer while the label would still claim a full batch.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The intake screen's voxel-size handling is left as it is.
Why it was decided: There is no metadata autofill to accept — only a static placeholder — so the fix would have been to read OME metadata, which is a larger change than the one raised.

What was decided: Item 3's objects are NOT recoloured by per-slice 2D connected components.
Why it was decided: They already take a colour per 3D object id, and a 2D labelling would show a dozen colours while the readout said three.

What was decided: The spherical margin gets its own tests in test_nuclei.py rather than relying on the existing suite.
Why it was decided: Replacing the mechanism turned nothing red, because no test had ever asserted the xy-only behaviour it removed.

What was decided: Import torch before Qt at the interactive entry point.
Why it was decided: Measured on this machine: importing qtpy.QtWidgets and then torch raises OSError WinError 1114 loading c10.dll, while the reverse order is fine.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Carry item 7's review decisions to the pool at the commit rather than leaving every cell a candidate.
Why it was decided: PoolWriter writes every cell CANDIDATE and pending_measurement takes only CONFIRMED unless include-unreviewed is passed, so a session that reviewed every cell and saved produced measured 0 cells across 0 images from the exact command the SAVED popup prints, and an export of 6 cells with no measurements at all.

What was decided: Leave a cell with no review decision as a candidate rather than confirming it by default.
Why it was decided: That is the honest record of a session where review was skipped, and measure --include-unreviewed still stamps every such row reviewed equals false, so the distinction survives to the spreadsheet.

What was decided: Record triage's accepts from its own resolved flags, using setdefault so a rejection is never overwritten.
Why it was decided: accept_this_screen and accept_rest_of_file are a pure status flip that sets resolved and emits a signal, so a reviewer who accepts three screens and then the file would otherwise leave no decision behind at all. setdefault keeps a rich-review rejection intact when triage later clears the rest of the file.

What was decided: Pass item 1's confirmed voxel size into the flow's image read.
Why it was decided: ImageSource refuses a file that records no voxel size unless it is given one, and item 1 asks for it and confirms it either way precisely because files can lack one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Release the session's channels before the derivation runs.
Why it was decided: segment_image opens the file and reads its own channels, so the session's copies are pure duplication through the one call that peaks highest, with the downsampled stack, threshold mask, closed mask, label volumes and Cellpose all live at once.

What was decided: Delete the demo pool after the end-to-end run and verify its absence rather than leaving it.
Why it was decided: Section 2's standing constraint: both schema bumps, pool 1 to 2 and params 5 to 6, are free only while no pool exists, and a leftover demo pool becomes the first real pool by accident.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Verify the end-to-end run by pasting the two commands exactly as the SAVED popup prints them.
Why it was decided: That is what makes item 8's completion state tested rather than merely drawn, params-hash included.

What was decided: Change no colour and hand the three soft pairs to the user rendered on a real field.
Why it was decided: The user's instruction was to prepare it and not decide alone.

What was decided: Report that CD68 positive renders as ffff37 and the seed mask as c9ffff without changing either colour.
Why it was decided: A derived layer sits by construction where its own channel is brightest, and section 6f.3 makes every layer add, so the reviewer sees the sum rather than the swatch.

What was decided: Deliver task 22 as a published artifact rather than as files in the repository.
Why it was decided: The whole task is looking at images, which terminal output cannot carry, and the panels are dressed in the program's own chrome and typeface so they are seen in the surroundings they will appear in.

What was decided: Run no mutation pass for task 22, because it shipped no behaviour.
Why it was decided: No module changed, no test changed and the suite was untouched at 706 UI tests and 1194 in full.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep the commit gate silent, with a disabled Continue and the exclamation beside Commit, and build no Not-committed popup.
Why it was decided: Reverses the decision of 2026-08-17 to raise a popup naming the changed control on every screen with a COMMIT.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Mark the plan's Not-committed popup amendment superseded in place rather than deleting it.
Why it was decided: Section 4 item 2 states the rule by property, every screen with a COMMIT, so an unmarked amendment would be rediscovered later as unbuilt work.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep all three soft colour pairs as they are and rely on the picker and the translucency slider.
Why it was decided: The user's decision after seeing the panels, closing flag 4: the colour combos are fine, the user can play around with transparency and also change colours if they want to.

What was decided: Keep the additive-sum finding recorded at flag 4 after the flag was closed.
Why it was decided: The mechanism is real and will resurface the next time a derived layer is given a colour, so closing the decision does not retire the explanation.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Hand the build to a session 5 task loop of five tasks rather than closing it as finished.
Why it was decided: The pipeline half is proven end to end on two real images, but the interface has never been shown and no screen has ever rendered.

What was decided: End each of the interface tasks by opening the application and looking at it rather than by tests alone.
Why it was decided: Tasks 1 to 22 were verified by tests and tasks 23 to 26 cannot be, because a test asserting that a widget was re-parented proves nothing about whether an image appeared.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move one napari canvas between the screens rather than giving each screen its own viewer.
Why it was decided: SemiAutoApp.place_canvas re-parents NapariViewer.widget() into the arriving screen's canvas host and every other host stands empty.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Declare each screen's panel arrangement as data on the screen and apply it from the driver.
Why it was decided: viewer.CanvasLayout on each screen class, with place_canvas applying set_ndisplay then set_grid then reset_view.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Default the napari viewer to show False and take its widget from the private _qt_viewer.
Why it was decided: Verified against napari 0.7.1's own qt_viewer.py rather than transcribed: QtViewer is a QSplitter holding canvas.native and QtDims and nothing else, so taking it takes the picture and the z slider and leaves the layer list, layer controls and menus behind, which is right because section 4 gives every screen its own Colours and Layers blocks.

What was decided: Reduce the two-pane thumbnail to its mask pane when a tile is constructed rather than when it paints.
Why it was decided: pipeline._thumbnail stores two stacked max projections as one (2, H, W) array and ReviewCell.thumbnail is specified as the mask-only projection, with nothing converting between them, so the tile unpacked a 3D shape into height and width and raised inside paintEvent, where Qt turns a traceback into a warning and paints an empty tile.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Clear the viewer on every screen arrival.
Why it was decided: Every screen was inheriting every earlier screen's layers. napari assigns a grid panel from layers.index(layer), so items 3, 5 and 6's arrangements were computed over a pile of other screens' layers, and a layer name can change kind between screens: item 6 draws the size ramp as a Labels layer called cells and item 9a draws the confirmed cell set as an image called cells, so show_image found the labels layer still sitting there and item 9a never opened, reporting Unable to interpret as labels colormap.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Scroll the selection list between a floor and a ceiling, and clamp the window to the available display.
Why it was decided: SelectionList built one QLabel per cell with nothing to scroll in, and one measured field holds 537 objects, so the window was photographed 2470 px tall on a resize to 1400 by 900, carrying item 6's lower panel and its Detail header off the screen entirely.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Refit the camera on every arrival and paint the radio buttons from the chrome palette.
Why it was decided: napari fits the camera when the first layer lands in an empty viewer and never again, but this canvas moves between panels of different sizes and grids, so item 4 was photographed with its DAPI occupying the middle 45% of a black panel. reset_view runs after the grid and ndisplay, because those are what change the viewbox it is fitted to.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Open the real application on a real display from a committed shakeout script and photograph every screen.
Why it was decided: scripts/gui_shakeout.py walks all ten screens plus rich review and never calls napari.run(), pumping the loop by hand so it always terminates.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Have every commit screen write its typed values onto the session.
Why it was decided: session.chosen is what screen_save.session_params serialises and what PipelineCompute reads, and only items 9a and 9b ever wrote to it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Answer the three pipeline-backed commits in the driver rather than inside the screens.
Why it was decided: Items 3 and 9b compute with pure functions from their own modules and own their commits, while items 2, 4 and 5 need ImageSource, detect_nuclei and build_cell_mask.

What was decided: Rewrite PipelineCompute.detect to the call the pipeline actually makes.
Why it was decided: It was never called from anywhere and it had drifted: detect_nuclei takes diameter_px and not diameter_um, which is an unexpected keyword and a missing required argument at once, and it returned the NucleiResult where the caller wanted its labels.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Force the progress line to paint before a commit's work begins, scoped to exclude user input.
Why it was decided: Every commit screen set the working line before its work and cleared it after, and not one ever appeared on screen, because the work is synchronous so between the two calls the event loop never runs and no paint event is delivered.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: End item 4's set_detection with a draw.
Why it was decided: It computed the membership fractions and refreshed the readout and nothing redrew the canvas, so item 4 computed 35 nuclei and drew none of them: the readout went from microglial 0 of 0 to 5 of 35, the exclamation cleared and Continue enabled, while the picture stayed the same DAPI with nucleus labels ticked over an empty layer.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Press COMMIT on all five commit screens in the shakeout and photograph the committed state.
Why it was decided: The walk stopped at arrival and photographed every screen in the state it opens in, and until this task the button ran no work to photograph.

What was decided: Make the synthetic compute a subclass of the real one, overriding only the image read and the detector.
Why it was decided: As a separate class it had drifted three ways in one task: measurement_mask was missing entirely so item 5's COMMIT raised AttributeError the first time anything pressed it; detect answered at native resolution while the real one answers at segmentation resolution; and derive skipped speck_floor_um3, so item 6 listed 45 volumes of which 42 rounded to 0 um3 and item 7 drew 42 tiles that were one white pixel stretched over the tile.

What was decided: Clip each synthetic Gaussian at 0.6 of its amplitude.
Why it was decided: Uniform noise plus unclipped Gaussians gave every blob a tail across the whole field, so the background was a ramp rather than a floor; threshold_channel at coefficient 0.18 put its cut inside that ramp, every slice came back over max_foreground_fraction 0.40, and the empty-slice guard suppressed the lot at 0.0000% foreground on every slice.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Cascade a commit's invalidation to every step downstream of it, and never cascade invalidate.
Why it was decided: Item 4 is the only screen with a Back button and it goes to item 3, so this path is a user's to walk: commit the 200 to 500 s detection, go Back, move cell_coefficient, COMMIT item 3 again, Continue.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Re-read a screen's gate when it arrives, except item 1 whose sync writes rather than reads.
Why it was decided: Each screen keeps Continue and the red exclamation in step with Flow through its own sync, which runs when one of that screen's controls moves, so without an arrival call the commit-cascade fix would never have reached the glass.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Hand item 4 both channels at segmentation resolution rather than mixing native and working frames.
Why it was decided: The plan decided on 2026-08-13 that nucleus labels are displayed and edited at working resolution while the DAPI image is shown at native with the labels carrying a scale of 1, 2, 2. napari uploads image layers to the GPU and a production field is 2304 by 2304 by 40, which is 849 MB per float32 channel at native against 212 MB downsampled, and item 4 shows two.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Reuse item 3's committed mask for detection rather than rebuilding it.
Why it was decided: build_cell_mask over the whole stack is about 59 s at 40 by 2304 by 2304 and item 3 has already paid it, storing the mask on the session at its COMMIT.

What was decided: Refuse to start the mutation runner unless every mutation names a file the runner owns.
Why it was decided: One entry mutated ui/viewer.py, which was not in the runner's file list, so the restore never restored it and the md5 check at the end never looked at it, leaving the mutation live in the tree.

What was decided: Delete the pristine snapshot whenever the code legitimately changes mid-task.
Why it was decided: The runner restores from its snapshot at the top of every invocation, including a bare list, so a legitimate edit made after the snapshot was taken is silently reverted by the next call.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Remove the guard that skipped the arrival refresh for a freshly built screen.
Why it was decided: It skipped the refresh for screens being shown the first time, on the argument that their constructors had just synced.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Route every gesture through ViewerPort rather than through napari directly.
Why it was decided: The port grew bind_click, bind_double_click, bind_key, bind_dims and unbind_all, plus show_points and a Click event carrying position, modifiers and the ray.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Move the z-stepping contract into one gestures module and keep the Qt key handlers beside it.
Why it was decided: Six screens step through z.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give items 9a and 9b a set_z to match the step_z they already had.
Why it was decided: The shared binding could move them by a delta, but napari's own z slider reports an absolute slice and had nothing to call.

What was decided: Open item 2 on the middle slice and give it a working z control for the first time.
Why it was decided: Its draw has taken z and depth since task 10 and the driver always passed the defaults, so the z-batch box was inert and the z slice label read the words with no number after them.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Bind shift-left and shift-right as well as left and right, on all six z screens.
Why it was decided: The user's rule of 2026-08-20: when splitting a nucleus clump the user should be able to change z with the arrow keys while still holding shift to stay in split mode, so the seeds for the daughters land in the right place.

What was decided: Grow a hand-placed seed into the nucleus it lands in rather than stamping a fixed block.
Why it was decided: The user's rule of 2026-08-20: the user adds a seed to the centre of a nucleus in xy and z, and the program finds the nucleus.

What was decided: Do not apply the detector's minimum nucleus volume to a hand-placed seed.
Why it was decided: That floor is the detector's, and the seed is the user overriding the detector on exactly the cases it got wrong.

What was decided: Stamp a ball of the expected diameter when a seed lands on nothing at all.
Why it was decided: The user has asserted a nucleus is there and the gesture's contract is to add one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Replay the operation record onto the committed labels rather than drawing the committed volume.
Why it was decided: delete_nucleus, add_nucleus and release_shift each appended to the record and called draw, and draw pushed the committed volume, so a double-click on a nucleus recorded a deletion and left the nucleus on screen while microglial 5 of 35 kept answering for the detection as it arrived.

What was decided: Count item 4's detected nuclei from the ids actually present rather than from the array length.
Why it was decided: It was the size of the membership fractions array, and that returns one entry per id up to the largest, so deleting nucleus 1 of 2 left id 2 in the volume, the array still 2 long, and the strip still reading of 2 with one nucleus on screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Convert a click in two steps at the point of capture and undo it in exactly one place.
Why it was decided: Section 4a.1 requires native full-image voxel coordinates, converted once at the point of capture and never in a reader.

What was decided: Apply rich review's crop offset once, where a split marker is captured.
Why it was decided: Every layer there is drawn cropped, so a click arrives crop-relative.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Take the keys to unbind from the difference in napari's keymap rather than from the string that was passed.
Why it was decided: napari's keymap is keyed by KeyBinding objects and not by the string, so binding u lands under KeyBinding U and shift-left under KeyBinding Shift+Left, and popping the raw string in unbind_all removed nothing, silently.

What was decided: Drive the gestures against real napari in the shakeout on every run.
Why it was decided: The suite could not see the keymap fault at all.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Have item 4 call the shared z-stepping binding rather than its own copy.
Why it was decided: Item 4 had built its own copy of the arrow and dims bindings, so three mutations on the shared key list and follow handler came back green: the contract was in one place and item 4 was obeying another.

What was decided: Remove the zeroing of the split target before a split.
Why it was decided: split_by_watershed assigns every voxel of the object to exactly one marker, since a split never discards material, so each one is overwritten anyway.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Z-batch depth applies on ENTER or focus-out, not on the COMMIT button.
Why it was decided: Item 4's commit is 200–500 s of Cellpose and item 9a has no commit at all, so a view control must not cost a recompute.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Layer pushes suppress napari's dims events for their duration.
Why it was decided: Adding a 3D layer back into a 2D world emits current_step synchronously and re-entered the layer list mid-mutation, which segfaults rather than raising.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A layer whose dimensionality changed is removed before being re-added.
Why it was decided: napari makes a duplicate name unique with a suffix, so adding over the top left a stale layer drawn underneath the new one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Pinch-to-zoom is answered in the callback slot dims_scroll vacated.
Why it was decided: napari refuses to route any modified scroll to the camera, so that slot is the only place a pinch still arrives.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Screens push their z onto the viewer as well as reading it back.
Why it was decided: bind_dims synced one way only, so an arrow key moved the derived 2D outline and left every 3D channel on napari's slice.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 3 swaps to threshold-and-objects panels after COMMIT.
Why it was decided: The committed mask was never on screen, so n objects counted something the screen could not show.

What was decided: Item 3's objects are coloured by the cycling label ring at a single alpha.
Why it was decided: Everything drawn has been identified, so there is no second class for an alpha to carry.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The layer list is rebuilt on a mode change rather than patched.
Why it was decided: napari assigns a grid panel by layer index, and re-adding the raw layer would silently swap the panels with every colour and header still correct.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 6 selection is by list only — clicks on the field and detail views do nothing.
Why it was decided: The user's rule, taken after the pointer path was built and found unnecessary.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ViewerPort.value_at was removed along with that click.
Why it was decided: The port is *what a screen needs and nothing more*, so a method no screen calls does not belong in it.

What was decided: Item 6's size ramp is jet over 0.125–0.875, replacing cividis.
Why it was decided: 3DMorph uses jet on this exact screen, so a reader who knows 3DMorph reads it without translating.

What was decided: The ramp is restricted at both ends rather than only the floor.
Why it was decided: Full jet runs #000080 to #800000, relative luminance 0.016 and 0.046 — effectively invisible at both ends on a black canvas.

What was decided: The lost lightness-monotonicity is kept as a test asserting the ramp is not monotonic.
Why it was decided: §6d's accessibility reasoning was outweighed rather than refuted, so the cost is written down rather than quietly deleted.

What was decided: grow_nucleus sizes its window and fallback ellipsoid per axis in micrometres.
Why it was decided: An xy pixel measure applied to z spanned the whole stack, growing a 7.6 µm nucleus across 35 slices instead of 13.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2 pushes 2D planes so napari offers no z slider.
Why it was decided: The user's rule that the arrow keys are the only z control, matching items 3 and 5.

What was decided: ring_colour moved from screen_nuclei to palette.py.
Why it was decided: Item 3 needed it, and importing it from item 4's module coupled two screens for a twelve-entry cycle.

What was decided: The sealed holdout was not run to choose a parameter.
Why it was decided: It is a spent one-shot resource, and fitting to it would destroy the only unbiased Phase A accuracy estimate.

What was decided: No DAPI threshold before detection.
Why it was decided: Recall held at 95% but under-split rose 10→13 and clump pairs fell 31→28 on the marked set — it removes dim *real* nuclei.

What was decided: stitch_threshold stays at 0.25.
Why it was decided: Raising it lost recall (95%→91%) and added false positives (67→85) while under-split never moved off 10.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: CanvasHost.take checks the widget's real parent instead of its cached mounted.
Why it was decided: The cache goes stale the moment another host re-parents the canvas, so a second visit never took it back.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's z slider is to be removed — approved, not yet built.
Why it was decided: Same rule as item 2, held back because it touches the coordinate conversion that already caused a silent doubling once.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: fill_soma_holes pads the mask by the structuring element's radius before binary_closing and crops back.
Why it was decided: scipy's default border_value=0 made the erosion delete every foreground voxel within one radius of the field edge — 8491 voxels of real Iba1 on the demo crop, and padding by exactly r measured byte-identical to padding by 4x and 8x.

What was decided: border_value=1 rejected as the fix for the closing's border erosion.
Why it was decided: It dilates the frame inward and invents signal along every edge — 550 voxels added on a 1050-voxel test shape — where padding is neither destructive nor generative.

What was decided: min_object_voxels is applied a second time, to the filled mask, inside build_cell_mask.
Why it was decided: The floor ran in threshold_channel two operations before find_cell_objects, so the closing manufactured 10- and 1-voxel objects the readout counted and the control had never seen.

What was decided: The second floor lands in build_cell_mask rather than in fill_soma_holes.
Why it was decided: min_object_voxels already lives in that signature, so the filler keeps its one job and its three existing tests keep their meaning.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Leaving the manufactured specks to item 6's cell-size cutoff rejected.
Why it was decided: Item 3's readout and item 6's own list would still both count them, and the control is named for a property the counted array would not have.

What was decided: The post-fill floor ships knowingly unguarded by any test that can fail.
Why it was decided: The closing is one slice thick and therefore per-plane, so a manufactured stray always has exactly the seed columns' voxel count and no floor value can separate them; the gap is recorded in the handoff instead.

What was decided: Outline nuclei becomes its own layer, microglial nuclei outline, holding only nuclei that pass membership_threshold.
Why it was decided: napari's contour replaces the shaded region rather than adding to it, so the old toggle turned the fills off whenever it was switched on.
