What was decided: The outline layer preserves label ids rather than renumbering them.
Why it was decided: Renumbering would recolour every nucleus, and the user's requirement was that a nucleus gain a boundary in the hue it already had.

What was decided: The outline layer draws every id at full alpha instead of reusing label_alphas.
Why it was decided: Nothing but microglial nuclei are in that volume, so there is no second class to mute against and repeating the muting would dim the thing the layer exists to sharpen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A log DAPI display toggle is added to item 4, off at arrival.
Why it was decided: Detection runs on log-compressed DAPI while the screen drew it linearly — p90 intensity renders at 2.9% grey and is 70.8% to the detector, and 35.9% of a confident nucleus core renders below 5% grey.

What was decided: log DAPI's contrast limits are taken from log1p of the raw 1st/98th percentiles.
Why it was decided: log1p is monotone, so the result is byte-identical to logging the volume first while avoiding an 850 MB second copy on a full field.

What was decided: An explicit item 1 display range is ignored while log DAPI is on.
Why it was decided: That range is expressed in raw intensity units and means nothing in log space, so logging its endpoints would show a number the user did not choose.

What was decided: The DAPI background estimator is a Gaussian high-pass, not a white top-hat.
Why it was decided: The top-hat is the better-behaved operator but measured 18.6 s on the demo crop against 0.65 s — roughly 546 s versus 19 s per field, across ~700 images.

What was decided: The background filter runs before the plaque veto, not after.
Why it was decided: A Gaussian estimate rings around a region of zeros — +189 against a background 95th percentile of 290, where a top-hat moved +0.11 — and the veto is the only step that writes zeros into DAPI.

What was decided: The filtered DAPI feeds everything downstream of the filter, including the add-a-nucleus gesture.
Why it was decided: Detection seeing filtered data while grow_nucleus saw raw would build a hand-added nucleus from different intensities than every automatic one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A live slider for the background filter rejected in favour of channel-live, labels-on-commit.
Why it was decided: The parameter changes what Cellpose is handed, so the labels cannot follow it without re-running detection.

What was decided: Tuning the background filter is deferred and it ships defaulting to off.
Why it was decided: The user asked for something usable the same day, and a non-zero default would be a number nobody has measured that changes every existing run.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The background filter's control is removed from item 4 and will get its own screen between items 1 and 2.
Why it was decided: The filter must run before the plaque veto, so a screen sitting before item 2 puts the control in the same order as the computation.

What was decided: The nucleus_background_sigma_um field is removed from SegmentationParams along with the control.
Why it was decided: A field name reaches the parameters file and the pool key permanently, and the name is exactly what is still being discussed.

What was decided: The post-detection label trim measured but not built.
Why it was decided: Trimming to 20% of each nucleus's own peak was the only rule that separated the four real nuclei from the ten spurious ones, but the user chose to build the pre-detection filter first.

What was decided: The draw-a-line measurement tool deliberately not designed.
Why it was decided: It is a new interface element across five or six screens and needs its own options conversation before any code.

What was decided: The new screen's two parameters are named dapi_background_strength and dapi_background_scale_um.
Why it was decided: cell_coefficient, plaque_veto_coefficient and mask_coefficient all already mean *multiplier on an Otsu threshold*, so reusing "coefficient" would have given a different operation the program's existing word for another one.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The background filter screen commits, storing the filtered DAPI as a session product.
Why it was decided: Items 2 and 4 and detection then read one array instead of each recomputing a filter measured at ~67 s on a production field.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The screen's two panels differ by the display transform and by nothing else, both carrying every layer and changing together.
Why it was decided: Item 5's recorded rule that the panels must be in the same state or the screen flatters one of them; with one panel filtered and the other not, every difference would have had two possible causes.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The screen takes item 5's frame without its accumulating table, and gets no z-batch depth box.
Why it was decided: Each extra slice in a z window costs its own background estimate because the subtraction and a max projection do not commute — about fifteen seconds behind every arrow key at depth 10 on a field.

What was decided: The background estimate is computed at half resolution above a 64 px sigma and exactly below it.
Why it was decided: Measured on crop2: 2.54% worst-voxel error at the gate for a 3.8x speedup, against 201% error at 4.6 px where the half-resolution grid stops sampling the kernel at all.

What was decided: The exact Gaussian at every sigma rejected.
Why it was decided: It is ~310 s on a 40 x 2304 x 2304 field at the screen's 12 µm default — a five-minute commit standing in front of every other screen in the flow.

What was decided: The recorded cost of the Gaussian estimator was overturned, from 0.65 s to 10.5 s on the demo crop.
Why it was decided: scipy's kernel radius is four sigma so cost is linear in sigma, and the original figure could not have been taken at the 12 µm scale the screen defaults to.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The strength control became a number box with no ceiling, after being a slider at 0-1, then 0-2, then 0-4.
Why it was decided: Once the screen's derived layers were made commit-gated there was nothing left for a live control to preview, and a box ends a ceiling that had moved three times in one sitting.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Both of the screen's parameters take effect on COMMIT and neither previews.
Why it was decided: What the button buys is the whole-field product and a whole-field readout, and neither can be taken from the one slice on screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The screen carries three layers — DAPI, DAPI kept and DAPI removed — with the derived pair greyed out until COMMIT.
Why it was decided: Before the button is pressed there is no answer to what survives, so a checkbox that could be ticked to reveal nothing would be the control contradicting itself.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The derived pair is pushed as empty arrays rather than withheld until the commit.
Why it was decided: napari assigns a grid panel by layer index, so adding two layers later would renumber every layer and move the split between the two panels.

What was decided: DAPI kept is drawn yellow.
Why it was decided: The user's choice; blue and red already mean DAPI and *removed* on item 2, and that screen's precedent is that a state of a channel takes its own colour.

What was decided: Committing switches the picture to DAPI kept and turns DAPI off.
Why it was decided: Kept is a subset of the channel, so leaving both on under additive blending would draw the surviving signal at double weight and the removed part at single.

What was decided: The *DAPI removed* readout is a share of intensity computed on the linear channel.
Why it was decided: The filter subtracts an amount from every voxel rather than deleting a set of them so there is no count to give, and log intensities do not sum to a total a share can be taken of.

What was decided: Detection reuses the committed filtered channel and is passed a zero strength meaning *already filtered*.
Why it was decided: Re-filtering there would subtract the background twice, which is the trap products[Step.VETO] already carries for the undilated plaque mask.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 6's field view draws each cell's own silhouette, painted largest first so the smallest lands on top.
Why it was decided: It was a maximum over label ids, and ids come from arbitrary connected-component order, so a small cell under a larger-id one was erased — zero pixels drawn on a purpose-built fixture.

What was decided: Item 6's field view is built from the measurement mask rather than the segmentation mask.
Why it was decided: The volumes in the list beside it are measurement-mask volumes, so a segmentation-mask picture would show silhouettes systematically smaller than the numbers it sits next to.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's napari z slider removed by making every layer on the screen two-dimensional.
Why it was decided: viewer.dims.ndim is the maximum over every layer, so converting the five array layers was not enough — an empty points layer reshaped to (0, 3) kept the third axis alive with no markers placed.

What was decided: Split markers are drawn only on the slice being shown, keeping their own z in the record.
Why it was decided: napari's out_of_slice_display defaults to False, measured directly, so an off-slice marker was already invisible and the rendered picture is unchanged.

What was decided: The measurement mask is split directly by the microglial nuclei, replacing the two-stage grow-from-segmentation arrangement.
Why it was decided: Nuclei are already the sole authority on cell separation, and item 5's mask has its own closing radius and its own object floor, so growing item 3's labels into it decided cell count on the wrong mask.

What was decided: Hole filling is dropped from the measurement mask.
Why it was decided: Hole filling exists so membership fractions work, and membership runs against the segmentation mask before this, so closing the lumens only inflates every exported volume.

What was decided: Debris is stored rather than discarded, as one aggregate per image with no per-component records.
Why it was decided: Anything genuinely worthless has already been deleted by min_object_voxels at item 3, so what survives to here is real signal that was being thrown away silently.

What was decided: Debris is hidden at items 6 and 7a and drawn as part of the scene in rich review.
Why it was decided: It is context rather than something to review or edit, and item 6's own history is a screen listing 45 volumes of which 42 rounded to 0 µm³.

What was decided: CD68 within debris is measured and exported.
Why it was decided: It costs almost nothing once debris is a mask, and it is what lets image_cd68_fraction_in_cell_masks decompose into cells, debris and genuinely-outside instead of one blurred figure.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Threshold 2 becomes required, with mask_coefficient unset raising rather than falling back to one-mask mode.
Why it was decided: The user's rule that any semi-auto user sets it while creating the parameters file for batch anyway, so a one-mask fallback is a second architecture nobody would use.

What was decided: A separate min_object_voxels for the measurement threshold, placed on item 5 where item 3 puts its own.
Why it was decided: Item 5 shared item 3's value and had no box for it at all, so the two masks could not be given different floors.

What was decided: A sweep of the other eighteen ground-truth crops declined before committing to the architecture change.
Why it was decided: On crop2 all four confident isolated somata landed in nucleated cells and none in a nucleus-free one, and the user accepted one crop as sufficient evidence.

What was decided: Item 2's contrast limits left as they are.
Why it was decided: Raised with the measurement — the same voxels are drawn on 0.01-3450 at the background screen and 0.00-3390 at item 2, a 1.8% difference — and the user chose to leave it.

What was decided: Re-tuning dapi_background_strength declined.
Why it was decided: Reported with the sweep — 35 nuclei found at strength 0 against 22 at strength 8, with the plateau between 0.6 and 2 — and the user chose to leave the value alone.

What was decided: Item 4's hand edits changing the picture but not the output remains parked.
Why it was decided: Reviewed and re-parked; it is a judgement about what the exported numbers are for rather than a technical choice, and nothing is blocked on it.

What was decided: The draw-a-line measurement tool remains parked, reaffirmed.
Why it was decided: Reviewed and re-parked unchanged: it is a new interface element across five or six screens and still needs its own options conversation first.

What was decided: Patch B built as a fill_holes flag on fill_soma_holes and build_cell_mask rather than by reading CellMask.raw.
Why it was decided: .raw skips the closing as well as the filling, which would have left mask_closing_radius_um on item 5 with its help text while doing nothing to the mask it names.

What was decided: The segmentation mask keeps both closing and hole filling; the measurement mask has no hole filling and takes the user's mask_closing_radius_um, where 0 means no closing at all.
Why it was decided: Measured on crop2: 841 649 voxels filled, against 823 295 / 741 920 / 683 304 unfilled at closing 0.8 / 0.4 / 0.0, so the value is honoured and 0 is a genuine no-op.

What was decided: A closing radius large relative to a soma cavity will still close it, and this is accepted unwarned.
Why it was decided: It is what a closing does to any concavity narrower than its element; at the 0.8 default the lumens stay open and are 2.18% of mask volume, so it does not bite in practice.

What was decided: speck_floor_um3 deleted from the program.
Why it was decided: It ran before debris existed and removed ~88% of objects (537 → 62 measured), so nothing could account for what it took and the debris totals could never have closed against the mask.

What was decided: measurement_min_object_voxels added for the measurement mask, defaulting to 20.
Why it was decided: 20 is item 3's existing value, so giving item 5 its own floor moves no number on its own.

What was decided: Item 5's new box is labelled measurement_min_object_voxels, not min_object_voxels.
Why it was decided: §2's rule that control labels are parameters-file identifiers has a test of its own, and the two boxes are different fields whose values need not agree.

What was decided: What measurement_min_object_voxels removes is not counted as debris.
Why it was decided: Unlike the deleted speck floor it is asked for, visible on its own screen and recorded in the parameters file, so what it removes is a stated choice rather than a hidden constant.

What was decided: assign_labels_by_connectivity kept as the mechanism carrying cells to native resolution, and assign_labels_to_native taken off the pipeline path instead.
Why it was decided: Its no-cell rule is exactly the debris definition, while the alternative's unbounded nearest-label fill would attach a detached debris blob to whichever cell happened to be closest.

What was decided: Debris derived as the measurement mask minus the surviving cells, in one expression.
Why it was decided: Both halves of the definition then fall out together rather than being two accumulators that have to be kept in step by hand.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Debris reaches item 7b through the existing everything else layer rather than a new layer.
Why it was decided: COMPONENT_05_PLAN.md §393 already defines that layer as the file's threshold mask minus this cell, which debris now falls inside.

What was decided: Debris CD68 is the threshold-free integrated sum only.
Why it was decided: cd68_threshold is Phase C and is None while segment_image runs, and the capture fraction this measure exists to decompose has a threshold-free denominator.

What was decided: Pool schema bumped 1 → 2 and parameters schema 6 → 7.
Why it was decided: Both bumps are free only while no pool exists, and a search of the whole project root found no pool.db, no pool directory and no parameters file.

What was decided: The parameters bump was taken for a field *removal* as well as an addition.
Why it was decided: A v6 file names a field v7 has no home for, so loading it silently would drop a floor the run was tuned with.

What was decided: The ground-truth acceptance check asks for the nearest label within 1.0 µm rather than testing the marker voxel itself.
Why it was decided: Iba1 is cytoplasmic, so a soma-centre marker sits in the lumen patch B stopped filling; the two affected markers were 0.60 µm and 0.22 µm from mask, well inside the 2.29 µm radius of the smallest cell.

What was decided: Threshold 2 reaffirmed as required, with the one-mask branch deleted rather than kept as a fallback.
Why it was decided: Reviewed against the cost of updating six test fixtures and upheld: a silent second architecture is how two routes drift into disagreeing about what a cell is.

What was decided: Reaffirmed that debris stays an aggregate per image rather than gaining per-component records.
Why it was decided: The consequence — that debris can never enter the convex-hull territory measures — was put to the user with that reasoning and accepted.

What was decided: §E's images.csv debris columns not built.
Why it was decided: Storing the fields without exporting them keeps this to one schema bump, so surfacing the columns later needs no second one.

What was decided: Item 7a debris rejections not reconciled with segment-time debris.
Why it was decided: The reconciliation is export-side work, and it sits inside the measurement-and-export question the user parked.

What was decided: The item 8 border-cell morphometrics toggle not built.
Why it was decided: Parked with every other item 8 question, including whether such a choice skips measurement or only drops rows at export time.

What was decided: Debris not admitted to the territory block.
Why it was decided: union_surveyed_um3 and its neighbours are convex hulls over per-cell records, and an aggregate volume has no hull.

What was decided: A thresholded debris CD68 at item 9a's threshold not built.
Why it was decided: It would have to become a Phase C measure with the debris mask stored, because cd68_threshold does not exist at the point debris is computed.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 7b's debris view not widened beyond the entered cell's bounding box.
Why it was decided: draw() clips every layer on that screen to that box, so widening it means changing the editor's whole loading contract rather than one layer.

What was decided: fill_soma_holes's redundant 3D binary_fill_holes not removed.
Why it was decided: Measured on a hollow cube, a hollow sphere and a cavity open through z, it adds 0 voxels beyond the per-slice loop, so it is pre-existing dead work rather than something this patch introduced.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The shakeout's failing z-slider probe on item 4 not debugged.
Why it was decided: It fails identically against the pre-patch backup, and a z slider was removed from item 4, so the probe is stale rather than the screen broken.

What was decided: Debris is the measurement mask minus every surviving cell, computed once in Phase C after review.
Why it was decided: Both operands are already durable — the Iba1 channel plus three hashed parameters, and the cells in the pool — so their difference is the only part that can disagree with its own inputs.

What was decided: The debris mask is not stored in the pool.
Why it was decided: Phase C already reopens the source image for CD68, DAPI and 6E10, so recomputing adds no dependency the call did not already have, against ~212 MB per production field that could still go stale.

What was decided: The four debris fields added to FileRecord on 2026-08-24 are removed again, pool schema 2 → 3.
Why it was decided: FileRecord is written at segment time, so debris stored there answers what no *derived* cell claimed while the export needs what no *surviving* cell claims.

What was decided: Debris has four numbered sources: 1a unclaimed objects, 1b components the coarse pass never saw, 2 the item 6 cutoff, 3 rejections at rich review.
Why it was decided: 1a and 1b are one thing to a reader and two to the code, so the numbering keeps the distinction available without forcing it on anyone.

What was decided: Border-touching debris is not counted separately from interior debris.
Why it was decided: The user's call, with the consequence recorded rather than hidden: a high debris fraction then mixes framing with segmentation failure.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 6's cutoff is applied destructively on leaving the screen, and the fold is monotonic.
Why it was decided: No screen after item 6 can navigate back to it, so a reversible view would answer a question the flow never asks.

What was decided: A cell rejected as real_cell does not become debris.
Why it was decided: It is a real cell the reviewer could not certify rather than a misdetection, so it stays a cell and remains takeable behind the transfer popup.

What was decided: A cell accepted as real is erased from the scene for every cell reviewed after it.
Why it was decided: OWNERSHIP maps confirmed to hidden, documented as "impossible — it is not drawn", so not drawing it makes its material untakeable by construction rather than by rule.

What was decided: Debris is takeable at rich review with no confirmation popup.
Why it was decided: It is unowned by definition, and §9.4e's reasoning that debris "has no arrays, so its voxels cannot be identified as owned even in principle" stopped being true when the patch gave it a mask.

What was decided: Rejected-real cells contribute convex hulls to union_surveyed_um3, overturning D-A2 of 2026-08-12.
Why it was decided: The exclusion rested on those cells having no morphometrics, which is a statement about mechanism rather than geometry, and NEW-b had already settled the same argument for the plaque measures.

What was decided: Rejected-real cells do not get a per-cell territorial_volume_um3.
Why it was decided: A per-cell number invites cell-to-cell comparison in a way an image-level aggregate does not.

What was decided: Rejected-real cells get a partial measurement row carrying bulk, signal and location but never shape.
Why it was decided: An uncertified boundary gives a broken skeleton but only a slightly wrong sum, so the two classes of measure do not degrade alike.

What was decided: The four per-cell CD68 measures are computed for rejected-real cells as well as confirmed ones.
Why it was decided: cd68_integrated is threshold-free, so it degrades smoothly where a skeleton does not, and cd68_status already exists to filter on.

What was decided: Rejected-real cells carry cell_volume_um3.
Why it was decided: Without it cd68_fraction, the literature's preferred form, is blank for exactly the rows the previous decision added.

What was decided: mean_z_um follows CD68 to confirmed-plus-rejected-real.
Why it was decided: A row carrying an intensity measure must carry the depth covariate every intensity comparison needs, or the measure is unusable.

What was decided: Territory becomes three categories — surveyed, debris, unsurveyed — with surveyed winning where they overlap.
Why it was decided: A fragment inside a cell's hull is tissue that cell surveys, and counting it in both would let the parts exceed the field.

What was decided: covered_fraction@d is renamed covered_fraction_cells@d and gains a covered_fraction_iba1@d sibling rather than being redefined.
Why it was decided: The cell column has already been reported under its own meaning, so folding debris into it would change a validated number without changing its name.

What was decided: The population goes in the column-name suffix rather than the prefix.
Why it was decided: The pair then sorts adjacently in an alphabetical column list, which is where a reader actually meets them.

What was decided: No debris_fraction column is exported.
Why it was decided: It is iba1_volume_debris_um3 ÷ iba1_volume_um3, and a derived column beside its own source can only ever disagree with it.

What was decided: The image counts become n_cells_confirmed, n_cells_lost_real and n_real_cells.
Why it was decided: The old pair differed only in word order and was read as duplicates, while the population most often wanted had no column at all.

What was decided: debris_status and debris_cd68_status are kept as two separate statuses.
Why it was decided: A missing CD68 channel leaves the volumes perfectly measurable, so one status covering both would make an image with no CD68 read like an image with no debris.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 7b's everything else layer is split into other cells in green and debris in yellow.
Why it was decided: One flat colour could not tell a neighbour from unclaimed material, so the question the screen exists to answer had no visible answer.

What was decided: other cells renders one picked hue in two treatments, faint soma and solid processes.
Why it was decided: What has to be adjudicated is whether a *process* belongs to this cell, and the soma is 53–84% of cell volume so a solid one would be a wall of colour with the processes lost against it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: this cell keeps its per-region scheme but regains a translucency slider that multiplies its region alphas.
Why it was decided: Setting the alpha outright would erase the entered-versus-not-entered cue, which is the one thing that layer's alpha carries.

What was decided: Only Iba1 signal, this cell and nucleus arrive on, moving other nuclei from on to off.
Why it was decided: Context the reviewer has not asked for should not be imposed, which is the rule the DAPI layer already followed.

What was decided: raw DAPI becomes DAPI as detected, carrying the background-filtered, vetoed, log-compressed volume.
Why it was decided: The detector runs on normalize_for_detection, which found 24 nuclei where an aggressive percentile clip found 5, so a reviewer judging a missed nucleus must see the volume that was judged.

What was decided: other nuclei shows only the nuclei of visible neighbours, with orphans left undrawn.
Why it was decided: A nucleus whose cell fell under the size cutoff would imply a neighbouring cell that is not there.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The context layers are widened by the margin and carry a per-layer translate.
Why it was decided: crop_box clips to the array it is handed, which was already the bounding box, so the margin could not widen anything and material beside a cell was never drawn.

What was decided: The editable cell mask is not widened along with the context layers.
Why it was decided: That is the whole loading contract, which this work deliberately did not open.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 6's Detail panel is built from the label volume rather than from the field projection.
Why it was decided: Reading the selection back out of a largest-first projection returns the cell minus every overlapping neighbour — measured as 55 pixels of a 64-pixel cell.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's slider runs item 3's full 0–3.0 range rather than stopping at item 3's coefficient.
Why it was decided: The cap rested on the parameter being a provable no-op above that value, which stopped being true when the debris patch made the seed a subset of the measurement mask: mask volume falls from 4803 µm³ at 0.18 to 153 µm³ at 3.00.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Every layer on rich review carries the voxel size as a scale, with the context offset converted to world units and clicks converted at the point of capture.
Why it was decided: The volume rendered flat by exactly 5.54×, which is the z:xy anisotropy, and napari applies translate after scale so an offset left in voxels would slide the layers by that same factor.

What was decided: RecordingViewer.show_labels parses hex colours the way the real viewer does.
Why it was decided: It previously stored anything at all, so a colour name passed where hex was required kept the whole suite green and crashed rich review on entry.

What was decided: The measure ledger is saved into docs/ as a reading aid explicitly subordinate to EXPORT_SPEC.md §5.
Why it was decided: §5 is parsed by tests/_spec_columns.py and the ledger is parsed by nothing, so a second column list has to say which of the two is load-bearing.

What was decided: Remove the stale z-slider claim from the shakeout's reported probes rather than re-investigating it.
Why it was decided: The paragraph claimed that the z slider moving the screen passes on every run.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The ! on triage gets the "?" §3d's *Seven popups* specified, one per screen on the first marked tile still showing.
Why it was decided: §3d calls it the strongest exception in the project — the border flag is the one thing a reviewer could not possibly infer — and a mark whose explanation vanishes while other marks remain is worse than none.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The ! and its "?" are centred as a pair, putting the mark a few px left of the thumbnail's midline on that one tile.
Why it was decided: A child widget is clipped to its parent, so the button cannot overhang into the gutter, and widening that tile would widen its whole grid column and step every column after it out of line.

What was decided: Resolving a cell from rich review is not a TriageAction, so u does not undo it.
Why it was decided: §3b already rules that triage's undo never reaches back into a finalised rich-review episode, which had its own undo and expired it deliberately.

What was decided: The rejection's cell count feeding n_real_cells was not built in this pass.
Why it was decided: It needs a schema field, a set_status argument, a widened decisions tuple and a changed definition for n_cells_lost_real, which is a data-model change rather than the UI fix being walked.

What was decided: Iba1 signal, other nuclei and DAPI as detected widen with the margin alongside other cells and debris.
Why it was decided: Widening two layers out of five grew the neighbours and the debris into a black field, because the channel they are cut from stopped at the old boundary.

What was decided: this cell and nucleus are not widened with the margin.
Why it was decided: They are the entered cell's own masks and bbox-shaped by definition, so widening them pads zeros and shows nothing, and they are the frame every translate is measured against.

What was decided: Iba1 signal takes a second array, iba1_context, separate from the intensity the editor decomposes.
Why it was decided: set_cell's intensity is what CellEditor works on, so widening it would move the editing frame under edits the reviewer has already made.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A layer is drawn in the context frame only when it was cut in one, decided per call rather than per layer.
Why it was decided: Putting the three new layers in CONTEXT_LAYERS outright made them bypass crop_box, which is the only margin mechanism the standalone route has, and a test with a small cell in a large volume caught it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The nearest drawn thing along the ray wins a double-click, replacing *"this cell wins ties"*.
Why it was decided: With a point a tie meant the same voxel; with a ray it would mean the cell wins even when occluded, so clicking a neighbour in front would remove a piece of your own cell behind it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A layer toggled off is not a click candidate.
Why it was decided: Only what is drawn can be hit, which is the same property that lets a confirmed cell be hidden rather than refused, and it makes the toggles a way to aim.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: CellEditor works in the bounding box grown by the margin slider's maximum, cut once at entry.
Why it was decided: It makes the silent decline unreachable by construction — the context box can never exceed a box padded by a margin it can never exceed — while keeping the margin a pure view control.

What was decided: The 20 µm margin maximum is kept and the editable pad built at it without measuring the cost.
Why it was decided: The user judged it affordable and chose to measure only if it bites; the untimed cost is recorded in editable_box's docstring as the first thing to suspect if entering a cell becomes slow.

What was decided: Detached material is taken with a bridge, after a warning naming the bridge length in µm.
Why it was decided: The reviewer is allowed through, so the popup's job is to make the cost visible — the bridge joins the mask and is measured as a process by the skeleton, the Sholl profile and the branch lengths.

What was decided: Taking the intersection of a take that does not fit was rejected.
Why it was decided: It would give the cell a process stopping at an invisible boundary, converting a UI limitation into a wrong measurement that nothing on screen could show.

What was decided: bridge_path is left computing in voxel space; only bridge_length_um passes sampling.
Why it was decided: What must not be wrong is the number shown to the reviewer; the path's choice among several near-equal pairs is a small distortion and making it physical would change a function three tests pin.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Nothing declines in silence — a refused take returns "unavailable" and says so on screen.
Why it was decided: double_click returned "add" while adding nothing, so a deliberate refusal was indistinguishable from a dead gesture, which is the position the user was actually in.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A transfer takes only the double-clicked process, never the whole neighbour and never its soma.
Why it was decided: other_cells is already 1-soma / 2-process, so labelling the components of == 2 splits a neighbour at its body; taking a cell body would be a merge rather than a transfer.

What was decided: Taking a neighbour's process removes it from the neighbour's mask, and debris addition is the only pure addition.
Why it was decided: Without the paired write both cells would carry the same voxels and volume, territory and Sholl would each count them twice.

What was decided: A cell may only have a process taken from it while it is not yet confirmed.
Why it was decided: Reviewed against the built behaviour and found already enforced: _repaint_scene erases a confirmed cell from the scene, so it is not in the array a click tests.

What was decided: A transfer may not empty its donor, and the attempt is refused out loud.
Why it was decided: A cell at zero voxels vanishes from payloads(), which would slide every later decision onto the wrong cell because apply_decisions joins by position.

What was decided: 7b edit persistence was parked to Phase C and then unparked and built in the same session.
Why it was decided: Parking it left the agreed paired write with nowhere to land, and the transfer could not be finished without it.

What was decided: Edits are painted into derivation.labels rather than carried as a payload override.
Why it was decided: payloads()'s own rule is that every quantity is derived rather than accepted from a caller, an override would have to recompute bbox, thumbnail, soma and counts through a second path, and the paired write falls out of painting for free.

What was decided: The paint happens once at finalisation, not on every edit.
Why it was decided: The episode's u unwinds everything until the cell resolves, so painting per edit would write a state the reviewer can still take back, and §9.4b already asks for one transaction per episode.

What was decided: A take subtracts from the donor's held payload immediately, rather than painting differentially or re-deriving.
Why it was decided: ReviewStep.cells is a snapshot taken once on arrival, so a donor entered later would paint its original mask back and silently undo the transfer.

What was decided: human_edited is stamped only on cells whose mask actually changed.
Why it was decided: It means *a person changed this*, not *a person looked at this*, which reviewed already carries.

What was decided: Splits remain parked, together with the stranded children of _finish.
Why it was decided: They renumber the label volume, which breaks the positional decision key, and they need the child-uid scheme and a MANUAL SplitMethod settled first.

What was decided: The duplicate _world_offset was deleted rather than kept in step with its twin.
Why it was decided: Python keeps the later definition, so correcting the first changed nothing and the context layers sat one padding away from the cell they belong to.

What was decided: The redundant tile-sizing mechanism was removed rather than the surviving mutation excused.
Why it was decided: Tile.setFixedSize and a setFixedHeight on the mark row did the same job, so reverting either left the other holding the property and no test could see it.

What was decided: A neighbour's soma on other cells is drawn lighter as well as at reduced alpha, on two channels rather than one.
Why it was decided: Alpha alone had to carry the soma/process distinction and answer the layer's translucency slider, so moving the slider degraded the encoding it was moving.

What was decided: The decomposition becomes three levels at 0.99 / 0.97 / 0.85, replacing two at 0.96 / 0.90.
Why it was decided: The shipped pair was an uneven ladder at ~4.5x then ~2.6x per step, and 0.97 evens it — interpolating to 0.969 on three cells independently.

What was decided: The three levels are cuts of one ToMATo fit rather than independent clusterings.
Why it was decided: ToMATo is hierarchical, so raising the merge threshold only ever merges and each finer cut is a strict refinement, making granularity conservation exact rather than measured.

What was decided: Raising the process coefficient from 0.96 to 0.99 is rejected as the fix for one process showing many colours.
Why it was decided: Cluster counts saturate because ToMATo merges only into an adjacent higher peak, so 183 of one cell's 202 regions were disconnected components no threshold can merge.

What was decided: Clicking the background in rich review rises one level rather than clearing the whole path.
Why it was decided: With three cuts those stopped being the same act, and clearing discards the descent just made to reach a neighbouring piece.

What was decided: Deleting a region mid-process severs the mask, and anything detached becomes debris.
Why it was decided: Debris is recomputed in Phase C as measurement mask minus claimed, so a fragment dropped from the cell's label volume becomes debris with no new storage and no schema change.

What was decided: The sever anchor is the soma, then the nucleus, then the largest component.
Why it was decided: find_soma returns no region when erosion consumes the cell and a two-channel study has no nuclei, so without a third fallback the anchor would be undefined.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: One undo restores both the removal and whatever it severed, as a single operation.
Why it was decided: Two operations would let one press leave the cell in a state it was never in — the middle of a process gone but its far end back.

What was decided: Severing is not applied to split children, after being agreed and built.
Why it was decided: It breaks split_by_watershed's documented reconstitution invariant, and a piece reachable only through a sibling's territory belongs to that sibling rather than to debris.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: No readout or popup announces a severing.
Why it was decided: The user judged the effect visible on screen without one.

What was decided: The nucleus lumen is closed before soma erosion, marked by the nucleus rather than by a blanket hole fill.
Why it was decided: A blanket fill could close rings formed by wrapping processes at different rates in 5xFAD and WT, putting a genotype-differential bias into cell volume.

What was decided: The lumen fill uses a 3D pass and a per-slice pass, not the 3D pass alone.
Why it was decided: Two of four cells read as having no lumen at all under the 3D pass and in fact carried 28.8 and 64.9 um3, the second holding 53.1 um3 of its own nucleus.

What was decided: soma_volume_um3 includes the nucleus the soma envelops.
Why it was decided: Imaris manual surface tracing and the nucleator both measure it that way, and with no ground truth of this project's own, comparability with the reference methods outweighed staying near the previous magnitude.

What was decided: No volume cap is added to guard the lumen fill against reaching a process loop.
Why it was decided: Across 20 cells no filled cavity exceeded its own nucleus — median 0.19x, maximum 1.01x — so the cap would guard something that is not happening.

What was decided: DAPI as detected is left eagerly allocated.
Why it was decided: It costs ~850 MB only on a production field, and production runs on Bunya where memory is not the constraint.

What was decided: A minimum component size on the decomposition is deferred until after the soma mechanism changes.
Why it was decided: rest = mask & ~soma is what generates the speck rind, so any threshold set beforehand would only need re-tuning afterwards.

What was decided: The four soma-accuracy validation steps are parked but recorded as required work rather than optional.
Why it was decided: The nucleator estimates volume from any interior reference point plus isotropic random rays, so the existing 264 point marks are usable without re-marking.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Deciding a triage band's last cell in item 7b advances item 7a to the next band on return.
Why it was decided: Coming back to 0 cells on this screen left Accept This Screen — a button that clears nothing — as the only way forward.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The file-done state is gated on remaining_in_file() == 0 rather than on the band index.
Why it was decided: An undo can restore cells to an earlier band while the reviewer stands on a later one, so the band index can be right while the sentence on screen is false.

What was decided: A reviewer who finishes a file stays on the band they finished on rather than advancing.
Why it was decided: Every band left is empty for the same reason, so advancing would only move the same empty grid.

What was decided: The advance is a loop past empty bands rather than a single step.
Why it was decided: split_into_screens only ever puts an empty band after another empty one, so the two are indistinguishable in normal use, but undo plus a re-accept can empty a later band out of order.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The proceed button reads Next File or Continue, derived from the file n of m counter already on screen.
Why it was decided: Semi-auto has file_total = 1 and forwards file_accepted to item 9a, so Next File would name a file the button could not open.

What was decided: undo returns to the band its action was taken on instead of decrementing screen_index.
Why it was decided: The decrement was correct only while an accept was the only thing that could move the band; the new advance records no action, so u restored band 1's cells while leaving the reviewer on band 2.

What was decided: u will not bring back a cell finalised in rich review.
Why it was decided: _leave calls _persist_edits, whose paint its own docstring calls monotonic and irreversible once done, so restoring the tile would leave the grid saying undecided while the record says rejected.

What was decided: The two accepts are disabled rather than hidden in the done state, with a helper sentence saying why.
Why it was decided: Items 1.5, 5 and 9b set the precedent of carrying a disabled state twice — the greyed control, and a sentence for anyone who cannot separate the two greys.

What was decided: Item 7a opening on an empty HARD band for files of three or fewer scored cells is not fixed here.
Why it was decided: band_sizes rounds the 15% quantile to zero below four cells — pre-existing, a different cause, and outside the item 7b return path this change covers.

What was decided: The soma becomes two mechanisms — a guaranteed nucleus anchor plus a thickness floor grown outward from it.
Why it was decided: One soma/process boundary can be wrong in two directions, each mechanism guards one, and the anchor is what makes a floor aggressive enough to reject any process safe to set.

What was decided: Growth from the anchor replaces selection among eroded remnants.
Why it was decided: The old rule could choose among the components erosion left but never split one, so a thick proximal process fused to the cell body was taken whole and the nucleus was powerless.

What was decided: A dimensionless thickness fraction is rejected in favour of an absolute threshold, after being proposed and agreed.
Why it was decided: A microglial process is ~0.5-1 um whatever the cell's state, and measured, the ratio inverted the criterion — a thin-bodied cell admitted 274.6 um3 of outside material where a thick-bodied one admitted 5.9.

What was decided: soma_erode_um is renamed soma_thickness_um and raised from 0.3 to 0.9.
Why it was decided: Median soma falls 58% to 25% of cell volume then plateaus at 23%, matching the only comparable published method at ~24% and keeping material at least 1.8 um across — between a 0.5-1 um process and a 4-8 um soma.

What was decided: The soma centroid is taken from the restored soma region rather than from the eroded core.
Why it was decided: It is the Dijkstra root for every branch length, the hierarchy and both Sholl profiles, so it should centre the region a reader would call the cell body.

What was decided: The sub-micron test fixtures are overridden with a stated threshold rather than having soma_volume_um3 added to BLANK_WITH_REASON.
Why it was decided: An exemption would hide a real regression in that column permanently, where an override records why the fixture cannot satisfy the physical threshold.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9b's log slider loses its absolute value box, leaving the slider as the only writer of plaque_threshold.
Why it was decided: ParameterSlider already draws a live value label above its own groove, so the box duplicated a number that stays on screen without it, and item 9a had dropped its box in the previous sitting.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The plaque picker row on item 9b defaults to red rather than magenta, taking the swatch selected on the running screen.
Why it was decided: The call was made against the live 6E10 canvas, which is the only place a 2 px outline's legibility over its own channel can actually be judged.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9b keeps the program-wide rule that Step by batch is disabled at z-batch depth 1 and live above it, and is the one screen of five that never implemented it.
Why it was decided: A headless probe of the real screen returned isEnabled() == False at depth 1 and again at depth 4, against four sibling screens that call setEnabled(self.depth > 1) inside set_depth.

What was decided: The rest of item 9b is accepted as built, closing its walkthrough.
Why it was decided: The screen was walked live and everything outside the three rows above was reported working.

What was decided: Item 9b, item 8 and Phase C are excluded from the bookkeeping sweep.
Why it was decided: The user scoped it mid-session — *"dont touch anything to do with item 9b or 8 or phase c"*.

What was decided: All nine parameters with no recorded purpose are written up, from the code that consumes each.
Why it was decided: The reason they were left bare did not hold: every one had a careful explanation already written in threshold.py, nuclei.py, split.py, membership.py or _thumbnail, so nothing had to be guessed.

What was decided: The test asserting that bare fields exist becomes a synthetic case rather than being deleted, against its own failure message.
Why it was decided: Its message weighed deletion against weakening the assertion, and a blanked fixture field is neither — the property *whatever is bare is marked bare in its own row* survives intact.

What was decided: A third test is added holding the real source to nothing bare.
Why it was decided: The synthetic test proves the marker works and cannot prove there is nothing to mark; neither half is worth much alone.

What was decided: Guard tests count the screens carrying each shared block, and deliberately do not name which screens.
Why it was decided: Every stale count found that day was prose with nothing comparing it to anything, while the flow count never drifted because test_ui_app derives it — and a named list is the list-to-maintain failure write_parameters_doc.py exists to abolish.

What was decided: HANDOFF_BUILD.md is marked closed with a banner rather than rewritten.
Why it was decided: Its front page told a fresh session to start at task 26, which shipped ten days earlier — a stale pointer at the entry point misleads before a reader knows enough to doubt it.

What was decided: The task-dated suite counts inside HANDOFF_BUILD.md are not back-edited.
Why it was decided: A count belongs to a dated event, so a task-25 figure is a record of task 25 and correct as such.

What was decided: COMPONENT_STATUS.md's test-count progression is extended with a new dated entry rather than the number overwritten.
Why it was decided: The block states that rule itself — *"a count belongs to a dated event or it does not appear"* — so overwriting it would break the convention it exists to enforce.

What was decided: docs/HANDOFF_PHASE_B.md is opened as the live handoff.
Why it was decided: A banner on the closed one says *don't read this* and a fresh session still needs somewhere to go.

What was decided: The two universal rules in COMPONENT_03_PLAN.md lose their screen count instead of having it corrected.
Why it was decided: Neither rule ever depended on the number, and a universal rule that names a count acquires a way to be wrong that its own content does not have.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: *"Five screens carry a COMMIT"* is left uncorrected in app.py and gui_shakeout.py.
Why it was decided: Both sit inside blocks headed *"— task 24"*, where five was true, and a dated record is not stale.

What was decided: The headings of EXPORT_SPEC.md §39 and the SHAKEOUT bridge section are marked superseded and reverted.
Why it was decided: Both bodies already carried the correction sixty-odd lines below a heading that still said *"built"*, and the heading is what survives a scan of a 242 KB file.

What was decided: A current status block is added above the 2026-08-20 one in SHAKEOUT_FINDINGS.md rather than replacing it.
Why it was decided: The old block is accurate for the four screens it covers, and the three still-open early items (O2, m8, m7) would be lost behind a newer heading.

What was decided: CELLS_LAYER is renamed to MASK_LAYER in screen_cd68.py.
Why it was decided: The constant held "measurement mask" after the user's correction and only two lines referenced it, so the flagged rename cost nothing.

What was decided: The word *"selects"* stays in soma.py's docstring as a dated pointer rather than being deleted.
Why it was decided: It records what the old rule could not do — choose among the components erosion happened to leave, with no way to split one.

What was decided: A real_cell rejection's cell count will be persisted per cell as n_real_cells_here and carried into the exports.
Why it was decided: The popup and Resolution.n_cells already capture the number and _leave drops it by writing a three-tuple, so only the persist-and-count chain is missing.

What was decided: n_real_cells_here reads 1 on confirmed rows, the reviewer's number on real_cell rejections, and blank on debris.
Why it was decided: Debris is excluded from every cell count, so printing 1 there would imply it counts toward something it does not.

What was decided: plaques.csv's n_cells_within@d follows the multiplicity rather than staying an object count.
Why it was decided: phasec.py ties cell_labels to n_real_cells' inclusion rule precisely so the two columns cannot count cells by two different rules.

What was decided: real_cell_loss_rate becomes R/(C+R), dropping debris from the denominator.
Why it was decided: It is currently R/(C+R+D), and the function's own docstring says the concern is the sample being thinned unevenly between genotypes — debris was never in that sample.

What was decided: n_real_cells_here is also emitted as a per-row column in cells.csv.
Why it was decided: The image totals cannot say which rejection carried the count, so neither the review nor n_cells_within@d could be audited from the CSVs alone.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The count popup's Cancel returns to the reject-reason popup instead of committing the rejection with a count of 1.
Why it was decided: Cancel aborts on the first popup and commits on the second, so one word does two different jobs in consecutive popups of a single flow.

What was decided: The sentence promising that debris image data is deleted permanently is removed from reject_question(), the popup itself kept.
Why it was decided: Verified that nothing in the codebase deletes cell arrays — the only unlink in store.py is temp-file cleanup — and the popup is how the reject reason is chosen.

What was decided: §9.4e's array deletion, and the two design statements resting on it, are not built or corrected here.
Why it was decided: Both are parked, and this change needs only that the popup stop promising something unbuilt.

What was decided: SCHEMA_VERSION goes from 3 to 4 with no migration path.
Why it was decided: No pool exists on disk, so the bump costs nothing today.

What was decided: n_cells_confirmed is not made multiplicity-aware.
Why it was decided: The count popup fires only on a real_cell rejection, so a confirmed cell is always exactly one cell.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: soma_method is offered on item 6.5 as a dropdown, reversing the same-morning ruling that fixed it at anchor_sheet.
Why it was decided: The program otherwise had no way to ask for the soma to be the nucleus and the cytoplasm around it, and making the boxes follow the method removed the inert-control objection that had justified hiding it.

What was decided: opening is the answer to "nucleus surrounding soma only" rather than a new anchor-only mechanism.
Why it was decided: §37 measured only 2.2% of a cell clearing the thickness floor on these masks, so soma_volume_um3 came out 83% anchor — the opening already is the perinuclear region on this study's data.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: anchor_sheet remains the selected default, with opening second in the dropdown.
Why it was decided: It is what the study has been walked under, so the default's reachability changed while the default itself did not.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The dropdown displays the stored values anchor_sheet and opening rather than plain-language labels.
Why it was decided: Every other row on item 6.5 prints its SegmentationParams field name, so a friendly label would be the one place on that screen where the glass and the parameters file said different words.

What was decided: Choosing opening resets the three anchor_sheet boxes to their defaults instead of remembering what was typed.
Why it was decided: An inert value still travels in params_hash, so two opening runs producing identical cells would otherwise key two different pools.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: soma_method moves out of HIDDEN_FIELDS into item 8's read-only block.
Why it was decided: session_params filters session.chosen against READ_ONLY_FIELDS, so a method chosen on 6.5 while it stayed hidden would have been silently dropped from the parameters file while item 7b drew the soma under it.

What was decided: n_real_cells_here is nullable and stores NULL on a debris row rather than 1.
Why it was decided: A stored 1 on a row that is not a cell is a number that means nothing and that a later SUM would add up, whereas NULL leaves the column summable as it stands.

What was decided: Pool.set_status derives the debris NULL from the reject reason instead of accepting it from callers.
Why it was decided: One call site forgetting to pass it would put a 1 on a non-cell row indistinguishable from a genuine single, which is why add_cell already computes n_voxels rather than trusting a caller.

What was decided: Item 7's review decisions become a frozen Decision dataclass instead of a widened tuple.
Why it was decided: A 4-tuple unpacked positionally in two files is one field insertion away from putting the note where the count goes, and nothing would raise.

What was decided: R is multiplicity-factoring in every column and every file, not only in the loss rate's numerator.
Why it was decided: A count meaning rows in one column and cells in another would leave the printed rate disagreeing with the columns printed beside it.

What was decided: real_cell_loss_rate becomes R/(C+R), dropping debris from the denominator.
Why it was decided: Debris is not a cell, so the previous R/(C+R+D) contradicted the function's own docstring and disagreed with n_real_cells, which had excluded debris since 2026-08-11.

What was decided: n_cells_confirmed and n_real_cells are emitted in export_summary.csv beside the loss rate.
Why it was decided: n_cells stays a row count, so once R counts cells no column remained from which a reader could recover the denominator and check the rate by hand.

What was decided: covered_fraction@d is left untouched by the multiplicity.
Why it was decided: It is an area, and how many cells a reviewer judges a clump to be does not change how much of the plaque's surface that clump covers.

What was decided: n_cells_within@d counts cells rather than labels, accepting that one unsplit clump can now read as clustered on its own.
Why it was decided: The user's instruction that the column be multiplicity-aware, taken with that scientific consequence stated in advance rather than discovered later.

What was decided: §9.4e's array deletion is superseded and will not be built.
Why it was decided: check_integrity reports missing_arrays for every cell row with no .npz, so deleting a debris cell's arrays would leave the pool permanently failing its own integrity check.

What was decided: The reject popup's claim that debris image data is deleted permanently is removed, and the asymmetry it draws is renamed as counting.
Why it was decided: Nothing in the codebase deletes a cell's arrays, so the sentence told every reviewer an irreversible thing had happened when it had not.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A ChoicePopup widget is built so the reason popup gains a real Cancel.
Why it was decided: ConfirmPopup returns a bool, so Escape and the window's X both returned False and were read as debris — the answer that removes the cell from every count.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The count popup's Cancel is relabelled Back and returns to the reason question instead of committing.
Why it was decided: .ask() or 1 made Cancel commit a rejection at one cell, so the same word meant abandon on the first popup and commit on the second.

What was decided: The three statements resting on §9.4e are recorded as right about the outcome and wrong about the mechanism, not as false.
Why it was decided: Rejection is still irreversible in the interface — the tile leaves the grid on mark_resolved — even though the arrays survive.

What was decided: Leaving Reject unstyled rather than colouring it red is reaffirmed after half its justification was deleted.
Why it was decided: The user re-affirmed it on being shown that the popup no longer carries the irreversibility warning the original decision had relied on.

What was decided: Item 9b's seed mask is the plaque veto as applied, dilation included, rather than products[Step.VETO].
Why it was decided: That product is undilated by contract because detect_nuclei re-applies the margin itself, so the spring-green layer drew a narrower mask than item 2 showed and seeded_ids classified against it.

What was decided: Seeded and unseeded follow the veto's dilation or erosion rather than being independent of it.
Why it was decided: The user set aside the risk that an eroded veto could collapse the seeded count, on the ground that the value is dilating most of the time.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: class_plane takes the z-window mode, shipped in the same change as item 9b's Step by batch gate.
Why it was decided: The toggle is the only writer of batch_mode, so while it was dead the mismatch between z:z+depth and window_bounds was unreachable, and enabling one without the other would have exposed it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Items 9a and 9b store the threshold as the slider's own label renders it, through ParameterSlider.as_displayed.
Why it was decided: At decimals=0 the label read 2681 while session.chosen held 2681.4372, so the hashed parameters file and the screen disagreed by exactly what the label had rounded away.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Neither a coarser exact slider nor a read-only readout is added to guard the log slider's quantisation.
Why it was decided: Storing what the label displays makes the quantisation visible on the glass and needs no control, so both remedies offered when the trade was first flagged became unnecessary.

What was decided: Item 9b's accumulating table renames its first column from grow to threshold.
Why it was decided: The column holds plaque_threshold, so grow named the mask rather than the parameter and failed to sit beside floor, which is min_plaque_volume_um3 under the same shorthand.

What was decided: The plaque outline's default weight drops to 0.15, shared by all three of its states.
Why it was decided: LAYERS derives the committed pair's weight from the plaque row and _reweight drives all three, so dimming only the provisional outline would look broken at the moment the commit is being checked.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A new screen, item 6.5 Soma Allocation Parameters, is inserted between the size cutoff and cell review.
Why it was decided: Everything on it moves the white soma at item 7b, and item 8 had refused these same fields on the ground that a mechanism must not be flipped after the cells were reviewed under a different one.

What was decided: bounded_occupancy is deleted along with soma_bound_um and soma_occupancy_theta.
Why it was decided: Those two parameters were the whole of that criterion and the only two anchor_sheet never read, so they sat in params_hash as controls that could not change anything.

What was decided: SOMA_MIN_SHEET_UM3 becomes the parameter soma_min_sheet_um3 and is offered on item 6.5.
Why it was decided: Its own tuning record is a user walking it 30 → 15 → 30 → 60 → 30 by hand-editing the source, so the number the notes twice name as the lever was the one no screen could reach.

What was decided: PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION goes 7 → 8 for the two removed and one added soma fields.
Why it was decided: All three move the Phase A hash, and a search confirmed no pool.db and no parameters file existed anywhere under the project root, so the bump orphaned nothing.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 6.5 writes its values onto the cached Derivation as well as onto session.chosen.
Why it was decided: Item 6 builds the derivation before 6.5 is reached, and payloads() measures each soma lazily from the fields the derivation carries, so writing them there costs no re-segmentation.

What was decided: Every soma parameter is plumbed from the derivation through set_cell to editing.soma_region.
Why it was decided: Item 7b drew the soma at find_soma's built-in defaults whatever the session held while the export measured the chosen values, which breaks §3b in the direction that looks correct.

What was decided: The soma boxes move out of HIDDEN_FIELDS into a read-only group of their own on item 8.
Why it was decided: Item 8's note had hidden them because no screen asked for them, and it named that as the condition for their return.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Every screen except items 1, 9a and 7b gains a Back button that goes back exactly one step.
Why it was decided: Each screen's recorded reason for having none reduced to *going back invalidates what is downstream*, which the discard rule turns into the behaviour rather than an objection.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A screen is at its defaults whether reached forwards or backwards, and Back discards everything from the target forward.
Why it was decided: The alternative, where the screen returned to keeps what was chosen, would need prepare to know its arrival direction and all twelve of its branches audited for re-entry.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Going back to item 6 or earlier clears the derivation and pays a full re-derive on the way forward.
Why it was decided: apply_cell_size_cutoff folds cells into debris in place and renumbers the survivors, so lowering the cutoff cannot restore them and the only alternative held a second 850 MB label volume.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Back raises one Yes/No confirmation, built in the driver, naming the screen returned to and what is discarded.
Why it was decided: Ten screens each raising their own would be ten chances to word it differently and one chance to forget it, and the loss at item 7a is a review pass rather than a threshold.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 8's Back is disabled once SAVE has been pressed.
Why it was decided: Before SAVE nothing exists in the pool, and after it a Back that walked away would leave a written parameters file describing cells the session no longer holds.

What was decided: BACK_FROM is derived from FLOW_ORDER minus a NO_BACK set rather than written out.
Why it was decided: A hand-kept map is a list to maintain, which is the failure this project has had to go back and repair four times.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's Back loses its exemption that nucleus edits survive the trip.
Why it was decided: The discard rule is uniform across screens, and the user confirmed the change on being shown that item 4 had been the one exception to it.

What was decided: Item 7a's Back leaves review entirely for item 6.5, discarding every triage decision and rich-review edit.
Why it was decided: Triage's pages and rich review are not steps, so back-one-step already lands on item 6.5 without a special case.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2 gains a log DAPI display toggle, off at arrival, redrawing both DAPI layers on one shared log-space ramp.
Why it was decided: It was the only one of the three screens showing DAPI to draw it linear, and it is the screen judging how much dim plaque-adjacent DAPI the veto removes.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's DAPI removed by the veto readout stays on the linear channel whatever is displayed.
Why it was decided: Log intensities do not add up to a total that means anything, so a share of total intensity is only a share in the units it was measured in.

What was decided: log1p and its limits move to preview.py, shared by items 1.5, 2 and 4.
Why it was decided: screen_background.log_view had recorded that a third caller earns the move and that there were two, and item 2's toggle is the third.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's COMMIT branch is fixed to redraw the filtered DAPI that item 1.5 committed.
Why it was decided: prepare used _dapi while the commit branch read the raw channel, so the screen showed the right DAPI on arrival and swapped to the unfiltered one exactly when COMMIT was pressed.

What was decided: The item 8 border-cell toggle is not added.
Why it was decided: remove_xy_border is already deprecated-always-False on the reasoning that dropping cells at measure time is irreversible, while touches_xy_border lets the analyst include or exclude them freely per question.

What was decided: The three voxel-count parameters are not converted to µm³ now, and are held for Phase C.
Why it was decided: They are Phase A fields on screens already walked, so the conversion moves params_hash and touches segmentation at the moment the walk is finishing.

What was decided: Fixing the voxel-space skeletonisation is assigned to Phase C rather than done now.
Why it was decided: It inflates skeleton length by 47% and adds three spurious endpoints at this study's 5.5:1 sampling, but skimage.skeletonize has no spacing parameter, so the remedy is resampling to isotropic at real memory and time cost.

What was decided: COMPONENT_STATUS.md is left untouched despite a stale row saying rejection reasons are unbuilt.
Why it was decided: That row sits inside a table the handoff already flags as an un-re-audited 2026-08-11 snapshot, and correcting one row would make the rest of it look current.

What was decided: The Bunya session takes the NVIDIA A16 GPU.
Why it was decided: Cellpose runs do_3D=False per slice, the most GPU-friendly shape there is, and rich review is the only ndisplay=3 screen, so software rendering would make rotating a cell volume painful.

What was decided: Bunya runs on the non-bare python/3.10.4-gcccore-11.3.0 module.
Why it was decided: It matches the laptop's 3.10 minor version so every cp310 wheel applies unchanged, and bare builds may omit sqlite3, which is the pool itself.

What was decided: Dependencies are frozen for Bunya in requirements-bunya.txt, with torch deliberately excluded from it.
Why it was decided: numpy 2.0.2 with cellpose 3.1.1.3 is not a set pip would resolve to by accident, and torch must be installed as the CUDA build first or cellpose picks the CPU one for you.

What was decided: A packaging test suite is added, asserting what a wheel would actually ship.
Why it was decided: The packages.find defect that shipped no UI package at all was caught by reading, and its own comment said the failure would first appear on Bunya.

What was decided: No Bunya runbook is written.
Why it was decided: The user is the only operator of the program and said so directly.

What was decided: The agenda is re-prioritised so every item is ordered by whether it blocks a Bunya install, with Phase C after.
Why it was decided: The user set the goal as getting semi-auto uploadable, installable and runnable there before any measurement or export work begins.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: min_spur_um is reviewed and left at 1.0 and off the picker screens.
Why it was decided: The sweep over 152 real cells puts 1.0 inside a plateau — 31% of branches removed with the WT/5xFAD endpoint ratio holding at ~1.98 and max branch length unchanged — and no reviewer can judge a pruning length by eye.

What was decided: The voxel-space skeleton is fixed by resampling the mask to an isotropic grid before thinning.
Why it was decided: One arm of true length 9.00 µm read between 5.40 and 11.95 µm depending only on its orientation, while an isotropic-but-coarse control got the z/x ratio right.

What was decided: The recorded "47% long, three spurious endpoints" characterisation of the defect is withdrawn rather than cited.
Why it was decided: Its fixture was two equal crossing cylinders, whose medial locus is a sheet, so the isotropic reference itself returned 2 endpoints for a 4-armed shape.

What was decided: The mask is resampled through a signed distance field in true microns onto SKELETON_TARGET_UM = 0.20.
Why it was decided: 0.20 measured 2.6% worst orientation error against 16.2% at the 0.1083 lateral pitch, and uses 0.88x the native voxel count.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Zooming the binary mask and thresholding at 0.5 is rejected as the resampler.
Why it was decided: It lost a real endpoint on 2 of 6 fixture geometries where voxel-space thinning lost none.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ndimage.zoom(grid_mode=True) is rejected in favour of the default convention with its matching spacing rule.
Why it was decided: grid_mode=True measured 10.9% orientation spread against 5.7%, despite being the tidier pairing in theory.

What was decided: The resampling target is a module constant rather than a user parameter.
Why it was decided: The user's call: it is a numerical-validity choice of the same kind as MIN_MESH_VOXELS, not a scientific knob.

What was decided: Comparability with Fiji's Skeletonize3D is knowingly given up.
Why it was decided: Fiji thins in voxel space, so matching it would mean keeping a 65.6% orientation spread in order to reproduce someone else's wrong number.

What was decided: Test fixtures are rasterised from shapes defined in microns rather than assembled from voxel boxes.
Why it was decided: rod() was physically a 0.325 µm plate and radial_fan was one-voxel wireframes, so both agreed only with a thinner that ignores physical scale.

What was decided: Per-cell 3DMorph-style figures stay unexported and write_cell_figures unwired.
Why it was decided: The user set them aside explicitly in favour of the masks — *"i am okay with no per cell image being exported like 3dmorph rightnow"*.

What was decided: Every kept cell's mask is exported as its own TIFF by a new prestomorph masks command.
Why it was decided: The masks have been on disk since Phase A and .npz is a numpy archive that Fiji, MATLAB, Imaris and 3DMorph all fail to open, so format was the entire gap.

What was decided: The exported mask is binary, not the masked intensity PrestoCell writes.
Why it was decided: Fiji's Skeletonize (2D/3D) takes a binary mask directly, while 3DMorph takes no mask at all — it reads intensity and runs its own threshold GUI — so copying PrestoCell would have served neither target.

What was decided: The full-frame label volume is not what this export writes, and write_label_image stays unwired.
Why it was decided: The unit of work in skeletonisation is one isolated cell, and the label volume is Imaris' preferred shape rather than a skeletoniser's.

What was decided: Foreground voxels are written at 255, not 1.
Why it was decided: ImageJ defines an 8-bit binary image as 0/255, and a 0/1 image skeletonises identically while opening as an almost-black frame — so the error is invisible in the output and visible only to the person.

What was decided: Every exported mask is padded by one voxel of background.
Why it was decided: The stored mask is cropped tight to its bbox so the cell touches the array edge on all six faces, and a thinning algorithm cannot tell an array face from an object face — the reason morphometrics._surface already pads before marching_cubes.

What was decided: The voxel size is embedded in each TIFF as ImageJ spacing/unit metadata.
Why it was decided: At this study's 5.5:1 anisotropy a tool assuming isotropic voxels reports a z length as an x length and nothing in an uncalibrated file contradicts it; PrestoCell embeds no voxel size in any of its three outputs.

What was decided: The masks are ImageJ TIFFs rather than the OME-TIFF write_label_image produces.
Why it was decided: Fiji reads ImageJ metadata natively with no importer dialogue, where the OME writer exists for Imaris.

What was decided: Mask export is its own command rather than a flag on export.
Why it was decided: A mask is a property of the pool — written once by Phase A, altered by no later phase, independent of any parameter set — while export's folder is keyed by params_hash and refuses without --params.

What was decided: masks/ is a sibling of exports/ rather than a child of it.
Why it was decided: An immutable ~20,000-file dataset inside a hash-keyed folder would be duplicated by every re-export.

What was decided: The cell filter is KEPT_STATUSES, not CellStatus.CONFIRMED alone.
Why it was decided: schema.KEPT_STATUSES already records that filtering on CONFIRMED alone drops every cell Phase C has run on, so the folder would come out plausibly sized and quietly incomplete.

What was decided: --include-unreviewed is offered and the empty result is stated in words rather than reported as success.
Why it was decided: PoolWriter writes every cell candidate and review --pool is not built, so a batch pool selects nothing — and an empty folder with exit 0 is exactly what that looks like from outside.
