What was decided: --params-hash narrows the export to cells holding a measurement at that hash.
Why it was decided: Measuring does not change a cell's status, so a status filter cannot express "the rows of that run's cells.csv" — the join wanted when comparing an external skeleton against this program's own.

What was decided: manifest.csv records each mask's path relative to the folder, plus bbox, voxel size and pad.
Why it was decided: The folder is normally copied to the machine running Fiji, and a skeleton point returns to whole-image coordinates only as bbox origin + point − pad.

What was decided: manifest.csv is written even when no cell matches, and a selected cell whose .npz is gone is counted and named.
Why it was decided: An empty folder with no manifest is indistinguishable from a command that never ran, and a silently short folder is how a crashed Phase A task goes unnoticed.

What was decided: The SAVED popup prints the masks command beneath the measure/export pair.
Why it was decided: The user asked for it to instruct on masks as it already instructs on carrying forward to Phase C.

What was decided: The masks command is not a third ordered step in the popup and carries no --params-hash.
Why it was decided: measure→export is a genuine order because export reads what measure wrote, whereas the masks existed before the popup was drawn — and a hash there would narrow to measured cells, of which there are none at that instant.

What was decided: SaveParametersScreen.saved is wired in app.py's generic block to show the completion popup, and close_program_requested to self.close.
Why it was decided: show_saved() had no caller anywhere in the tree, including the 2026-08-24 backup, so a finished session wrote everything correctly and then sat there with no bridge to Phase C.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The completion popup is shown with setModal(True) and show() rather than exec().
Why it was decided: exec() spins its own event loop and does not return until the dialog closes, which would hang the one headless test proving the popup appears at all.

What was decided: SavedPopup renders every line including lines[0], its own Parameters file heading.
Why it was decided: It rendered self.lines[1:], so one of the two paths the popup exists to name printed bare above a labelled Pool.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The popup's tests assert the labels the widget lays out rather than joining popup.lines.
Why it was decided: The model was correct throughout and the defect was in the view, so a test reading the model passed whatever the widget actually drew.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The guard that the popup is reachable lives in test_ui_app.py rather than beside the widget.
Why it was decided: SavedPopup's own tests called show_saved() themselves, so only the driver's suite can answer whether anything else calls it.

What was decided: The test that SAVE's arrays reach disk is written at the driver, so its payload is Derivation.payloads()'s own.
Why it was decided: A test handing add_cell three arrays it invented would prove only that store writes what it is given, which was never in doubt.

What was decided: No guard is added against pressing SAVE a second time.
Why it was decided: Measured: the same file name is refused by the collision message, and a renamed re-save rewrites the same deterministic cell_uids rather than duplicating cells.

What was decided: O2 and m8 are struck from the handoff's open-decisions list.
Why it was decided: The item list behind the handoff had recorded both closed since 2026-08-25, so they had been presented as awaiting a decision for six days after ceasing to be one.

What was decided: The soma's two mechanisms are given two radii, soma_anchor_um splitting off soma_thickness_um.
Why it was decided: Sweeping the shared number on _microglion drove the anchor from 21992 to 31360 voxels until it was 100% of the soma, and the soma grew under a stricter floor.

What was decided: soma_anchor_um defaults to soma_thickness_um's existing value of 0.9.
Why it was decided: The split adds a parameter and must not move a number, asserted by a default find_soma agreeing voxel-for-voxel with one told to couple the two radii.

What was decided: soma_anchor_um is classified Phase A.
Why it was decided: It changes soma_centroid on every stored cell record, which is the root of every branch length and both Sholl profiles.

What was decided: anchor_sheet stops reading soma_thickness_um, and item 6.5 hides that box under it.
Why it was decided: With the anchor on its own field the thickness floor is genuinely unread there, and a box left visible would let an inert value reach params_hash.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: SOMA_THICKNESS_UM_DEFAULT is promoted from ui.screen_soma into soma.py.
Why it was decided: It was the only soma default homed in the UI layer while the pipeline reads it, and the new second radius needed a coherent home beside it.

What was decided: PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION goes 8 to 9.
Why it was decided: Adding a Phase A field moves the pool hash even at identical settings, and a v8 file names no value for a field this build requires.

What was decided: A test asserts payloads hands find_soma every soma field, derived from the dataclass rather than hand-listed.
Why it was decided: Deleting anchor_um=self.soma_anchor_um left the entire suite green, so the value would have reached the screen, the parameters file and the pool key while the measured soma used a built-in default.

What was decided: No sweep is run to choose the two opening radii.
Why it was decided: There is no ground truth to score a curve against, and this project has twice read a sweep feature as structural and been wrong — the 58% to 25% cliff was z rounding and the plateau was two mechanisms cancelling.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Both radii stand at 0.9 as chosen values rather than inherited ones.
Why it was decided: The user drove the flow with the dropdown on opening and confirmed the soma drawn on item 7b.

What was decided: The 0.7 to 1.35 plateau is recorded as a cancellation rather than a structural boundary.
Why it was decided: Across it the soma median sits in a two-point band while the anchor climbs from 78% to 99% of the soma, and from 1.5 upward the anchor is the whole of it.

What was decided: Phase 2 of the opening plan, widening the sweep, is not run.
Why it was decided: soma_anchor_um is a definitional choice about how much cytoplasm counts as cell body, which more evidence of the same kind cannot settle.

What was decided: EXPORT_SPEC.md §32 gets a banner and current parameter names while §18 is left as written.
Why it was decided: §32 is live and unparked so what it names will be acted on, whereas §18 already declares every mention of the old name historical.

What was decided: soma_thickness_um's one-line summary is rewritten to describe the thickness floor.
Why it was decided: Regenerating PARAMETERS.md showed both radii carrying the same description, because the 2026-08-30 rewrite had made that line describe the anchor.

What was decided: The border-cell display filter is parked as a non-issue.
Why it was decided: The exclamation mark is already visible before entering rich review, so the reviewer can see which cells are affected without it.

What was decided: The agenda is reordered to Phase C measurement and export, then a full local run on the user's crop, with Bunya last.
Why it was decided: The user changed the sequencing so that a full run exercises finished measurement and export code rather than having to be repeated after it.

What was decided: A full suite run is required when Phase A or C is touched alongside Phase B, and targeted tests otherwise.
Why it was decided: The radius split changed executable pipeline and measurement code, unlike the comment-only bookkeeping that followed it, which correctly stayed targeted.

What was decided: min_spur_um is re-derived on the corrected skeleton and reaffirmed at 1.0.
Why it was decided: The genotype separation peaked there, 4.64 at no pruning against 5.23 at 1.0, and max branch length was untouched out to 1.5.

What was decided: The WT/5xFAD endpoint ratio is not to be cited until the anomaly is explained.
Why it was decided: WT median endpoints went 79 to 183 on the same 23 cells while 5xFAD went 40 to 35, and pruning does not separate the two candidate causes.

What was decided: A7 is fixed as its own patch before the skeletonisation build.
Why it was decided: It edits the mask both skeletons are thinned from, and separating it kept the skeletonisation work inside Phase C and on targeted tests.

What was decided: bridge_path chooses its joining pair in microns rather than in voxel indices.
Why it was decided: A pair two slices apart at 1.20 µm scored 2.0 while a genuinely nearer in-plane pair ten voxels apart at 1.083 µm scored 10.0.

What was decided: "Touching" becomes an explicit 26-adjacency test rather than any distance threshold.
Why it was decided: Passing sampling would turn the old sqrt(3) into 1.73 µm, and no micron threshold separates an in-plane corner neighbour at 0.153 µm from a z-diagonal one at 0.619 µm.

What was decided: The fabricated bridge is 0.5 µm thick in physical units, replacing BRIDGE_WIDTH_VOXELS = 3.
Why it was decided: The user's value; three voxels drew 1.8 µm through depth against 0.33 µm across, and that material is then measured as cytoplasm.

What was decided: Phase C is split into skeletonisation, measurement and export as three build stages.
Why it was decided: The existing agenda sorted into the three with almost no residue, which marks a real seam rather than an invented one.

What was decided: Two skeletons are built and kept per cell, soma-free and soma-anchored.
Why it was decided: The pair answers A2 by construction: on a detached fixture soma-free reported 6 endpoints over 2 components and the tree 4 over 1.

What was decided: GliaTrace-style minimum-spanning-tree tracing is not adopted.
Why it was decided: Its soma is excluded from the authors' own performance evaluation, zRes appears nowhere in the toolkit, and the rooted tree we already compute gives the same structural benefits.

What was decided: The soma-anchored skeleton is the shortest-path tree already returned by the existing Dijkstra.
Why it was decided: Its predecessors array was being computed and discarded, and N reachable nodes give N-1 edges so it cannot contain a cycle.

What was decided: The soma region is collapsed to a single root node.
Why it was decided: On stars of straight unbranched arms the soma-free skeleton reported 1, 3 and 3 junctions where the collapsed tree reported 0, 1 and 0, every one an artefact of the cell body.

What was decided: Branch lengths are measured from the soma surface, with no dual reporting of the centroid form.
Why it was decided: The intra-soma path adds a genotype-correlated offset, 5xFAD somata being about twice WT volume.

What was decided: The soma-anchored order is collapse then prune, reversing an earlier agreement to prune first.
Why it was decided: Pruning after the collapse applies min_spur_um to processes as they leave the cell body rather than to raw segments still holding the medial tangle.

What was decided: The soma-free order is loops then spurs.
Why it was decided: Cutting a cycle turns one arm into a dead end, and only a spur pass running afterwards can see it.

What was decided: Loops are always detected and counted, with pruning a parameter defaulting to none.
Why it was decided: Detection is lossless and pruning is not, and a loop may be two processes of one cell genuinely touching.

What was decided: Loop pruning applies to the soma-free skeleton only.
Why it was decided: The tree is acyclic by construction, and applying the rule to the shared skeleton would let the setting silently move the tree as well.

What was decided: Skeletons are stored simplified to root, junctions and tips rather than at full resolution.
Why it was decided: Full resolution is roughly 4,000 nodes per cell and 0.5-2 GB across the study, against about 220 MB simplified.

What was decided: Skeletons are stored as nodes and edges in microns, never as a voxel image.
Why it was decided: The skeleton lives on the resampled grid, so a stored voxel array would not overlay the mask and mapping back is lossy in both directions.

What was decided: Skeleton files are keyed by params_hash rather than stored beside the mask.
Why it was decided: min_spur_um and loop_prune_method both reshape a skeleton, so one run would silently overwrite another's.

What was decided: A radius is stored per node, with its refinement deferred to the measurement stage.
Why it was decided: The user's call; it is the first process-thickness data this pipeline has ever held.

What was decided: Loops are counted on the simplified graph rather than on the voxel graph.
Why it was decided: 26-connectivity makes triangles of any diagonal run, so a four-armed star with no loop at all reported 4 and an eight-armed one reported 12.

What was decided: n_junctions is counted by node degree rather than by the node's recorded role.
Why it was decided: Role survives the collapse, so an eight-armed star of straight unbranched arms reported 1 junction where the answer is 0.

What was decided: Fast-marching skeletonisation is declined despite being 3DMorph's own default.
Why it was decided: The review states it resolves only larger branches, which is the wrong trade for a phenotype carried by fine process counts.

What was decided: skeletonize is guarded against returning a silently empty skeleton.
Why it was decided: A solid 4088-voxel capsule thinned to nothing while the same array transposed gave 46 skeleton voxels.

What was decided: min_spur_um ships at 0.0 rather than 1.0.
Why it was decided: Both derivations of 1.0 are superseded, and applying no filter is more defensible than applying an unvalidated one.

What was decided: loop_prune_method becomes a real parameter immediately rather than alongside its dropdown.
Why it was decided: It changes measurement output so it must be in hash(), and adding it later would move the hash a second time and orphan any run between.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 8 gains the loop-rule dropdown directly under the spur length.
Why it was decided: The user's specification; they are the only two measurement choices that screen makes.

What was decided: human_edited correctly does not survive a re-segmentation, and the schema comment claiming otherwise was wrong.
Why it was decided: The user settled the column's meaning as whether this cell's mask was edited by a human, and re-segmentation regenerates the mask from the parameters.

What was decided: A human_edit_kind column is added, taking none, mask_edited, split or both.
Why it was decided: One boolean could say that a human touched a cell but never what they did.

What was decided: split_method is not used to populate the provenance column.
Why it was decided: It records which automatic splitter ran, so every pbc and watershed cell had no human anywhere near it.

What was decided: human_split is added as a stored field that nothing yet sets.
Why it was decided: The exported column is defined by it, and shipping with split undefined would change the column's meaning later rather than only widening its reachable values.

What was decided: The column is named human_edit_kind rather than edit_provenance.
Why it was decided: "Provenance" contains the substring "nan", which the export suite scans the whole CSV for in order to prove no NaN reaches a cell.

What was decided: avg_nearest_neighbour_um counts C + R and does not factor multiplicity.
Why it was decided: Only one of the three cells in a clumped rejection is actually the nearest, so factoring would invent two neighbours at zero distance.

What was decided: cells.csv is split into seven per-cell CSV files.
Why it was decided: 53 columns now and ninety-odd after the new measures is past what one row can be read across.

What was decided: Skeleton columns measurable on both skeletons appear on both sheets, prefixed anchored_ and free_.
Why it was decided: Both sheets carry a column called n_endpoints, unambiguous within a file and colliding the moment anyone joins them.

What was decided: human_edited is dropped from the export.
Why it was decided: human_edit_kind fully determines it, and with splitting unused the two are the same column in two spellings.

What was decided: Section, region and image index stay as a best-effort filename parse, blank when unmatched.
Why it was decided: The pattern will not hold for other users, but region is this study's own design variable since fields were chosen by anatomical region.

What was decided: A single .xlsx workbook is rejected in favour of seven separate CSVs.
Why it was decided: It is a dependency question rather than an OS one: openpyxl would have to join the 147 packages frozen for Bunya.

What was decided: The proposed eighth "miscellaneous" sheet is dropped.
Why it was decided: detached_skeleton_um was its only member and folds onto the soma-free sheet.

What was decided: mean_z_um is placed on the identity sheet.
Why it was decided: It is a fact about where the cell is rather than about signal.

What was decided: Fractal dimension and lacunarity are deferred rather than dropped.
Why it was decided: They need the 2D-versus-3D decision and a choice of lacunarity definition first, since FracLac's validation is 2D.

What was decided: The MicrogliaMorphology cluster assignment is deferred.
Why it was decided: It requires a 2D projection path, because those clusters are defined on 2D EDF projection features.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Graph betweenness centrality is held back.
Why it was decided: MMQT validated a 59-feature compound score rather than that feature on its own.

What was decided: Phase C reads the stored cell.soma_centroid wherever only a point is needed.
Why it was decided: _measure_rejected_real was calling find_soma with default parameters while every other path used the run's six, so a rejected cell's distance came from a soma nothing else in the export agreed with.

What was decided: The skeleton root keeps find_soma's centroid rather than the stored one.
Why it was decided: The root must be the centre of the region it is collapsing, so pairing a region from one call with a point from another would be a worse bug than the one being fixed.

What was decided: contact_area_um2 is measured on the surface mesh instead of counting voxel faces.
Why it was decided: The old estimate charged every surface voxel one xy face, so two boxes of equal true area measured 5.2x apart by orientation alone.

What was decided: cell_plaque_links.csv becomes C + R, carrying distance columns only.
Why it was decided: R already exported nearest_voxel_to_plaque_um, so withholding the rows published nothing less while leaving n_cells_within@d with no link-table aggregation that could reproduce it.

What was decided: polarity_index is measured on the soma-anchored tree.
Why it was decided: The free skeleton keeps detached fragments, and one of equal length behind the soma drags a true 1.0 down to 0.5.

What was decided: detached_skeleton_um is measured directly on the free artefact rather than as free minus anchored.
Why it was decided: The subtraction also contains the intra-soma path the collapse absorbs: 11.28 um against 7.02 um of real fragment on a four-armed cell.

What was decided: detached_skeleton_um returns NaN when the soma exists but holds no skeleton node, not only when there is no soma.
Why it was decided: With nothing to call attached every component counts as detached, which would report a healthy cell's whole arbour as debris.

What was decided: _link_extras takes a crop-local soma point rather than the soma object, with C and R both passing the stored centroid.
Why it was decided: R has no soma object to pass, and sharing one point makes soma_distance_um and soma_to_plaque_um unable to disagree across two files.

What was decided: Dropping hull_span_ratio and the three nucleus columns from cells_mask.csv is reaffirmed, taking it 19 to 15.
Why it was decided: FracLac's density measure is the reciprocal of ramification_index already exported two columns away, and the nucleus columns arrived unplanned in a previous session's table.

What was decided: The fork count is prefixed on both sheets while total_skeleton_um and total_length_um keep their distinct names.
Why it was decided: A fork is the same measure counted on two artefacts, which is exactly what the prefix rule covers, whereas the two length totals are genuinely different computations.

What was decided: Two test fixtures were corrected rather than the assertions that failed on them.
Why it was decided: The tests asserted the right thing and the fixtures stored no soma_centroid, which the real pipeline stamps on every cell.

What was decided: BLANK_WITH_REASON is kept as an empty dict rather than deleted.
Why it was decided: The test that stops an allow-list entry outliving its column still needs somewhere to look, and the next legitimate blank needs somewhere to be written with its reason.

What was decided: detached_skeleton_um decides "inside the soma" on the isotropic skeleton grid, not the native voxel grid.
Why it was decided: Node positions are derived on that grid and are meaningful only to half a voxel of it, and sharing it makes this test and the collapse's root test agree by construction.

What was decided: The claim that the grid change closed a wrong-number path was withdrawn before it shipped.
Why it was decided: Measured half-voxel tolerances are 5.54:1 native against 1.02:1 isotropic, but neither bound strictly dominates, so no reduction in false attachment could be demonstrated.

What was decided: A second physically-scaled test fixture was added rather than rescaling the shared one.
Why it was decided: Rescaling would have taken the fixture image from 256 KB to about 24 MB and moved every count and coordinate assertion in some ninety tests.

What was decided: The _shapes.detached_bar default radius is 0.9 um, not the process radius of 0.7.
Why it was decided: At 0.7 the fragment thins to nothing in company, so the default keeps a fixture failure from ever being mistaken for that defect.

What was decided: The skeletonize component-loss defect was pinned rather than fixed.
Why it was decided: The fix re-thins every cell in the study and every skeleton figure in the export is downstream of it, which made it the user's call rather than a follow-up.

What was decided: The defect is recorded as a strict xfail rather than a passing test asserting the broken behaviour.
Why it was decided: A green test asserting wrongness hides the defect from every run's summary and does not force whoever fixes it to come back and remove the marker.

What was decided: Three soma-to-object distances read their field by trilinear interpolation instead of rounding the centroid to a voxel.
Why it was decided: Rounding cost up to 0.29982 um in z against 0.054 in plane, while interpolation measured exact to float32 on all three axes.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The in-crop and padded-window guards were deliberately left rounding.
Why it was decided: Keeping the range test on the rounded index means no cell moves between carrying a distance and carrying a blank, so only the value improves and not the population.

What was decided: scripts/branch_point_correction.py was flagged rather than fixed or re-run.
Why it was decided: It is analysis rather than pipeline, and whether its voxel-space thinning is a live defect or correct historical scoping was left unverified.

What was decided: The link table's method gap was left unfixed, though the cost objection recorded against it was corrected.
Why it was decided: The per-plaque distance transforms it was said to require already run for n_cells_within@d, so the barrier is the stage the pairs are built in, not the cost.

What was decided: The provisional command names measure-plan and merge-measurements are kept as shipped names.
Why it was decided: Single words like plan or collect were shorter but hid the pairing with measure and merge, which is the only thing that tells a reader of a submit script which fold belongs where.

What was decided: build_manifest does one glob at the depth rule and then a case-folded suffix test, rather than one glob per extension.
Why it was decided: A directory listing at depth 3 costs the same either way, so a second pass over Lustre buys nothing and both spellings then live in one place.

What was decided: The */*/* search depth is NOT widened while fixing the .tiff extension.
Why it was decided: Measured on the RDM the same day: every one of the 573 images sits at depth 3 and the 731 .vsi sidecar files at depth 5, so widening gains nothing and reaches them.

What was decided: segment refuses an --images root that disagrees with the one recorded in the manifest.
Why it was decided: The tasks would segment the manifest's images whatever the command line said, which is the same two-sources-for-one-fact defect _roles_for_run already refuses one field over.

What was decided: That root comparison uses normpath and normcase and NOT resolve().
Why it was decided: Scratch and the RDM reach the same tree through symlinks whose real paths differ per node, and make_file_uid hashes the path as given, so resolving would refuse a run whose stored identifiers are perfectly consistent.

What was decided: An out-of-range --index prints what it found and exits 0.
Why it was decided: The second job waits on the first with --dependency=afterok, so a task exiting non-zero because the array bound was one too large would hold that job in the queue forever.

What was decided: A negative --index is refused with exit 2 instead of exiting 0 like an out-of-range one.
Why it was decided: paths[-1] is a valid Python index and the wrong image, and a negative value cannot arrive from $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID, so it is a typo and should be loud.

What was decided: Forcing --device gpu on a machine with no CUDA is honoured rather than silently falling back to CPU.
Why it was decided: Cellpose's own error names the real problem, and a silent fallback would make the override a request the program is free to ignore, which is the only thing the flag exists to rule out.

What was decided: The detection device is recorded in run_id and never added to SegmentationParams.
Why it was decided: That dataclass is hashed and the hash names the pool, so a hardware difference would put the CPU half of a study in one pool and the GPU half in another.

What was decided: The whole-image nucleus label volume is stored before it is upsampled.
Why it was decided: On a 40 x 2304 x 2304 field that is roughly 210 MB of int32 against 850 MB for an array upsample_xy restores exactly and cheaply on demand.

What was decided: MeasurementFragment exposes the same two method names Pool already carries.
Why it was decided: measure_file then writes to a fragment or to the database by being handed a different object, so there is no second path through the measuring itself for the two routes to drift apart in.

What was decided: The measurement fragment is deliberately NOT used as a context manager inside run_phase_c's loop.
Why it was decided: __exit__ writes on a clean exit and an exception caught inside the loop is a clean exit from its point of view, so a half-measured image would have been written, merged, and then looked complete.

What was decided: Phase C failures go to their own measurement_failures/<params_hash>/ directory rather than into Phase A's failures/.
Why it was decided: The two phases fail for different reasons at different times and status reports them separately, so one mixed directory would make "which images still owe me a measurement" unanswerable from the filesystem.

What was decided: A read-only Pool refuses each write method by name rather than letting sqlite raise.
Why it was decided: attempt to write a readonly database identifies none of a dozen possible callers, and a call that reached that point is a routing mistake worth naming.

What was decided: Phase C's fragments are deleted after their merge commits, and Phase A's still are NOT.
Why it was decided: Batch's resume signal is fragment existence, whereas measure's queue is the measurements table, so only one of the two can lose that file safely.

What was decided: The serial measure path needs no pinned plan and is not given one.
Why it was decided: It computes its list once in one process, so the index drift the plan exists to stop is a property of an array rather than of a loop.

What was decided: prestomorph status exits 0 whether or not work is outstanding.
Why it was decided: Outstanding work is the ordinary state between two jobs, and a non-zero exit would fail a submit script that was doing exactly the right thing.

What was decided: review --pool rebuilds a pipeline.Derivation per file instead of passing derivation=None.
Why it was decided: _persist_edits, _label_of, _on_material_taken and would_empty_a_donor all return early without one, so the pool route's rich-review edits would have silently reached nothing.

What was decided: Derivation.segmentation_filled is a zero-length array on the pool-backed route.
Why it was decided: It exists only for payloads(), which this route never calls, so an empty array makes a future caller fail loudly rather than measure n_voxels_segmentation against a volume of zeros.

What was decided: Pool review builds tiles for the unresolved cells but payloads for every cell in the file.
Why it was decided: _other_cells_around needs an already-decided neighbour's mask to find its soma and _donor_of needs it to notice a transfer, so filtering the payloads would make that neighbour invisible to both.

What was decided: Whether an edited cell moved is decided by comparing voxels, not bounding boxes.
Why it was decided: add_cell accepts whatever box a caller gives, so a cell with a loose stored box compared unequal and was stamped human_edited when nobody had touched it.

What was decided: replace_cell_mask rebuilds soma_remnant_found and agreement_score from the same find_soma call as the centroid.
Why it was decided: Three facts drawn from one computation cannot disagree, whereas a stale agreement score beside a rebuilt centroid is exactly the inconsistency the method exists to prevent.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Back in pool review ends the sitting and raises no confirmation popup.
Why it was decided: Every decision was written to the pool as it was made, so nothing is lost, unlike semi-auto where they live only in memory until item 8.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: No completion screen was written for the empty review queue; it prints one line and closes.
Why it was decided: No built screen says an empty queue is a success state, and inventing one would be a new visual element, which is a standing stop-and-ask on this project.

What was decided: Pool.create_cell and Pool.delete_cell are NOT built alongside replace_cell_mask.
Why it was decided: Cell splitting in batch review is out of scope, and that is the whole of what those two methods served in this component.

What was decided: COMPONENT_05_PLAN §9.4c is NOT built, and the operational rule is not to re-run merge on a reviewed pool.
Why it was decided: The handoff scoped this build to replace_cell_mask only, and widening preserve_cell is a decision about what a deliberate re-segmentation may overwrite, which is the user's to take.

What was decided: review and interactive reach ui/ through one shared _ui_entry_points helper.
Why it was decided: test_ui_boundary.py asserts cli.py holds exactly one import from the interface, and two lazy imports would have been two doors rather than one door used twice.

What was decided: _cmd_stub is deleted and its two tests rewritten to assert the opposite.
Why it was decided: review was its last caller, so the stub became dead code the moment the pool-backed route landed.

What was decided: The handoff's stated test baseline of 1706 is overturned in favour of 1804.
Why it was decided: PROJECT_LOG.md §66, written the same day as the handoff, records 1804, so the 98 between them are the 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 work rather than this build's.

What was decided: docs/PARAMETERS.md is NOT regenerated.
Why it was decided: SegmentationParams was not changed by this build, and tests/test_parameters_doc.py passing is what confirms the generated file is still in sync.

What was decided: COMPONENT_04_PLAN §4's open question 4 on per-image walltime stays open.
Why it was decided: It needs a measured Cellpose time on gpu_cuda at the full 2304 x 2304, which is a measurement to be taken on the first real run rather than a decision to be made.

What was decided: COMPONENT_04_PLAN §5a's "one pool, cells flagged" is overturned as stale, and segment now refuses a semi-auto pool.
Why it was decided: COMPONENT_03_PLAN §4a.3 and §4a.9 had already replaced it with two pools and the code followed the newer decision, so the line said the opposite of what the program does.

What was decided: An image with no CD68 channel runs end to end — item 9a is skipped in semi-auto, its parameters are inert in batch, and every CD68 measure exports blank.
Why it was decided: cd68_channel was already int | None with None meaning *this image has no such channel*, so the state was representable everywhere downstream and only the interface crashed on it.

What was decided: CD68 absence is a study-level statement rather than a per-image one.
Why it was decided: cd68_channel is a Phase A field, so a CD68-free run takes a different phase_a_hash and its own pool — a half-and-half study could not be merged into one export.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: No banner, confirmation line or extra dropdown value is added at intake to declare CD68 absent.
Why it was decided: Assigning no channel to cd68 already is the declaration, and the user accepted that forgetting and deciding then look identical rather than add a second way to say one thing.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's "CD68 in" column shows an em dash when there is no CD68 channel.
Why it was decided: commit_result fell back to 0.0, and 0.0% containment is a plausible finding on the screen whose whole purpose is judging containment.

What was decided: Item 5's "CD68 in" column is not dropped when CD68 is absent.
Why it was decided: The table accumulates one row per commit under a fixed header, so a column that came and went would make the table's width follow the session.

What was decided: NO_BACK becomes derived — INTAKE plus the first applicable step after REVIEW.
Why it was decided: With CD68 present the first step after review is still 9a, so the full flow is provably unchanged and the skip case falls out of the same function rather than a second code path.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Back from item 9b does not lead to REVIEW when 9a is skipped.
Why it was decided: Re-entering review after leaving it would mean re-deciding cells that were already decided, which is the property NO_BACK exists to protect.

What was decided: The flow skips item 9a only when roles are declared and lack cd68, never when roles is empty.
Why it was decided: An empty roles means intake has not run rather than that a decision was made, and has_roles() already refuses to leave item 1 without it.

What was decided: Per-cell cd68_status reads no_cd68_channel while every CD68 value column stays blank.
Why it was decided: image_cd68_status and debris_cd68_status already name the reason, and a blank status beside blank values cannot be told from a measurement that failed.

What was decided: Item 8 prints not set — no CD68 channel assigned rather than plain not set.
Why it was decided: Reaching item 9a and leaving the slider untouched is a different fact from having no channel, and both printed identically.

What was decided: cells_cd68.csv is still written, with its full schema and blank values.
Why it was decided: A fixed schema is what lets a CD68-free export be read by the same tooling as any other; omitting the file would make the file set follow the data.

What was decided: load_params does not refuse a null cd68_channel alongside a non-null cd68_threshold.
Why it was decided: The params_hash check already refuses a hand-edited file and skipping item 9a stops the semi-auto route producing the pair, so the combination is made inert rather than an error.

What was decided: 6E10/plaque is not made optional in the same change, despite carrying the identical defect.
Why it was decided: Wiring it would pull in item 2's veto and item 4's DAPI suppression as well as item 9b, widening the testing surface for a hole the user chose to leave open and known.

What was decided: The change is not verified by an end-to-end run on a real image.
Why it was decided: Targeted tests after each build bit plus one full suite were accepted as sufficient evidence, and the user waived the real run.

What was decided: The build proceeds bit by bit with targeted tests after each, one full suite after the last, and bookkeeping only after that.
Why it was decided: Bookkeeping written during a build records intentions rather than outcomes, and this project requires a count to belong to a dated event.

What was decided: docs/COMPONENT_03_PLAN.md is not amended for the flow change.
Why it was decided: It carries no mention of the DAPI Background Filter or Soma Allocation screens either, so flow changes have not been written back to it since the GUI build began.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The build waits for the concurrent patch session to finish before any file is touched.
Why it was decided: There is no git, so two sessions editing one file means the later write silently wins and the earlier work is unrecoverable.

What was decided: The contrast-limit memo is keyed on array identity guarded by a weakref that evicts on death.
Why it was decided: CPython recycles an address after a collection, so a bare id key can hand one channel's ramp to another, and a stale key serving a wrong preview is the one failure a preview cannot have.

What was decided: preview.reset_limit_cache() is added as a test-only hook.
Why it was decided: set_volume ends in draw(), so a test written without a reset counts zero percentile calls and passes against the unfixed code.

What was decided: The contrast memo's tests are not filed with preview's other tests in test_ui_screen_threshold1.py.
Why it was decided: That file is not in the item's targeted set, so its own regression would sit outside the tests the handoff says to run.

What was decided: The contrast memo holds eight entries.
Why it was decided: Six layers on the widest screen plus a spare, and an entry is two floats and a weak reference.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's "project first" is implemented as slicing the z window first and computing on that window.
Why it was decided: max(where(veto, dapi, 0)) is not where(max(veto), max(dapi), 0), so combining projected planes lets a bright unvetoed voxel into the overlay above depth 1.

What was decided: log_view moves onto the projected plane while the contrast limits stay on the whole volume.
Why it was decided: log1p after a clip at zero is monotone so the picture is identical, and windowed limits would restretch the ramp under the judgement on every z step.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's DAPI-removed readout is memoised by object identity rather than an id stamp.
Why it was decided: The two arrays compared are ones the screen already holds, so an address cannot be recycled underneath the comparison.

What was decided: Item 2's Otsu threshold is held in one slot keyed on the plaque channel object plus its coefficient.
Why it was decided: A session holds one plaque channel, so a second slot could only ever hold the previous image's, and keying on the coefficient alone would serve the next file the wrong mask.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Typing on item 1.5 is asserted to leave the derived layers invisible rather than zeroed.
Why it was decided: Their data only reached zeros through the redraw the item removes, and both toggles are disabled, so the stale array is unreachable until the next draw zeroes it.

What was decided: Item 6 holds the field projection and the finished border outline, not the intermediate ring.
Why it was decided: The ring has no other consumer, so keeping it would be a third piece of state able to go stale.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's microglial readout stays live on every slider step while only the redraw waits for release.
Why it was decided: It is a comparison over the roughly 35 membership fractions the commit already computed, and it is the feedback the threshold is actually chosen by.

What was decided: Two existing membership-slider tests now emit sliderReleased after set_value.
Why it was decided: Seven existing call sites already drive items 3, 5, 9a and 9b that way, and making set_value itself recompute would restore the per-step cost the item removes.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's per-step redraw is guarded on was_committed.
Why it was decided: Item 3's _invalidate_view already establishes that the redraw exists only to swap committed panels back, and after the first step there is nothing left to swap.

What was decided: Item 9a's mask reuse is asserted by call count plus contents rather than array identity.
Why it was decided: set_channels stores np.asarray(cells).astype(bool), which always copies, so an identity assertion could never hold.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The two whole-volume bool casts are deleted rather than moved after the window slice.
Why it was decided: outline_of_batch's own any(axis=0) already treats nonzero as true, so the cast has no work left once it is not applied to the whole volume.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: WindowCache lives in cache.py and the window-mode dispatch lives in viewer.cached_plane.
Why it was decided: Placement rule 4a.7 puts headless compute reuse outside ui/, and duplicating the window bounds in cache.py is the two-windowings trap task 27 recorded.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: ProjectionCache serves only raw max-projection layers, with derived layers on the LRU in both modes.
Why it was decided: It computes volume[window].max(0) and nothing else, so it cannot produce an outline, a np.where or a threshold.

What was decided: Depth 1 is never cached.
Why it was decided: A single slice is free, and depth 1 is the one place batch_plane and batch_projection disagree about whether the answer is a plane or the volume.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The rolling window cache holds four positions per layer rather than a shared entry count.
Why it was decided: All 31 positions of one layer is 657 MB at production width, and a shared bound would let one layer evict another layer's half of the same picture.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Each cached layer's source array is tracked beside the key instead of being hashed into it.
Why it was decided: The specified key names the layer, z, depth and mode but not the volume, so a commit's new mask would otherwise be served the previous one's planes.

What was decided: The nucleus cache holds the whole NucleiResult, not just the label array.
Why it was decided: segment_image uses .summary() for its batch log line as well as .labels, so the reuse path prints what the computed path would.

What was decided: NucleusCache is its own class carrying a peek rather than a reused SliceCache.
Why it was decided: A miss in derive must mean let segment_image detect for itself, not run Cellpose a second time, which a compute-callback API cannot express.

What was decided: segment_image gains five optional precomputed arguments, each with its own fallback.
Why it was decided: Batch passes none of them and is byte-identical, which is what keeps 6.1's reproducibility gate at one implementation rather than two routes.

What was decided: derive no longer releases the session's channels before segmenting.
Why it was decided: Handing the arrays over is one copy where releasing and re-reading was also one copy, minus five full channel reads, so the memory rule is honoured rather than overturned.

What was decided: PipelineCompute._detection_params becomes the single source for item 4, the cache key and item 6.
Why it was decided: detect read session.chosen while the key read session_params, whose display whitelist drops downsample and normalize — the exact shape of a cache handing segment_image labels at a resolution it is not expecting.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's two channel planes and item 9b's seed projection are passed the screen's own batch_mode.
Why it was decided: Both took the default rolling window while their outlines used the screen's mode, so ticking Step by batch drew the two halves of one picture from different slabs of the stack.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Back evacuates the canvas to the app and hides it, clearing canvas_home with it.
Why it was decided: The discarded screen's C++ destructor was taking napari's _qt_viewer with it, which aborts the process rather than raising, and a cleared home stops the next placement touching a dead host.

What was decided: The soma-delete catch-all reports the caller's own status rather than new wording.
Why it was decided: The soma is named explicitly before the guarded call, and inventing user-facing text is the user's call rather than the builder's.

What was decided: SaveParametersScreen exposes its inner column.
Why it was decided: Wrapping the form in a scroll area makes screen.layout() the outer wrapper, and an existing test walks the form's order to place the divider.

What was decided: Triage's undo emits the uids it restored.
Why it was decided: A sweep of the grid's resolved flags cannot tell a cell that was never decided from one that has just been undecided.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The tile delete button asks its popups on the grid and records its decision on ReviewStep.
Why it was decided: The click happens on the grid, and every other decision in the program is recorded on ReviewStep.

What was decided: _decision_from is shared between rich review's resolution and the grid's rejection.
Why it was decided: Those four lines have already been wrong once, reading the storage names and recording a debris rejection as a confirmed cell.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The triage tile is not widened for the delete button.
Why it was decided: Measured: the glyph at 18 px pinned left plus the centred mark pair fits inside the existing 96 px, so no tile and no grid column moves.

What was decided: A rejection taken from the triage grid is undoable, overturning the plan's claim that rejection is irreversible within a session.
Why it was decided: It carries a TriageAction and nothing is destroyed until item 8, so undo returns the tile, drops the decision and repaints one crop.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: _capture gains a where argument and four tests patch the popup class in widgets.
Why it was decided: Patching it in the old namespace let the screen build a real dialog, and exec_() with no display hangs the suite rather than failing it.

What was decided: Writing pool.csv is never allowed to fail a merge.
Why it was decided: The merge has already committed by then, and a file left open in a spreadsheet on a network share is the ordinary way the write fails.

What was decided: pool.csv is rewritten on every exit from merge-measurements, including both early returns.
Why it was decided: Nothing new to merge is exactly the case where the file on disk is a Phase A snapshot whose statuses have all since moved.

What was decided: The pool.csv writer refuses to open a pool that does not exist.
Why it was decided: Connecting creates the database file, so writing the CSV could otherwise leave an empty pool behind.

What was decided: The measured values are not added to pool.csv.
Why it was decided: They are cells.csv's, keyed by parameter set, and two homes for one figure is two answers to one question.

What was decided: The masks folder name is defined once as export.MASKS_DIR.
Why it was decided: cli.py may make only one crossing into ui/, so the alternative was a third literal — and a literal in three places is how the two mask routes drifted apart.

What was decided: export --with-masks writing to the parent of --out is confirmed and built.
Why it was decided: After the export path loses its duplicated hash, that parent is the output root, so both mask routes land on the identical folder.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's hand edits are reaffirmed not to reach the numbers, by construction.
Why it was decided: edited_labels copies before mutating, and the only writer that could reach the pushed view — napari's paint brush — is unreachable because the embedded widget carries the canvas and z slider without the layer controls.

What was decided: The empty directory left by merge-measurements is measurement_fragments/ itself, not the per-hash folder the handoff named.
Why it was decided: Measured on a real merge before touching it: the per-hash folder has been removed since that function was written.

What was decided: The parameters file's hidden-field gap is recorded rather than fixed in this patch.
Why it was decided: It is unreachable while no screen writes downsample or normalize, and it is a screen_save question rather than one of the patch's items.

What was decided: No suite runtime figure is carried forward.
Why it was decided: Three measured full runs are 361 s, 817 s and 361 s, a spread larger than any change the code has made.

What was decided: The build runs as three phases, one item at a time, with targeted tests per item, a wider set per phase, the full suite once at the end, and bookkeeping only after everything is green.
Why it was decided: Written as the handoff's working rule so a green targeted run cannot be mistaken for a green suite, and so no record is written of a result the tests have not yet produced.

What was decided: Contrast and log limits are memoised per volume identity in preview.py instead of recomputed inside every draw().
Why it was decided: Measured on a production field the three np.percentile calls cost 3.43 s, 2.41 s and 3.57 s, and items 1.5, 2, 4 and 7b all made them per redraw.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's draw projects the z window first and applies log_view, np.where and the outline to the plane.
Why it was decided: One arrow key cost ~35 s and allocated 3–4 GB of transient arrays, and items 4 and 9b already state the project-first rule.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's DAPI removed readout is computed once when the veto changes rather than on every draw.
Why it was decided: It is a whole-field number and cannot move on a z step.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 2's plaque Otsu threshold is memoised on plaque_veto_coefficient so COMMIT reuses what arrival computed.
Why it was decided: Arrival and COMMIT each paid the same ~17 s threshold when only plaque_dilate_um had moved.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 1.5's commit-gated boxes stop calling draw() on every keystroke.
Why it was decided: Typing cost ~9.4 s a character, and it was the only screen in the flow whose gated boxes redrew — items 2, 3, 4 and 5 only invalidate.

What was decided: Item 6 computes the field projection, border ring and outline once in set_cells, and the cutoff box stays live.
Why it was decided: self.labels is set once and the cutoff is applied on the way out, so np.bincount at 2.63 s and find_objects at 0.68 s were rebuilding a constant per keystroke.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's membership slider recomputes on sliderReleased, with its value label and _sync still live on every step.
Why it was decided: value_changed fires on all 1000 slider steps and each redraw cost ~5 s, so a drag queued hundreds of them.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 4's microglial readout stays live on every slider step.
Why it was decided: It is a comparison over the few hundred fractions the commit already computed, and it is the number the threshold is chosen by.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's coefficient slider takes item 3's was_committed guard, and item 3's drag test is ported to it.
Why it was decided: Item 3 already refuses to recompute mid-drag, and item 5 was paying two cache-missing 0.25 s preview_mask calls per step.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 9a thresholds the projected plane and reads products[Step.THRESHOLD_2] on arrival.
Why it was decided: Thresholding the whole volume then projecting cost 1.01 s against 0.106 s, and item 5's commit already stored the measurement mask with nothing reading it.

What was decided: The whole-volume .astype(bool) copies in items 4 and 5 are removed rather than moved.
Why it was decided: outline_of_batch's own any(axis=0) already treats nonzero as true, so the cast was copying the volume before the window was sliced out of it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The projection cache serves both window modes — ProjectionCache for batched, a SliceCache LRU for rolling.
Why it was decided: The user uses both modes, and precomputing all 31 rolling positions is 657 MB per layer at production width.

What was decided: Cellpose's result is cached in memory for the session, keyed on the detection parameter subset.
Why it was decided: Item 4's COMMIT and item 6's derive run detection at the same parameters minutes apart, and the labels are already in RAM.

What was decided: No persistent on-disk nucleus cache is built.
Why it was decided: Batch already runs Cellpose once per image, so a disk tier would only survive a program restart while adding a lifetime and a clean-up inside the user's output folder.

What was decided: Batch does not write to the nucleus cache.
Why it was decided: Each batch run sees every image once, so the entries would pay off only on a re-run at different downstream parameters.

What was decided: derive reuses the committed threshold and veto products and the channels already in memory, instead of session.release() and five disk reads.
Why it was decided: Compute.detect already reuses items 2 and 3's committed masks for the same reason, so this is the established pattern rather than a new one.

What was decided: Rich review's editing frame stays cut at the margin slider's 20 µm maximum.
Why it was decided: The reviewer must be able to edit out to the full allowance, which is worth more than the decomposition cost it carries.

What was decided: Item 4's hand edits still do not reach the numbers.
Why it was decided: Semi-auto is used only to set parameters for batch, so the edits are a way of seeing whether detection is good enough.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The Back crash is fixed by evacuating the canvas to the app before the screen holding it is discarded.
Why it was decided: setParent(None) on the outgoing screen destroyed napari's _qt_viewer with it, and the headless suite cannot reach it because RecordingViewer has no widget to reparent.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Back's behaviour is not changed, only its crash.
Why it was decided: Flow.discard_from already delivers the "arrive as if fresh" semantics that were asked for again this session.

What was decided: Deleting the soma is refused by an explicit check and a catch-all behind it, both routed through report_unavailable.
Why it was decided: CellEditor.remove already raised correctly, but an unhandled exception in a Qt slot under PyQt6 calls qFatal() and aborts the process.

What was decided: Item 5 pushes a zero plane for an absent CD68 channel.
Why it was decided: Panel assignment is by layer index at stride=3, so skipping the two CD68 layers moved Iba1 out of the right-hand panel; item 1.5 already pushes zeros for exactly this.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's CD68 picker row is not greyed out when the channel is absent.
Why it was decided: The zero plane fixes the picture, and an inert row is harmless.

What was decided: Item 8's column is wrapped in a QScrollArea.
Why it was decided: Its 23 read-only rows plus the controls put SAVE and Back off the bottom of the Bunya desktop.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The frames' right-hand control columns are not made scrollable.
Why it was decided: Item 8 is the screen that actually failed, so the rest is recorded as a known hole rather than fixed.

What was decided: Triage gets a delete button on every tile, drawn as × at the !'s size and pinned to one side, running rich review's two reject popups.
Why it was decided: The bundled IBM Plex Sans has no trashcan, no U+232B and no U+2716, and the interface refuses to substitute a font.

What was decided: A painted trashcan icon is not drawn.
Why it was decided: × is in the bundled font and is one character rather than a vector path to maintain.

What was decided: A triage deletion is undoable, and its tile leaves the grid immediately.
Why it was decided: Nothing is destroyed until item 8, so the decision can still be taken back.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Triage's undo is fixed once for both bulk accepts and deletions, dropping the decisions and restoring the scene.
Why it was decided: undo() only cleared the resolved flags, so twenty accepted cells came back on screen and stayed recorded confirmed for item 8 to write.

What was decided: masks resolves the single measured parameter set itself and refuses, naming them, when the pool holds several.
Why it was decided: Without --params-hash it wrote 12 TIFFs and zero skeletons with the manifest's four skeleton columns blank in every row, and export_pool already refuses the same way.

What was decided: Item 8's generated masks command carries --params-hash.
Why it was decided: export_command already emits it, and the reason for omitting it was true only at the moment item 8 is shown.

What was decided: Item 8's export command drops the redundant hash folder from --out.
Why it was decided: The path came out as exports/835a98debb6f/export_20260903_835a98de/, naming the same run twice.

What was decided: pool.csv is written at the end of merge and rewritten at the end of merge-measurements.
Why it was decided: Pool.export_csv existed with no callers, and a Phase A snapshot goes stale the moment anyone reviews a cell.

What was decided: pool.csv does not carry the measured values.
Why it was decided: Those are cells.csv's and are keyed by parameter set, so holding them in both creates a second answer to one question.

What was decided: The emptied measurement_fragments/ folder is removed after the merge.
Why it was decided: It was the only empty directory left anywhere in the output.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The SAVED popup is reworded to say masks are available any time and skeletons once the run has been measured.
Why it was decided: Once masks resolves the parameter set itself the same command writes SWCs after measuring, which the old wording did not mention.

What was decided: Both mask routes write into output_root/masks, with --with-masks using Path(args.out).parent / "masks".
Why it was decided: The two routes produced identical content in two places, so anyone who tried both ended up with two copies.

What was decided: _detection_params becomes the single source for every field in the nucleus cache key.
Why it was decided: session_params filters chosen through a display whitelist that turns downsample=4 into 2 and normalize='none' into 'log', so the key and the computation named different runs.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 5's channel planes and item 9b's seed layer are made to honour their own window mode.
Why it was decided: Each drew two halves of one picture from different slabs of the stack above depth 1, and the projection cache is keyed on the mode.

What was decided: The handoff's claim that measurement_fragments/<params_hash>/ survives the merge is overturned.
Why it was decided: Measured before the change: the per-hash folder was already being removed, and the parent is what survives.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: show_step releases the outgoing screen's WindowCache.
Why it was decided: release() was written and called by nothing, and five screens visited at depth 10 held ~1.3 GB of planes for the length of the session.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: WindowCache._track holds a weak reference per source rather than an id() stamp alone.
Why it was decided: A freed array's address is handed to its replacement in 4 of 5 trials at these sizes, and preview._cached_limits already guards the identical hazard.

What was decided: The remove catch-all gets its own note, "That cannot be removed. Nothing was changed.", and removal refusals are titled "Cannot remove that".
Why it was decided: It borrowed the caller's take status, so a refused deletion was explained as a refused take under a title naming a gesture the reviewer had not attempted.

What was decided: The parameters file's use of plain session_params is left unfixed.
Why it was decided: It could record a hidden detection field the run did not use, but no screen writes those fields and no downsample control is planned.

What was decided: The stale build/, prestomorph.egg-info/, .pytest_cache/ and __pycache__/ artefacts are deleted from the Bunya copy before it is uploaded.
Why it was decided: Every file in build/ was verified mirrored in the source tree, and stale bytecode beside new source is how an install appears to change nothing.

What was decided: OMP_NUM_THREADS is set before the device is resolved in batch.main, not after it.
Why it was decided: resolve_device(None) calls gpu_available, which imports torch, so on the default --device auto the variable was reaching a pool that already existed.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 7a is wrapped in a whole-screen scroll area like the other twelve, reversing the exclusion taken the same day.
Why it was decided: The grid's own bar scrolls the grid, leaving the button bar at the bottom of the screen unreachable on a window taller than the display.

What was decided: The tile grid is given a floor of GRID_ROWS (4) rows rather than being wrapped on its own.
Why it was decided: A scroll area shrinks to almost nothing, so without a floor the body's minimum stays tiny and the outer bar has nothing to scroll.

What was decided: That floor is a minimum height rather than a fixed one.
Why it was decided: The grid keeps its stretch factor, so a tall display still shows more than four rows, where a fixed height would cap a large monitor at twenty tiles.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: self.scroll means the whole-screen area on all thirteen screens, and FrameE's grid area is renamed grid_scroll.
Why it was decided: _scroll_areas looks scroll up by name, so without the rename it would go on reporting the grid as the screen's area.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Both of triage's scrollbars are always shown, and its header scrolls with the content.
Why it was decided: A bar that is only sometimes there is one a reviewer cannot rely on grabbing, and a scrolling title is what the other twelve screens already do.

What was decided: row_px is passed from screen_triage into FrameE rather than the tile constants being copied into frames.
Why it was decided: screen_triage imports from frames, so the constants cannot travel back without an import cycle, and a copy would drift the first time a tile changed size.

What was decided: The full suite was not re-run for the 7a and A2 fixes.
Why it was decided: The batch change is a statement reordering inside one function and FrameE has exactly one construction site, and 422 targeted tests covered both areas green.

What was decided: test_triage_is_not_wrapped_a_second_time was inverted rather than deleted.
Why it was decided: It existed to pin the exclusion being reversed, so the reversal has to be visible in the same place the decision was.

What was decided: HANDBACK_PATCH_CPU.md was amended in place with supersession markers rather than rewritten.
Why it was decided: It records what that session decided and why, so silently correcting it would destroy the reasoning a later reader needs.

What was decided: No guard was added to Pool.array_path checking the file_uid it is handed.
Why it was decided: cell_uid is <file_uid>__c<n> and the path names the file id twice, so a mismatch cannot return another cell's arrays — it can only miss.

What was decided: prestomorphspeedtest ships docs/EXPORT_SPEC.md and docs/PARAMETERS.md.
Why it was decided: They are test inputs rather than prose, and without them nine tests skip instead of passing, which is a weaker check of an install.

What was decided: BUNYA.md is not shipped in prestomorphspeedtest.
Why it was decided: The user asked for that folder to carry no installation instructions.

What was decided: No parameters file is shipped in prestomorphspeedtest.
Why it was decided: Batch will not be run before semi-auto, and semi-auto is what writes that file.

What was decided: prestomorph/export.writers.bak is dropped from the deployment copy.
Why it was decided: It is a working-tree artefact that bunya test never shipped, and nothing imports it.

What was decided: measure_cell_entry.py's stub gains _neighbour_soma and an empty _soma_cache.
Why it was decided: B7 routed _other_cells_around through the cache, so the pre-patch script raises AttributeError on the first cell against patched code.

What was decided: test_the_thread_count_is_printed_and_recorded_in_the_run_id pins gpu_available to False.
Why it was decided: It hardcoded cpu in the expected run_id, so it was asserting the machine has no GPU, and it failed on Bunya with aim2:cuda:16t.

What was decided: The debris patch's new measurement-threshold object floor is named mask_min_object_voxels.
Why it was decided: It matches the mask_coefficient and mask_closing_radius_um pair already naming that mask's parameters, and a field name reaches the parameters file and the pool key permanently, so an established convention beats a fresh coinage.

What was decided: CD68 integrated within debris is computed in Phase A, so segment_image reads the CD68 channel for the first time.
Why it was decided: The figure belongs on the file record and the file record is written at Phase A, while the alternatives — persisting a ~212 MB debris mask per field for Phase C, or re-implementing the split there — both cost far more than one channel read that is summed and dropped.

What was decided: Whether assign_labels_by_connectivity is repurposed or deleted is deferred until item A of the debris patch is built.
Why it was decided: It has its own twelve-test file, two screen docstrings quote it and scripts/sweep_morphometrics.py is a live caller, so whether its orphan-component logic genuinely serves debris identification is a question only the built code can answer.

What was decided: Cells removed by remove_xy_border, and components cut by the new measurement-mask object floor, are not counted as debris.
Why it was decided: HANDOFF_PATCH_DEBRIS.md defines debris as exactly the components no microglial nucleus claims plus cells under min_cell_volume_um3, and widening that mid-patch would move a definition the user settled in discussion.

What was decided: soma_thickness_um stays at 0.9 after re-derivation on the fixed ruler.
Why it was decided: The sweep shows a plateau from 0.7 to 1.2 um where the median soma fraction moves under 2 points, bounded below at 0.7 (31.4% rising to 38.7% at 0.6 as the erosion starts claiming processes) and above at ~1.35 where mechanism 2 stops contributing.

What was decided: The re-derived value is NOT raised above 0.9 as EXPORT_SPEC.md predicted.
Why it was decided: The prediction was that the fixed ruler would retain depth and push the answer higher, but at T >= 1.65 the soma fraction equals the anchor fraction exactly, so raising it deletes the erosion term rather than enlarging it.

What was decided: The 0.7-1.2 plateau is recorded as cancellation between the two mechanisms, not as robustness.
Why it was decided: soma_thickness_um sizes the anchor and sets the erosion floor at once and they move in opposite directions: across the sweep the anchor median rises 17.0% to 34.7% while mechanism 2 falls from 29.6 points to zero.

What was decided: soma_anchor_um will be added so the anchor radius and the erosion floor are separate parameters, defaulting to the same value.
Why it was decided: The sweep confirmed sweep_soma_thickness.py's own prediction that the two mechanisms want two radii; with one parameter neither curve can be read on its own.

What was decided: sweep_soma_thickness.py gains an explicit --method, defaulted to opening.
Why it was decided: It called find_soma without a method and so inherited anchor_sheet after the 2026-08-30 default change, silently sweeping a mechanism that reads thickness_um only to size the anchor.

What was decided: The sweep table's header order was corrected to follow the data it prints.
Why it was decided: The row appends the old-ruler column before the anchor column while the header listed them the other way round, mislabelling both in every run with the old-ruler column enabled.

What was decided: SOMA_THICKNESS_UM_DEFAULT moves into soma.py and is imported everywhere else.
Why it was decided: 0.9 is a bare literal in seven places across pipeline.py, phasec.py, soma.py, ui/editing.py and ui/screen_soma.py, while the other three soma parameters are already module constants imported from soma.py.

What was decided: The containment defect is downgraded from a blocking fix to documented-and-monitored.
Why it was decided: No cell exceeded 100% of its own volume at any threshold from 0.4 to 2.0 um on real cells; the 108% case that raised it was synthetic.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: soma_sheet_area_um2 and soma_min_sheet_um3 are frozen rather than walked against the screen again.
Why it was decided: The record shows 16 to 8 to 6 to 4 to 5 and 30 to 15 to 30 to 60 to 30 converging on nothing, and the CD68 literature review found the field has no convention for the soma/process split to converge on.

What was decided: A corridor distance cap will be added to anchor_sheet.
Why it was decided: On cell 3 the spurious component is 135 um3 at 19.4 um from the nucleus against a real body component of 131 um3 at 0.5 um, so the artefact is larger than the body and no size floor can separate them.

What was decided: agreement_score and the corridor's minimum cross-sectional area will be exported.
Why it was decided: Both are already computed and discarded, and the CD68 review names nucleus centring and junction continuity as its two primary diagnostics for telling true somatic hypertrophy from a tethered process segment.

What was decided: CD68 stays measured over the whole cell mask rather than being restricted to the soma - reaffirmed.
Why it was decided: The review's question is whether the CD68-dense zone is soma at all, so a soma-restricted measure would encode the answer into the measurement.

What was decided: Soma volume will be split into anchor-contributed and mechanism-2-contributed shares per genotype.
Why it was decided: The review reports reactive cells carry short thick processes and the shipped 5 um2 sheet threshold is a 2.5 um disc, so the criterion may absorb process into soma preferentially in 5xFAD and inflate the genotype difference it is used to measure.

What was decided: The cohort will be run under both soma methods and reported as a sensitivity analysis.
Why it was decided: opening is the mechanism with published precedent, so agreement between the two carries more weight than either alone.

What was decided: The AUC figures are not treated as validation of any soma criterion.
Why it was decided: The labels are a distance-to-nucleus proxy - beyond 5 um counted as process, within 1.5 um as body - not traced somata, so they rank criteria against each other without validating any of them.

What was decided: Reporting the morphological opening rather than the raw eroded remnant is reaffirmed.
Why it was decided: The remnant understates the soma by a shape-dependent amount, so its bias would track the very morphology under comparison.

What was decided: The patch-2 measure/export build was halted partway through bit 1 and prestomorph/phasec.py reverted to its pre-patch state, with no tests run.
Why it was decided: The user stopped the session mid-edit, and with no git in the tree a hand reversal verified back at 905 lines, the original _link_extras signature and a clean import was the only way to leave the tree in a known state.

What was decided: The in-flight change making _link_extras take a soma centroid point instead of a SomaResult object was not kept.
Why it was decided: The build stopped before bit 3 gave that signature its only new consumer, so retaining it would have left a parameter change with nothing calling it.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Embed ONE napari canvas and re-parent it into whichever screen is showing, rather than giving each of the seven viewer screens its own viewer.
Why it was decided: Seven viewers is seven OpenGL contexts and seven copies of the layers beside a 3.17 GiB image, and the flow already guarantees exactly one screen is visible at a time.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: A screen with no picture leaves the canvas parked in the previous screen instead of re-parenting it out.
Why it was decided: setParent(None) turns a widget into a top-level window, which is the stray napari window this task exists to remove.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Declare each screen's panel arrangement as data on the class (viewer.CanvasLayout) and let the flow driver apply it on every arrival.
Why it was decided: Grid and ndisplay are viewer state, not screen state, and a screen is built once but shown many times.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Make NapariViewer(show=False) the default and expose the canvas through the private window._qt_viewer rather than the public qt_viewer property.
Why it was decided: With the canvas embedded, a visible napari window is the canvas being in the wrong place.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Clear the viewer of all layers on every screen arrival.
Why it was decided: Nothing else removed a layer, so each screen inherited every earlier screen's. napari assigns grid panels by layer index, and item 6's Labels layer named 'cells' collided with item 9a's image layer of the same name, so item 9a would not open at all.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Call reset_view() when a screen arrives, and call it after the grid and ndisplay are set rather than before.
Why it was decided: napari fits the camera only when the first layer lands in an empty viewer, but this canvas moves between panels of different sizes; and the camera is fitted to the viewbox that the grid and ndisplay are what change.

What was decided: Scope the canvas host's black background to itself by object name instead of setting a bare background rule.
Why it was decided: An unscoped rule is inherited by everything mounted inside the host, including the z slider napari packs under its canvas, which would render black on black.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Track where the canvas belongs as a separate boolean (holds_canvas) from the widget actually mounted.
Why it was decided: RecordingViewer has no widget to hand over, so this is what keeps every placement and arrangement decision assertable in a headless suite while leaving 'did an image appear' to a person in front of a screen.

What was decided: Reduce the stored two-pane thumbnail to its cell pane when a triage tile is constructed, not inside paintEvent.
Why it was decided: pipeline._thumbnail stores [cell, nucleus] as one array and the tile unpacked it as 2D, raising inside a paint handler where Qt turns a traceback into a warning and paints an empty tile.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Give the selection list both a scrolling viewport with a maximum height and a minimum height.
Why it was decided: One row per cell and one measured field holds 537 of them: the window grew to 2470 px on a 950 px request, carrying item 6's lower panel off the display.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Cap the main window at the display's available geometry through a named fit_to_display helper.
