Why it was decided: Any child with an unbounded size hint drags the window past the screen, and the Bunya run happens in an Open OnDemand desktop inside a browser window whose usable area is unknown until the session opens and cannot be dragged back.

What was decided: Style QRadioButton explicitly from the existing three chrome colours.
Why it was decided: Nothing in the stylesheet named it, so the platform style drew the checked indicator invisibly on the dark ground: rich review showed two empty circles and one blank space, and the rendering mode in use was the one that could not be seen.

What was decided: Write scripts/gui_shakeout.py, which opens the real application on a real display, walks every screen and photographs each one, and treat that as the verification for tasks that tests cannot cover.
Why it was decided: A test that asserts a widget was re-parented proves only that a widget was re-parented.

What was decided: When a mutation did not bite, change the code rather than strengthen the assertion.
Why it was decided: The test painted a tile and asserted no exception, but Qt catches whatever a paint handler raises, so it could not fail in either direction.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Have every parameter-owning screen write its values onto session.chosen from _sync.
Why it was decided: session.chosen is what the parameters file serialises and what the pipeline reads, and only items 9a and 9b ever wrote to it, so every commit ran at dataclass defaults and the file recorded defaults -- on screens whose entire purpose is choosing the value. _sync is the one hook every control change and every commit already calls.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Skip a box that will not parse instead of substituting a default or a zero.
Why it was decided: float('') raises and a box mid-edit is not a choice; the last real value stands, and each screen's commit gate refuses on the same values, so a skipped field can never reach a commit anyway.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Put the number parser in one module (semiauto.parsed_numbers) rather than copying it into the five screens that need it.
Why it was decided: Five copies of a parser drift five ways, which is the same reason widgets.py exists.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Have items 2, 4 and 5 emit commit_requested for the driver to service, while items 3 and 9b keep running their commits inline.
Why it was decided: Items 3 and 9b compute with pure functions from their own modules and own their commits.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Flip the commit gate when the button is pressed, before the work runs, rather than after it succeeds.
Why it was decided: The gate answers whether the parameters have moved since the last commit, which the press itself settles.

What was decided: Pass the committed plaque mask into detect_nuclei as plaque_mask rather than suppressing the DAPI channel before calling it.
Why it was decided: The pipeline applies the veto inside the detector, so doing it beforehand would be a second implementation of the veto and the two would diverge the first time either changed.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Run item 4 entirely at segmentation resolution, downsampling the displayed channels to match the labels, rather than upsampling the labels to native.
Why it was decided: The labels come back downsampled and the pipeline downsamples the cell mask to match before taking membership, so anything else makes the screen's membership fractions disagree with the ones the save step will compute -- and an upsampled label volume costs about 849 MB on a production field.

What was decided: Give the measurement mask its own Compute method rather than adding a flag to the segmentation-mask method, and reuse item 3's min_object_voxels inside it.
Why it was decided: A separate method keeps both field names visible at the call site, and the pipeline passes the same min_object_voxels into both masks, so inventing a second control here would make the screen's mask differ from the one batch rebuilds.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Force a repaint inside CommitButton.set_working, excluding user input events.
Why it was decided: The progress line existed on every commit screen and never appeared: the work is synchronous, so between setting the text and the blocking call the event loop never runs and no paint event is delivered.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Keep commit work synchronous rather than moving it to a worker thread.
Why it was decided: The rule for these screens is progress shown and no cancel, so there is nothing for a thread to enable except responsiveness; the painted progress line plus a disabled button is the honest minimum, and threading Qt widget updates is the larger risk on the run that has to work first time.

What was decided: Rewrite PipelineCompute.detect to match the pipeline's own call.
Why it was decided: It was never called from anywhere and had drifted: detect_nuclei takes diameter_px, not diameter_um, so the body was a TypeError waiting for a caller, and it returned the result object where the caller wanted its labels.

What was decided: Phase C is split into three stages — skeletonise, measure, export — with export formatting only.
Why it was decided: Measure and export run back to back, so any number computed in the writer would be invisible to the pool and unreproducible from it.

What was decided: The one wide per-cell sheet becomes seven files keyed by cell_uid (identity, review, mask, skeleton_anchored, skeleton_free, cd68, plaque).
Why it was decided: The single sheet mixed populations with different row sets — R cells have a mask but no skeleton — so half its cells were blank by construction.

What was decided: R (rejected-real) cells get no row at all in the skeleton sheets.
Why it was decided: Only C is skeletonised; a present-but-empty row would read as a measured zero rather than as not attempted.

What was decided: The per-plaque sheet is NOT split the way the cell sheet was.
Why it was decided: Its 44 columns all key on the same object with the same row set, so a split would separate nothing that differs.

What was decided: The 44-column per-image sheet is left as one file for the same reason.
Why it was decided: One row per image, no population mixing, nothing to separate.

What was decided: plaque_id is replaced by plaque_uid everywhere, and file_uid is added.
Why it was decided: Label integers are only unique within one image, so they collide the moment two images are concatenated.

What was decided: Cells and plaques both carry centroid_zyx.
Why it was decided: The cells had no location column at all, so a plaque-to-cell distance could not be re-derived from the exports.

What was decided: plaques.csv gains touching_xy, touching_z, surface_area, solidity, max_feret and equivalent_diameter.
Why it was decided: All six fall out of geometry already computed for the contact test, so they cost nothing beyond writing them.

What was decided: integrated_6e10 is dropped from the per-plaque sheet.
Why it was decided: The intensity integral over a thresholded object is a function of the threshold, not of the plaque.

What was decided: core_volume and core_fraction go, and no plaque-core measure is exported at image or per-plaque level.
Why it was decided: The dense-core split needed a DAPI channel this study does not have.

What was decided: Covered-fraction ranges become 0.3, 0.6, 1.0 µm and CONTACT_TOLERANCES_UM moves 0.5 → 0.6.
Why it was decided: 0.6 µm is one z-step; a tolerance finer than the coarsest voxel dimension tests a distinction the data cannot make.

What was decided: RECRUITMENT_DISTANCES_UM = (5, 10, 20) is a separate axis from the contact tolerances.
Why it was decided: n_somata_within@5 is a recruitment question and n_cells_within@1 a contact question; one axis cannot expand both.

What was decided: n_cells_within@d and n_somata_within@r count C+R, with no multiplicity for R.
Why it was decided: R cells occupy territory and compete for contact even though they are not measured; double-counting a clump would inflate the density.

What was decided: cell_plaque_links.csv gains contact_area, soma_distance, is_nearest_plaque and polarity_index.
Why it was decided: The link row already identifies the pair, so these are the measures the pairing exists to support.

What was decided: No plaque-shells file, and no nodes/edges files.
Why it was decided: Shells are re-derivable from the long curve files, and a node/edge dump is the SWC artefact in a worse format.

What was decided: Border counts, territory and the lost-real count on images.csv are all C+R.
Why it was decided: A border or a territory is a physical fact about the cell, independent of whether it passed morphometric review.

What was decided: Iba1 volume ignores multiplicity, and image_iba1_integrated is added.
Why it was decided: The volume is a property of the mask, not of how many cells were resolved inside it.

What was decided: morphometric_status is replaced by a plain skeletonised / not-measured status.
Why it was decided: Its only real job was separating C from R, which a skeletonisation flag says directly instead of encoding it in a review verdict.

What was decided: n_cells_measured is not reinstated.
Why it was decided: It is n_confirmed under another name once the skeletonised flag exists.

What was decided: Sholl, the CD68 curve and branch lengths are written long; the segment file is segments_free.csv.
Why it was decided: Wide forms made the header width follow the busiest cell in the run, so the schema depended on the data.

What was decided: No export file's width follows its data — every count in §5.1 is a number, not a rule.
Why it was decided: VARIABLE_WIDTH in the spec parser could be deleted outright, which was the largest simplification the reshape bought.

What was decided: The two skeleton artefacts get prefixed column names where they measure the same thing on different skeletons.
Why it was decided: Unprefixed n_branch_points from an anchored tree and a free graph are different numbers with the same name.

What was decided: The radius of the first segment leaving the soma is measured, via edge_radius_um / edge_radius_max_um.
Why it was decided: It is the process-calibre measure 3DMorph reported, and the distance transform needed for it is already built.

What was decided: SWC is written as a rooted tree with a sidecar file for loop-closing edges.
Why it was decided: SWC cannot represent a cycle, and the soma-free graph legitimately has them; dropping them silently would lose real connectivity.

What was decided: docs/MEASURE_LEDGER.html is renamed docs/EXPORTS_LEDGER.html.
Why it was decided: It had stopped being a list of measures and become a record of what each file exports.

What was decided: Soma geometry for R cells is recomputed with the run's parameters; C keeps its stored soma.
Why it was decided: The stored R soma was written under different parameters, but C's was not — so recomputing C would replace a correct value with a re-derived one for no gain.

What was decided: _recover_lost_components re-skeletonises any mask component the skeletoniser dropped.
Why it was decided: _skeletonise silently returned nothing for some components, so a cell could lose a whole detached process without any column reading as missing.

What was decided: Solidity is computed against a rasterised hull rather than a hull over voxel centres.
Why it was decided: The mismatched bases gave solidity 1.149 on a sphere — a ratio that cannot exceed 1 by definition.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The link table is made exact, with a per-plaque padded window from find_objects instead of one global pass.
Why it was decided: The first cost estimate was wrong by three orders of magnitude; measuring it gave 2391 ms/cell, and the windowed form 51 ms/cell — 17 minutes for the study.

What was decided: scripts/link_table_gap.py is kept as a permanent cross-check between two independently written exact implementations, exiting 1 on disagreement.
Why it was decided: The approximation's error was assumed rare, and the instrument built to check that showed it was not.

What was decided: Mask export is NOT narrowed to CONFIRMED, and border counts are NOT switched to skeleton_status.
Why it was decided: Both were written as fixes and were regressions — the first drops every ANALYSED cell, i.e. all of them; the second excludes R, which contributes hulls.

What was decided: The scale-sensitive measures, including the CD68 split, get coverage at realistic voxel sizes rather than on isotropic toy arrays.
Why it was decided: An anisotropy bug at 5.54:1 passes every test written on a cube.

What was decided: Fractal dimension, lacunarity, cluster assignment, graph centrality and SWC structure types are deferred; so are problems 4, 5 and D6.
Why it was decided: None of them blocks the first full run, and each needs a decision the data has not yet forced.

What was decided: The manifest glob accepts .tiff as well as .tif, with the */*/* depth rule untouched.
Why it was decided: The RDM holds 573 images ending .tiff and 0 ending .tif, so the shipped pattern matched nothing at all.

What was decided: The depth rule is not widened beyond */*/*.
Why it was decided: Every image measured sits at depth 3 and the 731 .vsi sidecar files at depth 5, so widening would gain nothing and reach the sidecars.

What was decided: Bit depth needs no work anywhere in the loader.
Why it was decided: The RDM whole fields and the local crops are both float32 with identical voxel size and four channels, differing only in axis order and metadata flavour, both of which io.py already reads.

What was decided: cd68_threshold and plaque_threshold must be chosen on a full-size image, recorded as an operator note rather than a build item.
Why it was decided: They are the only two parameters that do not adapt per image, and the sampled crop read its plaque channel an order of magnitude below any whole field.

What was decided: The manifest becomes its own step, written once and atomically, printing the image count.
Why it was decided: Every array task re-globbed the whole tree and rewrote manifest.json with a plain write, and nothing anywhere printed the count the --array bound needs.

What was decided: An out-of-range --index prints a message and exits 0 rather than raising.
Why it was decided: The dependent merge-and-export job waits with --dependency=afterok, so a non-zero exit from a surplus task would hold it in the queue forever.

What was decided: Failure reports are named by file_uid rather than by bare filename.
Why it was decided: Two images sharing a basename in different animal folders overwrote each other's traceback.

What was decided: segment refuses a pool whose directory name marks it semi-auto; it does not derive pool_batch_<hash> for itself.
Why it was decided: ORIGINS and pool_dir_name exist to keep the two apart and segment --pool consulted neither, while deriving the name would take a path choice away from the operator.

What was decided: Nucleus detection auto-detects the GPU via torch.cuda.is_available(), with an explicit override.
Why it was decided: CellposeDetector defaults to gpu=False and nothing anywhere passed True, so a GPU partition would be paid for and left unused on the expensive step.

What was decided: The device choice does not enter SegmentationParams.
Why it was decided: That dataclass is hashed and phase_a_hash names the pool, so a hardware difference would split one study across two pools.

What was decided: The CPU-versus-GPU reproducibility caveat is dismissed rather than mitigated.
Why it was decided: Semi-auto will itself run on a GPU, so the two routes share the arithmetic.

What was decided: The nucleus label volume is stored once per image, before it is upsampled.
Why it was decided: The pool holds only each cell's own nuclei clipped to its own mask, so batch rich review would otherwise draw neighbours eroded at every cell boundary.

What was decided: Phase C writes one fragment per image and a separate command folds them in, rather than measure running serially.
Why it was decided: store._connect documents strictly single-writer access with no WAL and no busy_timeout, so concurrent array tasks collide on the lock after doing all the expensive work.

What was decided: Measurement fragments are deleted after merging.
Why it was decided: Measure's queue is the measurements table rather than fragment existence, so deleting them costs no resume signal — unlike Phase A's, which must be kept.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Fragments are deleted only after the merge transaction commits.
Why it was decided: A merge that dies before the commit leaves every fragment on disk and re-merging is idempotent, so the reverse ordering is the one way the run can be lost.

What was decided: Measurement merging is a separate command rather than an extension of merge.
Why it was decided: The two folds happen at different points in the chain, and one command doing both would re-parse and re-insert all 573 segmentation fragments every time measurements landed.

What was decided: run_phase_c gains per-image failure isolation matching batch.run_one.
Why it was decided: An unreadable image currently takes the whole task with it instead of costing only itself.

What was decided: The pool gains a read-only open mode for measure tasks.
Why it was decided: _connect runs the table-creation script on every open, so a task that only reads cells and masks is still a potential writer.

What was decided: Measure indexes a stable list of images holding measurable cells, not the pending list.
Why it was decided: The pending list shrinks as tasks finish and Slurm staggers array starts, so a late task's index pointed at a different image and the array still exited 0.

What was decided: A status command reports what is outstanding for both phases, alongside the stable index.
Why it was decided: A stable index stops drift but says nothing about a task that died of walltime, and an array that loses tasks reports success.

What was decided: Measure's index list is pinned to a file at submit time rather than computed live.
Why it was decided: Both phases then share one shape — a prepare step prints a number and the array reads a file — instead of two that look alike and differ under pressure.

What was decided: Batch cells are reviewed through a pool-backed review --pool on an interactive desktop, between segment and measure.
Why it was decided: PoolWriter writes every cell CANDIDATE and measure takes only CONFIRMED, so unreviewed batch output blanks the per-image cell counts and stamps every row reviewed=false.

What was decided: Mask edits are in scope for batch rich review and cell splitting is out.
Why it was decided: That reduces §9.4's storage foundation to replace_cell_mask alone, leaving create_cell and delete_cell unbuilt.

What was decided: review --pool takes the parameters file.
Why it was decided: The soma centroid is computed from the run's six soma settings and the pool stores only their hash, so an edited mask would keep a centroid nothing agrees with.

What was decided: Review is resumable across sittings and re-review within a pool stays forbidden.
Why it was decided: COMPONENT_05_PLAN §5 and §10 already settle both, and 573 images at roughly 60 cells each cannot be one sitting.

What was decided: Measure and export stay separate commands, submitted as two jobs.
Why it was decided: Measure is per-image and parallel while export is one pass that needs every measurement already present.

What was decided: No path-relocation work is built for the pool.
Why it was decided: The dataset leaves scratch only after measure and export and returns to the identical absolute path, and make_file_uid hashes the path exactly as given.

What was decided: No parser special cases are added for filing-system inconsistencies.
Why it was decided: The user is fixing 691619_reimaged and the TG-named files before the run, so a code workaround would outlive the problem.

What was decided: The build runs as ten items in dependency order, with the nucleus label store before pool-backed review and review last.
Why it was decided: Review reads the stored labels, and it is the largest item of the ten.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Every screen goes inside a whole-screen scroll area rather than scrolling only the right control column.
Why it was decided: Item 7b's overflow is its LEFT column at 870 px against the right's 308, so a right-column scroll would not have fixed the worst screen.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The scroll is applied as one uniform rule to all thirteen screens, including the ones that already fit.
Why it was decided: A selective rule means the next control added to item 3 or item 6 silently reopens the hole.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The vertical scrollbar is always shown rather than appearing only when the content overflows.
Why it was decided: Wheel and pinch are reserved for zoom wherever there is a canvas, so a bar that is only sometimes present is one a reviewer cannot rely on grabbing — item 7a's existing rule.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 8's own scrollbar moves from AsNeeded to AlwaysOn.
Why it was decided: It was the only screen left on the other rule once the other twelve were wrapped.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The screen title scrolls with the content rather than being pinned above the scroll area.
Why it was decided: Pinning costs ~30 px of permanent height on every screen and adds a structural exception item 8 does not have.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Item 7a's triage grid is NOT wrapped in a second scroll area.
Why it was decided: FrameE already scrolls its tile grid with the bar always on, and nesting two vertical bars makes the wheel land on whichever one the pointer happens to be over.

What was decided: The horizontal overflow is left unfixed and the horizontal bar stays off.
Why it was decided: Every FrameC screen needs 1196 px of width so a narrow desktop can still clip the right column, but the Bunya desktop's width has never been measured and no one has reported hitting it.

What was decided: The scroll work is built as Part D after Part C and before the single full-suite run.
Why it was decided: Part B already touches ui/app.py and review_pool.py, so leaving the settled A/B/C order untouched keeps a later failure attributable.

What was decided: The thread-count helper lives in a new prestomorph/cpu.py rather than in an existing module.
Why it was decided: Parts A, B and C all import it and none of them owns it.

What was decided: The thread count reaches functions through a process-wide value the CLI sets once plus an explicit threads= keyword on each threaded function.
Why it was decided: Threading a threads= argument through every intermediate signature would put a hardware fact into the pipeline's own vocabulary.

What was decided: The thread count never reaches SegmentationParams and is never hashed.
Why it was decided: The hash names the pool, so a 4-thread and a 16-thread run of one study would land in two pools — the same argument that kept --device out.

What was decided: --threads is added to segment, measure, review and interactive.
Why it was decided: Phase C and the review route both need a count, and a global flag before the subcommand is awkward in a Slurm submit script.

What was decided: OMP_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS are set outright rather than defaulted.
Why it was decided: The resolved count is printed at startup, so overriding a user's own export is visible rather than silent.

What was decided: tests/conftest.py is created to restore the process thread count after every test.
Why it was decided: batch.main sets it, so one test passing --threads 8 would leave the remaining 2100 tests spawning pools, which is the exact failure the fallback of 1 exists to prevent.

What was decided: Derivation.payloads() computes a chunk of cells at a time instead of materialising every payload.
Why it was decided: That class's own docstring fixes the memory cost at "one array, not sixty", and a full parallel map would hold ~60 cell crops beside the channels the session is already holding.

What was decided: Pool.load_arrays gains a file_uid parameter and every threaded caller passes it.
Why it was decided: The handoff recorded the method as pure filesystem, but it runs SELECT file_uid FROM cells when given no uid and the connection is check_same_thread=True, so the first threaded run raised sqlite3.ProgrammingError.

What was decided: Both of Phase C's per-cell loops accumulate in order, not just the first.
Why it was decided: The handoff said the second loop had no ordering constraint, but it also assigns label_value = len(cell_labels_index) + 1, which is the first loop's own reason for ordering.

What was decided: The prefetch memory budget is min(20 GB, one third of detected RAM), falling back to 4 GB when the machine will not say.
Why it was decided: A third puts the 64 GB A16 desktop on the 20 GB cap the plan asked for and degrades a 16 GB machine to ~5 GB instead of thrashing.

What was decided: A prefetched CellEditor is admitted or refused on an estimate of its size taken before it is built.
Why it was decided: The rule is stop rather than evict, and building one to find it does not fit spends 1.83 s to throw the work away.

What was decided: Freeing a resolved cell's editor is expressed as retain(pending uids) rather than release(uid).
Why it was decided: ReviewStep.entered is already None when the driver's slot runs, and a cell stops being pending three ways: rich review, a grid rejection, and Accept This Screen.

What was decided: The prefetch queue follows triage's own offer order through a new TriageScreen.pending_uids().
Why it was decided: Triage ranks worst-band-first, so file order would spend the budget on the cells the reviewer reaches last.

What was decided: EditCellScreen.set_cell accepts a prebuilt editor and ReviewStep gains the single construction path that produces it.
Why it was decided: A second expression of what a CellEditor is made of is how a prefetched editor and an entered one would come to differ.

What was decided: qc.triage_signals stays in load_file_scene's serial loop.
Why it was decided: It is a handful of array reductions beside a find_soma, and the handoff named two pieces to thread.

What was decided: Freeing a resolved cell's prefetched editor is confirmed safe even for a cell rejected as real_cell.
Why it was decided: Taking that cell's material runs off ReviewStep.scene and the payload masks and never off the donor's CellEditor, which the handoff asked to be confirmed rather than assumed.

What was decided: The neighbour somata's missing soma settings are left unfixed.
Why it was decided: ReviewStep._other_cells_around passes none of the six settings while CellEditor.decompose passes all six, but it is a pre-existing defect outside this patch's scope.

What was decided: Cellpose moves to CPU on both the batch and interactive routes.
Why it was decided: A wide CPU array finishes sooner than a GPU array that spends most of its life queueing, and the interactive desktop measured no great slowdown.

What was decided: Review and semi-auto must stay free of any torch CUDA op.
Why it was decided: VirtualGL breaks only CUDA Cellpose, by intercepting the cuDNN lookup, so being CUDA-free is exactly what buys hardware rendering for item 7b.

What was decided: No CUDA compute is added to review.
Why it was decided: It would re-break VirtualGL and cost hardware rendering to save milliseconds on per-cell crops.

What was decided: The thread count is environment, never a parameter, taken from SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK.
Why it was decided: Same rule the device already follows: the hash names the pool, so a 4-thread and a 16-thread run of one study must not split across two pools.

What was decided: Only strictly per-plane operations are threaded, and only where output is bit-identical.
Why it was decided: subtract_background, threshold_channel's slice loop, the xy closing and the per-slice fill all verified identical on a fixture whose three controls do fail.

What was decided: The 3D operations are left serial.
Why it was decided: binary_fill_holes 3D and remove_small_objects differ by 4800 and 696 voxels when split, and would need halo exchange or label stitching to fix.

What was decided: Threading goes inside the shared functions rather than in a UI wrapper.
Why it was decided: Splitting threshold_channel from outside gives each slab its own volume_contrast reference and changed 60453 voxels; threading inside makes that unreachable by construction.

What was decided: The distance-transform formulation of the xy closing is rejected.
Why it was decided: At the 0.8 um radius in use it measured 1.9x slower than scipy's disk and produced a mask differing in 10.1 percent of voxels.

What was decided: Workers write into disjoint views of a pre-allocated output rather than returning slabs to concatenate.
Why it was decided: Concatenating doubles peak memory on arrays that reach 850 MB per channel.

What was decided: OMP_NUM_THREADS is set before torch imports and set_num_threads after.
Why it was decided: OpenMP reads the variable once at load, so a later set_num_threads cannot undo a pool already built from the node's full core count.

What was decided: The thread count falls back to 1 when SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK is unset.
Why it was decided: The suite runs on a Windows machine where it is always unset, and any higher fallback would have every threshold test spawning pools.

What was decided: The thread count is printed at startup and appended to run_id.
Why it was decided: Identical reasoning to the device field: an allocation paid for and not used is invisible from the output otherwise.

What was decided: PipelineResult.report is wired into batch so each image logs a per-stage breakdown.
Why it was decided: run_one printed only a total, and report already existed with no callers anywhere, leaving batch runs undiagnosable.

What was decided: segment_image holds the cell channel in a local for its three uses.
Why it was decided: ImageSource.channel deliberately does not cache, so batch re-read one 850 MB channel three times per image across the whole study.

What was decided: ImageSource is not made to cache channels.
Why it was decided: Its docstring states the caller decides what to keep in memory, and caching there would change behaviour for the UI as well.

What was decided: Derivation.payloads is parallelised outright rather than gated on a measurement.
Why it was decided: find_soma measured at about 0.4 s per call on real cells puts payloads at 14 to 24 s per image, which settles it without further data.

What was decided: No --workers flag for image-level concurrency inside one segment process.
Why it was decided: The Slurm array already provides it, test_concurrency proves the fragment design safe across processes, and a second mechanism is a path to diverge.

What was decided: Merge, merge-measurements, manifest and export are left untouched.
Why it was decided: SQLite is single-writer by design with no WAL, and concurrent globbing against Lustre was already rejected once.

What was decided: Sixteen cores per task for both segment and measure, on a 100-wide array.
Why it was decided: With Cellpose on CPU the array is no longer capped by GPU availability, so walltime per task is what binds.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: Commits stay blocking and simply get faster, with no cancel button.
Why it was decided: CPU Cellpose measured no great slowdown on the interactive desktop, so the multi-minute wait that would justify a cancel did not materialise.

What was decided: The neighbour somata computed in _other_cells_around are cached.
Why it was decided: Measured at 7.95 s per cell entry, 81 percent of the program's own cost, because roughly 20 neighbours are recomputed on every entry and again on every margin move.

What was decided: load_file_scene's per-cell loop threads both load_arrays and soma_for.
Why it was decided: load_arrays was verified to be pure filesystem touching no SQLite, and soma_for is strictly per-cell.

What was decided: The next file's scene is prefetched one file ahead in a worker with its own read-only Pool.
Why it was decided: load_file_scene measured at 106.0 s and runs synchronously on the Qt thread for roughly 700 files; the connection is check_same_thread.

What was decided: Cell editors are prefetched during triage under a 20 GB rolling cap, freed as each cell resolves.
Why it was decided: Within a file the queue is the cells still candidate and resumable is not revisitable, so a resolved cell's editor can never be needed again.

What was decided: The cell prefetch uses 8 threads, sharing one pool with the file prefetch.
Why it was decided: Measured on the A16 desktop at 2.95x on 8 threads and 2.95x on 16, so the curve is flat past 8.

What was decided: Each prefetched editor is stamped with the mask it was built from and rebuilt on mismatch.
Why it was decided: Transfers remove voxels from a neighbour by construction, so a computed list of affected neighbours could miss one and open a stale cell silently.

What was decided: Outrunning either prefetch falls back to today's blocking behaviour.
Why it was decided: It is the smallest change, and after the first file or cell the wait is normally zero anyway.

What was decided: MARGIN_RANGE stays at 20 um.
Why it was decided: The prefetch pays the 1.3 s per cell off the critical path, so narrowing what the reviewer can see would buy nothing.

What was decided: No --device flag is added to interactive and no VirtualGL refusal check is built.
Why it was decided: The user's call: setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES in the launch instructions covers it without code.

What was decided: The BUNYA.md rewrite is deferred past this patch.
Why it was decided: Its instruction not to use uq-vglrun is now wrong, but the user chose to correct it after the build rather than during.

What was decided: Phase C's per-cell measure loop computes in workers and accumulates in the original order.
Why it was decided: measure_one is pure, but label_value is assigned from len(cell_labels_index) so iteration order decides the label ids.

What was decided: Phase C uses threads rather than processes, accepting roughly 1.6x.
Why it was decided: skeletonize gives 1.99x but convex_hull_image only 1.58x, and it dominates; processes were judged too large a change for the remainder.

What was decided: The convex hull algorithm is left exactly as it is.
Why it was decided: offset_coordinates, facet reduction and coarser rasterisation each move territorial_volume_um3 and union_debris_um3, both of which are exported.

What was decided: write_cell_figures stays unwired and is not deleted.
Why it was decided: The user does not want the roughly 80000 matplotlib renders now, and wiring them into a single-process export command needs its own design.

What was decided: The acceptance gate is a before-and-after pipeline comparison run by the user, with targeted equality tests as the development gate.
Why it was decided: The end-to-end diff proves the deliverable unchanged but cannot say which change moved it, so both are needed.

What was decided: OMP_NUM_THREADS is pinned to the same value on both sides of that comparison.
Why it was decided: Torch's thread count changes floating-point reduction order, which can move a nucleus and would read as a patch failure that is not one.

What was decided: Bit 6 suppresses cd68_levels only, leaving Columns.cd68_threshold still recording what the parameters carried.
Why it was decided: Nulling both turned the export summary's threshold into UNSET, which is a different claim about the run, and test_the_summary_records_every_value_a_column_name_depends_on caught it.

What was decided: The no_cd68_channel status becomes the named constant markers.NO_CD68_CHANNEL rather than a fifth written-out literal.
Why it was decided: The per-cell status had been blank for as long as it was precisely because nothing counted the places that string had to appear.

What was decided: Two export fixtures gain cd68_channel rather than the new rule being softened to accommodate them.
Why it was decided: Both set a CD68 threshold with the channel left at its None default while measuring CD68 from channel 1 of a real four-channel TIFF, so they described a run that cannot exist.

What was decided: Triage stops ranking on agreement_score and size_outlier_score, and both fields leave CellRecord entirely.
Why it was decided: Both were nucleus-derived, and the nucleus channel drives segmentation only — it has no measurement threshold, no equivalent of item 5, and was never built to be reconstructed faithfully in 3D.

What was decided: A cell with no nucleus assigned survives as a binary rule that forces the hard band, rather than as a graded score.
Why it was decided: The absence is unambiguous whatever one thinks of nucleus quality, which a graded score built on the same channel is not.

What was decided: nucleus_in_soma is kept as the one graded nucleus signal, and measures containment rather than co-location.
Why it was decided: Checked before building: the soma is clipped to the cell mask and nuclei are deliberately not clipped to cell boundaries, so the fraction is not 1.0 by construction and therefore carries information.

What was decided: The soma category scores raw soma volume rather than soma-over-cell.
Why it was decided: Soma-over-cell is one minus process_fraction, so a single observation would have scored badly in both categories and manufactured the bad-in-both evidence the two-category split exists to detect.

What was decided: detached_fraction is a volume share of the cell rather than a count of fragments above a size floor.
Why it was decided: A fraction needs no floor, so no parameter enters params_hash for a number that never touches a measurement, and a three-voxel speck sorts at the bottom on its own.

What was decided: Detachment reserves its best bracket for cells scoring exactly zero and ranks only the rest.
Why it was decided: Most cells have no detached material, and rank-bracketing a mostly-zero signal collapses twenty brackets into two.

What was decided: detached_fraction returns undefined rather than maximal when a cell has no soma.
Why it was decided: Mirrors morphometrics.detached_skeleton_um: with nothing to call attached, every component counts as detached and the measure reports the cell's whole arbour as debris.

What was decided: Twenty brackets.
Why it was decided: Images hold 100 to 250 cells, so twenty gives 5 to 12 cells a bracket — fine enough to separate, coarse enough that a hair's difference in a heuristic carries no weight.

What was decided: A run of equal values straddling a bracket boundary takes the worse bracket entire.
Why it was decided: Two cells with identical evidence must never be separated by where a boundary happens to fall.

What was decided: No QC signal is stored in the pool; both review routes recompute the soma at review time.
Why it was decided: A stored score is a second source for a fact that goes stale the moment a reviewer edits a mask, and review --pool already demanded --params to rebuild the soma centroid.

What was decided: soma_bbox_fill is one-sided low-is-bad, and measures bounding-box fill rather than sphericity.
Why it was decided: Two-sided would need a defensible claim about what a typical fill is, and bbox fill needs no surface extraction and stays stable on objects a few voxels across.

What was decided: A centroid_fallback soma joins "no nucleus" as a rule that forces the hard band.
Why it was decided: It means erosion consumed the cell and there is no soma at all, which no clean score elsewhere should be able to outweigh.

What was decided: largest_remnant is not made a hard-band trigger despite sitting beside centroid_fallback in soma.py.
Why it was decided: Every cell taking that path has no nucleus and is already forced by the first rule, so naming it would state one fact as two rules.

What was decided: A detached process does not force the overall hard band, only the top bracket of its own category.
Why it was decided: Promoting it to a top-level trigger would swell the hard band, and the category bracket already pushes such cells a long way forward.

What was decided: Derivation.size_ratios and Derivation.median_ratio are removed outright.
Why it was decided: They existed only to compute size_outlier_score and were being maintained on every cell edit, every size cutoff and every renumbering for that one consumer.

What was decided: Pool.cells_for_review stops ordering by score and returns the file's cells in file order.
Why it was decided: A rank depends on where every other cell fell, which no per-row SQL ORDER BY can express.

What was decided: triage_key becomes triage_keys(cells), taking the whole list.
Why it was decided: A bracket is a property of the population, so a per-cell key cannot compute one.

What was decided: review_order sorts by list index rather than keying a dict on id(cell).
Why it was decided: §70 item 2 was written the same week about id() recycling, and an index needs no argument about object lifetime to be correct.

What was decided: The three band fractions stay at 15 / 35 / rest.
Why it was decided: Reaffirmed explicitly when the ordering underneath them was reworked.

What was decided: The evaluation of whether the new ordering actually works is not built in this patch.
Why it was decided: It needs review decisions to exist before it can report anything, and no pool held any at the time.

What was decided: The prestomorphspeedtest tree is put under git with a baseline commit, and the live pool.db is backed up through sqlite3's online backup API rather than cp.
Why it was decided: Phase 0 of the speedup plan required a recoverable baseline before editing a tree with a live pool beside it; cp on an open SQLite file can copy a torn page, and both copies were verified integrity_check ok with identical counts before anything was touched.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: The speedup plan's central premise — that 26 to 56 s of the 7a→7b entry is napari's six layer uploads and the 3D render — is rejected on measurement.
Why it was decided: On the real A16 through VirtualGL the render is 0.07 s and the whole click-to-finished-picture entry is 5.90 s at baseline; the SETTLED column exists to catch napari 0.7 slicing asynchronously and came back equal to TOTAL on every cell, so nothing was arriving late.

What was decided: The 30 to 60 s the user experiences is recorded as environmental and not chased in code, with scripts/timed_review.py rewritten to identify it in a real sitting.
Why it was decided: The harness reproduces the plan's own 4.15 s compute baseline exactly (4.13 to 4.15 s across runs) but does not contain the slow case, so the four candidates — a session launched without uq-vglrun falling back to llvmpipe, prefetch contention on the same 16 CPUs, load_file_scene landing on the Qt thread, and memory pressure from EDITOR_CAP_BYTES — can only be separated in a live session.

What was decided: scripts/timed_review.py gains a time-to-first-frame hooked to vispy's own draw event.
Why it was decided: It is the number no wrapper around _enter can see, and it is exactly what separates an environmental cause from a code one.

What was decided: scripts/measure_gpu_entry.py is read-only and documents a private-Xvnc recipe rather than running on the reviewer's own display.
Why it was decided: It opens a real napari viewer on the real GPU, so run on :1 it would put a window on the reviewer's desktop mid-session.

What was decided: everything_else is deleted end to end.
Why it was decided: It became other cells + debris on 2026-08-25 and its name left LAYERS the same day, so no layer could ever ask for it — yet _enter went on calling _scene_around and handing the array to set_cell on every entry.

What was decided: crop_box is taken once per draw and passed into _world_offset, and region_adjacency collapses its voxel pairs with np.unique before building edges.
Why it was decided: crop_box ran six times per draw at np.nonzero over the whole editable frame (0.093 s/cell) and the Python adjacency loop re-added each edge thousands of times (0.094 s/cell); both changes were required to produce identical output, which the existing tests already compare.

Category: Graphical user interface layout, controls and program flow
What was decided: CellEditor.displayed() returns labels and alphas from one _displayed() walk.
Why it was decided: draw asked for them separately and copied the whole editable frame twice.

What was decided: _neighbour_soma is handed the study's _soma_params instead of inheriting find_somas defaults.
Why it was decided: Diffed both ways across 14 real neighbours: the corrected soma is a strict subset of the old one every time, not one voxel gained, and between 0.1% and 65% smaller; the voxels released render as process (value 2, which _context_status offers) rather than body (value 1, which it refuses), so what is takeable becomes what the export calls a process.

What was decided: OFFERED_RENDERING collapses to ("attenuated_mip",) and the rendering radio group and RenderingChoice.LABELS are removed.
Why it was decided: One option is not a choice; set_rendering stays and still refuses anything not offered, and LABELS_RENDERING was left untouched because additive would render a red label over blue DAPI as magenta.

What was decided: Four layers are visible by default — this cell, Iba1 signal, DAPI as detected, nucleus — and the other three are neither cut nor uploaded until first switched on.
Why it was decided: Hidden layers were 34.3 MB of the 65.4 MB uploaded per cell; context_wanted is the same seam margin_changed already rests on, and _cut_context reads the live checkbox so a layer left on carries across cells and is cut on arrival.

What was decided: The conditioned DAPI volume is held at float32 rather than float64.
Why it was decided: It is only ever looked at — no measurement reads it and the detector has its own path — and float64 cost 1.70 GB held per file and 47.8 MB uploaded per cell, which began to matter the moment that layer moved from off to on.

What was decided: RecordingViewer models _raise_labels_to_top.
Why it was decided: It had only ever agreed with napari about layer order because all seven layers happened to be pushed in one pass, and deferring the hidden ones broke that coincidence.

What was decided: Phase 5 of the speedup plan — narrowing the editable frame — is not built.
Why it was decided: The plan gates it at "only if still above 5 s" and the measured average is 3.31 s, and it is the one change in the whole plan that can reach the pool: _persist_one could stamp human_edited=1 on cells the reviewer never touched, and apply_cell_edit asserts the frame contains the whole footprint.

What was decided: draw's contrast limits stay on the editable-frame crop; only the comment claiming otherwise is deleted.
Why it was decided: Making the claim true re-stretches every cell's Iba1 and DAPI mid-study, which is a bigger visual change than the green layer the user explicitly accepted and was never put to them as one; it also lands a ~6 s np.percentile stall on the first cell of each file, already the slowest, and buys 0.118 s/cell.

What was decided: Every behaviour the speedup changed was mutation-tested by reverting it, and the two the suite did not catch got tests.
Why it was decided: Green is not the same as pinned: _neighbour_soma being handed _soma_params reverted with 425 still passing, and the float32 DAPI produces an identical picture at either dtype so nothing else could have noticed.

What was decided: The two new _neighbour_soma tests rest on a deliberately shaped neighbour — a body plus a one-voxel process — and assert that guard before anything else.
Why it was decided: On a round blob opening and anchor_sheet return the same region, so the tests would pass against the very defect they exist to catch.

What was decided: The skeletonisation patch lands in /scratch/user/s4920248/prestomorphspeedtest rather than a fresh checkout.
Why it was decided: It is the only tree under git with a measured baseline, and that choice is what changes the legacy-helper item: scripts/branch_point_correction.py exists in the local merged program but not there.

What was decided: loop_prune_method goes from lowest_intensity_voxel to none in both cohort batch files.
Why it was decided: The cycles being pruned are overwhelmingly tunnels in the Iba1 mask — 13 to 175 per mask — rather than two processes touching, so cutting them invents two endpoints per loop that answer to no anatomical feature, while free_n_loops already records the topology; it also restores Fiji's default, 3DMorph's default and our own LOOP_PRUNE_DEFAULT.

What was decided: The loop-prune change was verified pool-safe before the edit, and both batch files backed up.
Why it was decided: loop_prune_method is in PHASE_C_ONLY_FIELDS, so phase_a_hash() is 96dda808 (WT) and e34610c6 (5xFAD) before and after — no cell moves pool and none of the 16,417 review decisions is touched.

What was decided: A 1.0 µm³ size floor is applied to connected components of the resampled mask before thinning, as a real SegmentationParams field.
Why it was decided: resample_isotropic sheds speckle off thin processes and each speck becomes its own component — one cell that is a single object natively exported as 74 — and the speckle is genotype-correlated (mean 33.9 µm³ WT against 0.5 µm³ 5xFAD), so it would put a roughly 25× artefact into detached_skeleton_um, the column built to test whether detached fragments explain the WT endpoint jump.

What was decided: min_skeleton_component_um3 joins PHASE_C_ONLY_FIELDS.
Why it was decided: It is a measurement-time parameter, and a Phase A field would move phase_a_hash(), which is the pool key over 16,417 review decisions.

What was decided: The floor is applied to the resampled mask before thinning rather than to components after it.
Why it was decided: No speck then reaches _recover_lost_components, and the radius field is measured on the same voxels as the skeleton.

What was decided: _drop_small_components keeps the largest component when every component falls below the floor.
Why it was decided: A floor that can empty a cell converts a measurement into a missing row.

What was decided: A loop is opened by severing one voxel and leaving each half as a leaf edge, not by deleting the edge.
Why it was decided: Deleting asserts that mask-supported material does not exist; Fiji's two intensity modes both end in exactly one setPixel(stack, point, 0) and never remove a branch's length.

What was decided: Both endpoint counts are not carried alongside each other.
Why it was decided: The gap between the two rules is exactly 2 × free_n_loops on every cell measured, and free_n_loops is already exported and counted on the shared pre-pruning graph — exact while spur pruning is off, approximate once min_spur_um is live.

What was decided: Loop splitting is applied to the soma-free branch only.
Why it was decided: Cutting the shared voxel skeleton would move the anchored tree, which the module docstring forbids: the setting must never silently move the tree as well.

What was decided: A closed ring opens into one path rather than two halves.
Why it was decided: Found by testing: its chain has no anchor at either end, so splitting it like an ordinary edge produced two degenerate stubs and lost the entire loop.

What was decided: lowest_intensity_branch severs at the lowest voxel too, recorded as a deliberate divergence from Fiji's V1-vertex cut.
Why it was decided: One rule for where a cut lands beats two, and with loop pruning off for this cohort the difference is moot in practice.

What was decided: Endpoints become degree <= 1 rather than degree == 1.
Why it was decided: A node with no edge is an isolated skeleton voxel — a degenerate tip — and went unreported at 0 to 28 per cell.

What was decided: n_endpoints_voxel is deleted rather than wired up as the earlier handoff prescribed.
Why it was decided: It is a pre-pruning count on the shared skeleton, where Fiji re-tags after pruning and reports per tree, so exporting it would label a third quantity as Fiji's.

What was decided: The segmentation is not touched over the mask tunnels; free_n_loops is carried as a covariate instead.
Why it was decided: The endpoint question they bear on is settled by analysis after the cohort run, not by moving a threshold mid-study.

What was decided: Degree-2 nodes are dissolved after all pruning, on both artefacts, with the root protected.
Why it was decided: At min_spur_um = 1.0, 19 to 28% of surviving edges terminate at a node with two edges, inflating n_segments and deflating every segment-length statistic; the "<1% of edges" figure that argued against it had been measured at min_spur_um = 0, where nothing is pruned.

What was decided: The degree-2 merge is recorded as a deliberate improvement on Fiji rather than a match.
Why it was decided: Reading AnalyzeSkeleton_-3.4.2.jar showed the re-analysis sits inside if (bPruneCycles && pruneCycles(...)), so with loop_prune_method = none Fiji never re-analyses and leaves the stranded node exactly as we used to.

What was decided: The root, any node carrying a self-edge, and any node whose two edges lead to the same neighbour are exempt from the merge.
Why it was decided: Degree 2 at the root is two primary processes rather than a pass-through, and a ring's node reads as degree 2 while its only neighbour is itself.

What was decided: The merge bridges the join gap with a straight-line hop across the dissolved node.
Why it was decided: Found by testing: two edges meeting at one junction clump anchor on different voxels of it, because _simplify starts each chain from whichever voxel its own walk reached, so concatenation left a discontinuity of up to 1.89 µm; the hop restores continuity to 4.23e-07 µm and returns that interior to a branch, which is also what Fiji's re-tagging does.

What was decided: _orient_from_root runs one breadth-first sweep after the merge.
Why it was decided: The merge emits edges in walk order, and a rooted tree needs them parent → child before parent can be read off edge[:, 1], with the stored chain starting at the parent end.

What was decided: # Junctions stays degree ≥ 3 rather than Fiji's Vertex count, and is promoted to a confirmed divergence.
Why it was decided: A node with two edges is not a fork; free_n_triple_points and free_n_quadruple_points are degree-counted in Fiji too, so matching only # Junctions would leave our own trio incoherent; the measured gap is 0 to 5 per cell, at most 1.2%; and both node_role and the edge list persist to the .npz, so Fiji's count can be recomputed after the cohort run without re-thinning.

What was decided: The identity free_n_branch_points == free_n_triple_points + free_n_quadruple_points + (degree ≥ 5) gets its own test rather than being assumed.
Why it was decided: It holds only while every non-root node of degree ≥ 3 also carries NODE_JUNCTION, and the two counts use different predicates; the edge split, the degree-0 endpoint change and the degree-2 merge all move role assignment, so the patch could break it silently.

What was decided: Fiji's triple and quadruple point rule is confirmed different but not adopted.
Why it was decided: It censuses each clump's 27-neighbourhood for SLAB/END_POINT voxels rather than counting degree, but gives identical counts on 10 of 10 cells because a branch leaves a thinned clump through exactly one slab voxel, so keeping degree for all three costs nothing in agreement.

What was decided: The full-resolution voxel chain is stored per edge, and every geometry measure reads its ends rather than node_um.
Why it was decided: Geometry comes from the path and identity from the node: a junction node's stored position is its clump's centre of mass while edge_length_um accumulates from the boundary voxel where the chain leaves that clump, so geometry between two node_um entries compares an arc against a chord the arc never touched — which put tortuosity below 1 on 30.5% of edges, minimum 0.0913, arithmetically impossible for arc ÷ chord.

What was decided: The stored paths are kept rather than dropped for size.
Why it was decided: ≈0.28 GB compressed across the study, not the 0.5 to 2 GB an earlier estimate carried, and they are the prerequisite for the manually traced accuracy subset.

What was decided: _ring_order walks a closed ring in connectivity order rather than trusting np.flatnonzero.
Why it was decided: Raster order on a loop is meaningless.

What was decided: edge_tortuosity clamps at 1.0.
Why it was decided: The residual after the chain fix is 5.2e-08, under float32 eps of 1.19e-07 — float bookkeeping, and documented as such rather than as a measurement.

What was decided: Sholl counts crossings along each edge's own chain.
Why it was decided: The node test can only ever report 0 or 1 crossings, while a process that curves back across a shell crosses it three times and an edge with both ends inside a shell can still bulge past it, so the node test errs in both directions.

What was decided: The geodesic Sholl profile deliberately does not get the along-path fix.
Why it was decided: Geodesic radius is strictly monotone along every edge of a root-anchored shortest-path tree, so the node test is the exact answer there, and the geodesic scalars and rows must not move.

What was decided: polarity_index splits each chain and attributes every step to the side it is actually on.
Why it was decided: It put a whole edge on whichever side its midpoint fell.

What was decided: n_slab_voxels is counted from each artefact's own stored chains.
Why it was decided: _artefact took it straight from the shared skeleton, so both sheets reported the same figure and the anchored one silently included detached material it excludes from everything else.

What was decided: anchored_n_loops is dropped from the export.
Why it was decided: It carried the shared skeleton's cycle count, so it never described the tree it sat on, and a rooted tree is acyclic by construction.

What was decided: longest_shortest_path_um and max_segment_um are added.
Why it was decided: Fiji's Longest Shortest Path and Maximum Branch Length had no counterpart here — max_branch_um is the anchored tip-to-soma path, a different quantity.

What was decided: resample_volume_ratio is computed before the component floor is applied.
Why it was decided: It exists to measure what the resample cost, not what the floor removed.

What was decided: The 6 to 8% resample volume loss is characterised and nothing is changed.
Why it was decided: resample_volume_ratio is carried as a per-cell covariate with a warning, and mean_radius_um is flagged as biased; the isotropic resample itself is not up for revision, measured at 5.7% orientation spread against voxel space's 65.6%.

What was decided: Per-edge intensity is sampled unconditionally, never gated on loop_prune_method.
Why it was decided: Both pools run none, so gating it would blank the new columns for every cell in the study.

What was decided: The intensity neighbourhood is Fiji's rule ported exactly — offset max(1, round(max(pixel sizes) / pixel size)) per axis, a plain unweighted mean.
Why it was decided: It is anisotropy-aware by construction and adds no parameter; at this calibration it is a 3 × 13 × 13 box, near-cubic in physical space, and it is applied once with uniform_filter rather than per sampled voxel.

What was decided: mean_intensity and min_intensity are carried per segment on segments_free.csv, specced as segmentation diagnostics and never as morphometrics, with image_iba1_integrated named as the denominator.
Why it was decided: They are not comparable between images without that denominator, so specifying them as morphometrics would invite exactly the between-image comparison the numbers cannot support.

What was decided: Fiji's *inner third* intensity column is not carried.
Why it was decided: Two columns per segment already answer what the diagnostic is for.

What was decided: measure_cell's fallback is made to pass intensity.
Why it was decided: It built skeletons with no intensity at all and silently recorded loop_prune_needs_intensity, so tuning scripts and production were not measuring the same skeleton.

What was decided: Thinning that returns nothing retries the resample target down a five-value cascade instead of transposing the array.
Why it was decided: On 17 capsule radii the cascade rescued 2 that were empty at 0.20 µm and left 0 empty after all five targets; an explicit target_um from a caller is honoured exactly and never cascaded, and the recovery path is reported as resample_cascade, distinct from transposed.

What was decided: Five legacy helpers in morphometrics.py are deleted outright rather than moved to scripts/branch_point_correction.py.
Why it was decided: That script does not exist in the tree the patch landed in, and prune_spurs defined a spur differently from skeleton._prune_leaf_edges under the same name and units — a voxel-space Dijkstra rule against a rule on the simplified graph.

What was decided: The two spur tests are rewritten rather than repointed at the surviving rule.
Why it was decided: They asserted the deleted rule's answers about which voxels survived, where the surviving rule removes an edge.

What was decided: _prune_leaf_edges decrements degree as it removes.
Why it was decided: It converges either way, so which edges went in which pass depended on index order — a determinism defect, not a convergence one.

What was decided: SKELETON_ALGO_VERSION is mixed into SegmentationParams.hash(), never into phase_a_hash(), and it is built first.
Why it was decided: hash() digests parameter values only and also names skeletons/<params_hash>/, so after the artefact changed shape a cached .npz from an older build would reload under a parameter set that still matches and every downstream measure would read arrays that are missing or mean something else — a failure with no exception.

What was decided: min_spur_um is not re-derived and stays at 0.1.
Why it was decided: The user's decision; 0.1 is below the ≈0.197 µm per-cell floor, so spur pruning is provably a no-op on both pools and the columns it would move stay inert on the first run.

What was decided: The min_spur_um entry in the divergence list is deleted rather than kept.
Why it was decided: Fiji has both prune-ends modes — the GUI checkbox strips every end branch while run(int, double, …) applies a calibrated length threshold at length <= t — and min_spur_um reproduces the calibrated one, so it was never a divergence.

What was decided: End pruning stays after loop pruning, where Fiji prunes ends first, and is added to the divergence list.
Why it was decided: Cutting a cycle creates two stubs; Fiji creates them after end-pruning has already run and never re-prunes, so they survive at any length while ours cleans up after itself — inert for this cohort, where only one pruning stage runs.

What was decided: The two cohort batch files are regenerated as *.schema10.json beside the untouched originals rather than edited in place.
Why it was decided: load_params refuses on three independent counts — the missing min_skeleton_component_um3, the stale params_hash, and PARAMS_SCHEMA_VERSION 9 → 10 — and leaving the originals keeps the pre-patch configuration reproducible.

What was decided: prestomorph/ui/review_pool.py, prestomorph/ui/screen_size.py and tests/test_ui_app.py are excluded from the patch delivery.
Why it was decided: They carry uncommitted prefetch and OOM work from 2026-09-15 that predates this patch and that the skeleton work never touched.

What was decided: The pre-existing test_component04 thread-count failure is carried rather than fixed.
Why it was decided: It expects aim2:cpu:16t and gets aim2:cuda:16t because the node has a GPU, and it was confirmed failing on the baseline commit before any of this work began.
